item.title: lap: chunked history and branches in other folders
item.description:
Agents cannot work in parallel on one codebase today: lap has one history, one active session, and files on disk are shared. The design discussed with the user on 2026-09-27:

- **Chunks.** The log becomes a directory of chunk files, ordered by the hash chain (a chunk's first record's `prev` is the previous chunk's last hash). A chunk is sealed at a size limit or when a branch starts from it, and never written again. Existing logs split losslessly (no record or hash changes).
- **Branches.** A branch is a lap repository in another folder (a git worktree or a plain copy) whose history shares its parent's up to a base hash. `lap branch start [name] --from <parent>`. With branches, a commit must name its target.
- **Merge = adopt.** git merges the code; `lap merge` adopts the branch's commits into the parent's history with a three-way offset mapping (base / parent / branch), per file, stopping a file at its first conflict. What is left is committed by hand. Adopted commits get the parent's ids and a `from` link.
- **Registry.** The parent records where its branches live (`.lap/branches.json`, machine-local). It is hints, never errors: merged-and-gone branches are pruned silently; unmerged-and-gone ones are shown as missing.
- **The board is not branched**: agents in branch folders write to the parent's board.
- Views show branches.

The SPEC comes first, as a draft reviewed by the user, then chunks, then branches.

item.title: SPEC draft: chunked history, branches, merge by adoption

author: claude
body:
Draft written in lap session S103 (L2983), git `8424949`: `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` (321 lines), marked as a draft; `SPEC.md` is untouched until parts are built.

Covers: why; the decisions table; terms (lineage, branch, base, head, adopt); chunks (layout, naming `<lineage>.<n>.jsonl`, sealing at 4 MB and at branch start, order by the hash chain with no manifest, index/torn tail/verify/hash lookup changes, the lossless automatic conversion); branches (start: history copy or check, clean-files check, sealing, the `branch` record, registration; `--branch` required on commit and session start where branches exist; merge by adoption with the three-way offset mapping, touching = conflict, per-file stop, `from` links, sessions carried with their meta, the `merge` record, what is left); the registry and its hint-only rules; commands; the board; views; core rules that change; out of scope; three open questions.

One correction made while writing, recorded in the draft: sealing the parent's chunk at branch start *is* needed. In a git worktree the branch folder holds the parent's chunks as git last committed them; `branch start` brings them to the parent's head. If the parent kept appending to that chunk, git would see both sides change it differently. Sealed, both sides hold the identical final version, and the parent's next records go to a new file.

item.title: lap CLI: history stored as chunks
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Chunks (layout, why sealing, what changes elsewhere). Only the `main` lineage exists in this ticket; branches come in M-11, but nothing here may assume a single lineage in the file format.

**Goal.** lap reads and writes its history as `.lap/log/main.<n>.jsonl` instead of `.lap/log.jsonl`, with no change to any record or hash.

**Build**
- Chunk files `<lineage>.<n>.jsonl`, `n` zero-padded to 6 digits, from 1. The open chunk is the highest `n` of a lineage; lower ones are sealed and never written.
- Sealing: an append that would take the open chunk past 4 MB starts chunk `n+1`; a single record over 4 MB is a chunk of its own. The limit is a constant (`LAP_CHUNK_BYTES` in `lap.h`); tests need small chunks, so honour an environment override `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES`, and say in the SPEC that it exists for tests only.
- Reading a history: a lineage's chunks in `n` order, the chain continuous across them (a chunk's first `prev` = the previous chunk's last hash). `rec_log_load` and everything that reads "the log" (heal, replay, verify, search, rr, hash lookup) go through this.
- Torn tail: only in the open chunk; readers drop it, writers truncate it under the lock (today's rules, per chunk).
- Index (`idx.h`): entries point at (chunk, offset) instead of an offset into one file — it is a cache, change its format freely and bump its magic.
- `lap verify`: walks the chain across chunks; a break inside a sealed chunk is reported as `sealed chunk <name> was modified`.
- `Repo.logpath` and `LAP_LOG_NAME` give way to the log directory; nothing may still read `log.jsonl` except the conversion (T-105).

**Traps**
- `tests/e2e/run.sh` reads and tampers with `.lap/log.jsonl` in ~20 places (`wc -c`, `tail -1`, forged collisions, torn-tail appends). Give the suite one helper for "the open chunk" and "the whole history in order" and move every such line to it; do not weaken what a test checks.
- The stat cache, the per-file scratch arena and the missing-shadow replay (T-97, T-99) must keep their memory behaviour: re-measure `lap status` on a cache-less typec clone (see T-99's comment for the method) and compare.

**Done when**
- lap never creates or reads `.lap/log.jsonl` (except T-105's conversion);
- e2e covers: sealing at the limit (with the test override), a chain across three chunks, a torn tail in the open chunk, `verify` naming a modified sealed chunk;
- unit and e2e suites pass; typec clone `status` timings are in the closing comment next to T-99's;
- `SPEC.md` holds §Chunks (moved from the draft, which keeps the rest).

item.title: Existing logs convert to chunks by themselves; git and the skills follow
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Converting an existing log. Blocked by T-104.

**Goal.** Repositories with a `.lap/log.jsonl` (this one, typec) move to chunks without anyone doing anything, and git keeps tracking the history.

**Build**
- The first **writing** command that finds `.lap/log.jsonl` and no `.lap/log/` splits it at record boundaries into `main.000001.jsonl`, … (at the chunk limit), fsyncs, then removes `log.jsonl`. Under the lock; a crash midway must leave either the old file or a complete set of chunks usable (write chunks first, remove the old file last; a leftover `log.jsonl` next to complete chunks is removed on the next writer).
- Readers read either shape and never convert.
- `.gitignore`: `!**/.lap/log.jsonl` becomes the chunk directory (`!**/.lap/log/`).
- Everything that says to stage or keep `.lap/log.jsonl`: `.claude/skills/tickets/SKILL.md` (step 7: stage the log), `.claude/skills/lap/SKILL.md`, `cli/lap-cli/README.md` (three places), the root README if it names it.

**Done when**
- e2e: a repository with only `log.jsonl` is converted by the first commit; every record's hash is unchanged (compare the chain before and after); a reader on an unconverted repository works and converts nothing;
- converted for real: this repository's and a scratch clone of typec's log (not the user's typec folder), with `lap verify --deep` passing after;
- no skill or README tells anyone to stage `log.jsonl`.

item.title: Lap History reads chunked history
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Chunks. Blocked by T-104. Must land with T-104/T-105, or the view goes blank on a converted repository.

**Goal.** Lap History keeps working after the log becomes `.lap/log/`.

`packages/lap-vscode` does not ask the lap CLI for history: it parses the log file itself (`src/model.ts`, `src/extension.ts` around the `logPath`), watches it (`**/.lap/log.jsonl`), and activates on `workspaceContains:.lap/log.jsonl` (also merged into the combined extension's manifest by `packages/combined/scripts/build.mjs`).

**Build**
- Read the `main` lineage's chunks in `n` order as one history (same parser, fed chunk by chunk); fall back to `log.jsonl` for an unconverted repository.
- Watch `.lap/log/**` (a new chunk appearing must refresh too).
- Activation: `workspaceContains:.lap/log` plus the old event, so both shapes activate.
- Keep incremental refresh cheap: only the open chunk grows; sealed chunks never change.

**Done when**
- unit tests: a history split over several chunks parses to the same commits and sessions as the single file; an unconverted repository still parses;
- the view renders on a converted scratch clone of typec (light and dark theme);
- `npm run package` passes its check.

item.title: lap branch start: a folder becomes a branch of another
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Terms, §Chunks, §Branches → Starting one. Blocked by M-10 (T-104, T-105).

**Goal.** In a folder made by `git worktree add` or by copying the parent folder, `lap branch start [name] --from <parent folder>` makes it a branch: its history is the parent's up to a base hash, then its own.

**Build**
- Lineage-aware history: a folder's history = its parent's history up to the base (recursively, down to `main`), then its own lineage's chunks. The `branch` record (`{"type":"branch","id","name","parent","base","user","ts","prev"=base}`) is the first record of the lineage's first chunk and is how lap knows a folder's lineage, parent and base.
- The command, in order (SPEC steps 1–5): copy the parent's chunks (no `.lap/`) or check this folder's head is in the parent's history (copied folder) → `unrelated_history`; check every tracked file equals this folder's committed state → `not_clean` listing files; under the **parent's** lock, seal the parent's open chunk (create its empty `n+1`) and copy the sealed version here; write the branch record; add the registry entry (T-108 builds the registry; this ticket can write the entry through the function T-108 provides, or land a minimal writer T-108 then owns).
- Branch id: first 12 hex of SHA-256(base ‖ name ‖ time ‖ random nonce); `name` optional, defaults to the id. Names must be unique among the parent's branches.
- Ids continue the parent's `L`/`S` counters from the base.
- Refuse when the parent cannot be written (read-only), without leaving anything half-made in either folder.
- A branch of a branch: same command, `--from` a branch folder.

**Traps**
- Sealing is not optional: in a git worktree the branch folder's chunks are as git last committed them; without sealing, the parent keeps appending to a chunk the branch also changed, and `git merge` conflicts on it (SPEC §Why a branch start seals…).
- `lap` never writes tracked files (core rule 4): copying chunks writes only under `.lap/`.

**Done when**
- e2e, with real `git worktree add` and with a plain `cp -R`: start a branch, commit in both folders, `git merge` the worktree's git branch into the parent — **no git conflict in `.lap/log/`**; a branch of a branch; `unrelated_history`, `not_clean` and a read-only parent refused cleanly;
- `lap verify` passes in both folders; the parent's history is unchanged apart from the sealing;
- `SPEC.md` holds §Branches → Starting one and the core-rule changes it needs.

item.title: The branch registry: where branches live, as hints
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Registry and §Commands. Works with T-107 (which adds entries).

**Goal.** The parent knows where its branch folders are, for `lap merge` and the views — and never fails because of it.

**Build**
- `.lap/branches.json`: `[{id, name, path (absolute), base, started}]`, machine-local, not committed, written atomically under the lock.
- Checked, never trusted: an entry counts only if its folder exists and that folder's `.lap` is that branch (by the `branch` record's id).
- Pruning, by writers only: an entry whose branch was merged up to its head (T-112's merge record says so) and whose folder is gone is dropped silently. Unmerged or stopped-at-a-conflict and gone: kept, reported as `missing`.
- `lap branch list [--json]`: each branch's state (`active`, `merged`, `partly merged`, `missing`), commits since base and since the last merge, last known path. In a branch folder, also its own name, parent and base.
- `lap branch forget <branch>`, `lap branch move <branch> <path>` (the new path must hold that branch).
- No command fails because of the registry; the one error is `lap merge` finding the branch nowhere (T-112).

**Done when**
- e2e: a deleted unmerged branch shows as `missing` and `forget` removes it; `move` repoints a moved folder; a folder reused for something else is not taken for the branch; a deleted **merged** branch disappears on the next writing command without a message (with a stand-in merge record until T-112 lands, then with a real merge);
- `branch list --json` shape documented in `SPEC.md` (§Registry, §Commands moved from the draft).

item.title: Commits say which branch they go to, where branches exist
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Committing: say where. Blocked by T-107.

**Goal.** An agent cannot record work in the wrong folder by mistake.

**Build**
- In a folder that is a branch, or that has registered branches, `lap commit` and `lap session start` require `--branch <name>` (`--branch main` for the first lineage): missing → `branch_required`; naming another lineage than this folder's → `wrong_branch`. Both errors name this folder's branch, so the fix is in the message.
- A folder with no branches at all: commands unchanged (no flag needed, `--branch main` accepted).
- `--dry-run` applies the same check.
- The lap skill and the tickets skill say when and how to pass `--branch`.

**Done when**
- e2e: required in a branch folder and in a parent with branches; refused with the right name; unchanged in a plain repository;
- skills updated; `SPEC.md` holds the rule.

item.title: coboard: agents in a branch folder work the parent's board
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §The board. Independent of the lap CLI work.

**Goal.** One board for everyone: an agent in a git worktree or a copied folder moves tickets and comments on the parent folder's board, not on a copy that git would later have to merge.

**Build**
- coboard finds its board by walking up to `.coboard/` (see `packages/coboard/src/store.ts`, `findBoard`). Add an override that points it at another folder's board: an environment variable for the MCP server (e.g. `COBOARD_DIR`) and a setting for the Board view, passed through by the combined extension like `LAP_BIN`.
- Writes keep coboard's existing lock, so several agents in several folders writing one board stay safe.
- When a folder is a lap branch and no override is set, say so where it helps (e.g. the Board view notes that this folder's board is a copy), rather than guessing the parent.
- Docs: the README's Coboard section, and the tickets skill (agents in a branch folder set the override).

**Done when**
- tests: with the override, reads and writes go to the other folder's board; two processes writing through it concurrently lose nothing;
- the combined extension passes the setting to the coboard MCP server; `npm run package` passes its check.

item.title: Adoption: place a branch's commits on the parent's version of a file
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Merging (the per-file walk, offsets, conflict). Can start before M-11 is done: it is pure logic.

**Goal.** The algorithm at the heart of `lap merge`, as a pure module with unit tests, before any command uses it.

**Input:** the file at the branch's base (lines), the parent's current version (lines), and the branch's commits to that file in order (each a region: `old_start`, `old_lines`, `old_text`, `new_text`, in the branch's coordinates at that point). **Output:** for each commit, either its region translated to the parent's coordinates (and the parent's text after it), or a conflict — after which the rest of that file's commits are not placed.

**Rules**
- The parent's changes are the diff base → parent (lap's own `diff.c`).
- A branch commit whose region neither overlaps nor touches a parent change moves by the net lines the parent added or removed above it; each placed commit shifts the ones after it.
- Overlap is a conflict. **Touching** is a conflict too: both sides insert at the same point, or one inserts right at the edge of the other's change — either order would be a guess.
- A placed commit's `old_text` must equal the parent's text at the translated position; if it does not, that is a conflict (defensive: it means the mapping is wrong).

**Done when**
- unit tests (in `tests/unit/`): the user's example (parent adds an import at line 4, branch inserts a function at 51 → placed at 52); parent change below the branch's (no shift); deletions on the parent above; several branch commits shifting each other; overlap; both inserting at one point; touching at an edge; a pure insertion at the very top and bottom of a file; CRLF-free comparison as in `file_diff_load`;
- the module has no I/O and does not allocate beyond its arena.

item.title: lap merge: adopt a branch into the parent's history
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Merging, §Registry. Blocked by T-107, T-108, T-111.

**Goal.** After `git merge` brought a branch's code into the parent folder, `lap merge <branch> [--dry-run]` brings its history: every commit that can be placed, per file, with what is left shown by `lap status`.

**Build**
- Find the branch's chunks in this folder (a `git merge` brought them) or in its registered folder; else `branch_not_found`. Its base must be in this folder's history, else `unrelated_history`. A branch of a branch whose parent was adopted: resolve its base through the adopted commits' `from` links; if its parent's adoption stopped before that base, refuse and say so.
- Per file, run T-111's placement on: the base version (this history replayed to the base), the parent's shadow, and the branch's commits to that file after the last merge's `head`. Files stopped by an earlier merge of this branch stay stopped.
- Append, under the lock, in the branch's order: each placed commit as an ordinary commit with the next `L` id, translated coordinates, and `"from":"<branch commit hash>"`; each branch session as a new session (new `S` id, same purpose and **meta**, `from`), so `lap session list --meta ticket=T-12` still finds the work. Update shadows as commits do. Never write the working tree.
- Close with the merge record: `{"type":"merge","branch","name","head","adopted","left","stopped":[{"file","at"}],"user","ts","prev"}`.
- Report: adopted N of M; each stopped file and the first commit not adopted; then `lap status` shows the rest to commit by hand.
- `--dry-run`: the report, nothing written.
- Refuse with `branch_required`-style clarity when run in a branch folder against itself, or when the branch is this folder's own parent.

**Done when**
- e2e with real git worktrees: (1) disjoint files → everything adopted, `lap status` clean after; (2) the user's example (import on the parent, function on the branch, same file) → adopted with the shifted line, clean after; (3) a real conflict → that file stops at the right commit, other files adopted, `lap status` shows the resolution to commit, which is committed citing the branch hashes; (4) a second merge after more branch work adopts only the new commits and keeps the stopped file stopped; (5) `--dry-run` writes nothing;
- `lap verify --deep` passes in the parent after each; `lap show` on an adopted commit shows its `from` link;
- `SPEC.md` holds §Merging; `SPEC-branches.md` is down to what the views still need.

item.title: Reading another branch's history: --branch on log, show and rr
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Commands (the `--branch` reading bullet). Blocked by T-107, T-108.

**Goal.** From the parent folder, review a branch's work before or after merging it.

**Build**
- `lap log`, `lap show`, `lap rr` take `--branch <name>` to read another lineage present in this folder (a merged-in branch's chunks) or in a registered branch folder. Without the flag, they read this folder's own lineage, as now.
- `lap show <hash>` finds a commit in any lineage present, so an adopted commit's `from` link can be followed; the output says which branch it belongs to.
- `--json` outputs carry the lineage (`branch`) of each commit.

**Done when**
- e2e: log/show/rr of a branch from its parent, before and after `git merge` brought its chunks; following a `from` link with `show`;
- `SPEC.md` documents the flag and the JSON field.

item.title: Lap History: branches, and adopted commits linking to their originals
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Views. Blocked by T-106, T-108, T-113.

**Goal.** Watch agents' branches from the parent folder while they work, and see after a merge where each adopted commit came from.

**Build**
- A Branches group in Lap History from `lap branch list --json`: name, state (`active`, `merged`, `partly merged`, `missing`), commits since base / since last merge. Expanding an active or merged branch shows its sessions and commits (read with `--branch`), in the same layout as main's.
- A `missing` branch shows its last path and the two ways to fix it (`lap branch move`, `lap branch forget`), as commands the user can run.
- Adopted commits on main show a link to their original (`from`), which reveals the branch commit; a stopped file after a merge is listed with the first commit not adopted.
- Live refresh when a registered branch folder's open chunk grows (watch registered paths, cheaply).

**Done when**
- unit tests for the branch model built from `branch list --json` and for `from` links;
- rendered in light and dark themes with: an active branch, a merged one, a partly merged one, a missing one.

item.title: Board review: a ticket's work across branches
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Views, §Merging (sessions carry their meta). Blocked by T-112, T-113.

**Goal.** A ticket worked in a branch folder shows its sessions on the board, both while the branch is in progress and after it was adopted.

**Build**
- A ticket's sessions come from `lap session list --meta ticket=T-n`. Include sessions of registered branches still in progress (`--branch`), marked with their branch; after adoption, the adopted sessions appear on main with the same meta — show them once (the adopted one, linking to its original), not twice.
- The review tab of an adopted session shows each commit's `from` link, and a stopped file with the first commit not adopted.

**Done when**
- tests: a ticket's sessions before merge (in a branch), after merge (adopted, no duplicate), and partly merged;
- review tab rendered in light and dark themes for an adopted session.

item.title: SPEC draft amendments from the design review
item.description:
The review of `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` (2026-09-27, before building) found gaps. Fold them into the draft before M-10/M-11 build on it:

1. **Base and clean files.** The base is the parent's head at `branch start`; a folder whose files are not the parent head's state is `not_clean`, and the error says why (git HEAD behind lap's head; files lap tracks that git ignores). Recommend the layout where agents work in branches and the first folder only merges.
2. **Merge keeps the originals.** `lap merge` copies the branch's chunks (up to what it adopted) into the parent's `.lap/log/` when they are not there, so `from` links and `#hash` references survive the branch folder's removal.
3. **Ids across folders.** Ids in two folders can repeat; board comments cite hashes or `<branch>/S<n>`.
4. **Sessions on adoption.** An adopted session never becomes the parent's active session; a later merge adds to the session already adopted (by `from`); `session_end` is carried when the branch ended it; adopted messages are copied as they are, not re-checked.
5. **An empty open chunk is not sealed again.** Base is then the last record of the chunk before.
6. **The branch record names its base chunk** (`base_chunk`), and a folder's lineage is kept in machine-local `.lap/lineage`.
7. **`LAP_BRANCH`** environment variable is accepted where `--branch` is.
8. **No branch of a branch in this version.**
9. The diff effort cap makes a heavily rewritten parent file one change: its branch commits conflict.

**Done when:** the draft says all of the above; the affected tickets (T-107, T-109, T-112) are updated to match.

author: claude
body:
Amended by T-118 (the spec draft is the reference):
- **No branch of a branch**: `--from` a folder whose lineage is not `main` is refused with `nested_branch`. Drop the "A branch of a branch" bullet.
- The base is always the parent's head; a copied/worktree folder with `.lap/` is brought up to it (its head must be in the parent's history).
- `not_clean` names its two usual causes (git HEAD older than lap's head; lap-tracked files git ignores).
- The `branch` record carries `base_chunk`; `branch start` writes `.lap/lineage` (machine-local).
- An empty open parent chunk is not sealed again.
- The `branch` record leaves the branch with no active session.

author: claude
body: Amended by T-118: `LAP_BRANCH` in the environment counts as `--branch` when the flag is not given (the flag wins when both are present). The skills should tell orchestrators to set it per agent, and board comments cite commits by hash and sessions as `<branch>/S<n>`.

author: claude
body:
Amended by T-118:
- When the branch folder is reachable, seal the branch's open chunk (under its lock) and copy its chunks into the parent's `.lap/log/`, so `from` links survive the folder's removal and a later `git merge` meets identical files.
- No branch of a branch: drop the base-through-`from` resolution.
- Adopted sessions: `session_start`/`session_end` carried with `from`; they never change the parent's active session; a later merge appends to the already-adopted session; messages copied unchecked (`forced`, `user` kept).
- The effort cap: a parent file rewritten past the diff cap is one change, so every branch commit to it conflicts — expected, test it.

item.title: lap CLI: history stored as chunks
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Chunks (layout, why sealing, what changes elsewhere). Only the `main` lineage exists in this ticket; branches come in M-11, but nothing here may assume a single lineage in the file format.

**Goal.** lap reads and writes its history as `.lap/log/main.<n>.jsonl` instead of `.lap/log.jsonl`, with no change to any record or hash.

**Build**
- Chunk files `<lineage>.<n>.jsonl`, `n` zero-padded to 6 digits, from 1. The open chunk is the highest `n` of a lineage; lower ones are sealed and never written.
- Sealing: an append that would take the open chunk past 4 MB starts chunk `n+1`; a single record over 4 MB is a chunk of its own. The limit is a constant (`LAP_CHUNK_BYTES` in `lap.h`); tests need small chunks, so honour an environment override `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES`, and say in the SPEC that it exists for tests only.
- Reading a history: a lineage's chunks in `n` order, the chain continuous across them (a chunk's first `prev` = the previous chunk's last hash). `rec_log_load` and everything that reads "the log" (heal, replay, verify, search, rr, hash lookup) go through this.
- Torn tail: only in the open chunk; readers drop it, writers truncate it under the lock (today's rules, per chunk).
- Index (`idx.h`): entries point at (chunk, offset) instead of an offset into one file — it is a cache, change its format freely and bump its magic.
- `lap verify`: walks the chain across chunks; a break inside a sealed chunk is reported as `sealed chunk <name> was modified`.
- `Repo.logpath` and `LAP_LOG_NAME` give way to the log directory; nothing may still read `log.jsonl` except the conversion (T-105).

**Traps**
- `tests/e2e/run.sh` reads and tampers with `.lap/log.jsonl` in ~20 places (`wc -c`, `tail -1`, forged collisions, torn-tail appends). Give the suite one helper for "the open chunk" and "the whole history in order" and move every such line to it; do not weaken what a test checks.
- The stat cache, the per-file scratch arena and the missing-shadow replay (T-97, T-99) must keep their memory behaviour: re-measure `lap status` on a cache-less typec clone (see T-99's comment for the method) and compare.

**Done when**
- lap never creates or reads `.lap/log.jsonl` (except T-105's conversion);
- e2e covers: sealing at the limit (with the test override), a chain across three chunks, a torn tail in the open chunk, `verify` naming a modified sealed chunk;
- unit and e2e suites pass; typec clone `status` timings are in the closing comment next to T-99's;
- `SPEC.md` holds §Chunks (moved from the draft, which keeps the rest).

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S105 (L2998–L3101), git `aeb3548` + `81449ed`.

**What changed**
- New module `src/hist.{h,c}`: a folder's history is the chunk files of `.lap/log/` (`<lineage>.<n>.jsonl`) read as one stream. Offsets are positions in that stream; only the open chunk grows, so the index keeps plain offsets (magic bumped to `LAPIDX02`). It lists a lineage's chunks (refusing a gap, naming the missing chunk), reads ranges across chunk boundaries straight into one buffer, hashes the last complete record (past an empty or torn-only open chunk), repairs a torn tail in the open chunk, appends with sealing at the limit (a record bigger than the limit is a chunk of its own), and seals explicitly (a no-op on an empty open chunk — ready for `branch start`). Chunks of other lineages are not listed.
- `Repo` holds the `Hist` (listed after the lock for writers); `repo_log_load` replaces every `rec_log_load(path)`; `rec_log_parse` parses bytes in memory and names positions through a callback, only when a message needs one ("main.000002.jsonl line 7").
- A chain break is blamed on the chunk before the breaking record (the changed record is the one whose hash no longer matches); if that chunk is sealed, the error is `sealed chunk main.000002.jsonl was modified: …`.
- `LAP_CHUNK_BYTES` (4 MB) in `lap.h`; `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES` overrides it, noted as test-only in SPEC. `Hist.limit` lets unit tests set it directly.
- `SPEC.md` has §Chunks; the layout, the cache contract, the index, torn tail and verify say chunks. `SPEC-branches.md` keeps only what branches add.
- lap never creates or reads `.lap/log.jsonl` now: a folder with only that file gets `no history in …` until T-105's conversion.

item.title: lap CLI: history stored as chunks
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Chunks (layout, why sealing, what changes elsewhere). Only the `main` lineage exists in this ticket; branches come in M-11, but nothing here may assume a single lineage in the file format.

**Goal.** lap reads and writes its history as `.lap/log/main.<n>.jsonl` instead of `.lap/log.jsonl`, with no change to any record or hash.

**Build**
- Chunk files `<lineage>.<n>.jsonl`, `n` zero-padded to 6 digits, from 1. The open chunk is the highest `n` of a lineage; lower ones are sealed and never written.
- Sealing: an append that would take the open chunk past 4 MB starts chunk `n+1`; a single record over 4 MB is a chunk of its own. The limit is a constant (`LAP_CHUNK_BYTES` in `lap.h`); tests need small chunks, so honour an environment override `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES`, and say in the SPEC that it exists for tests only.
- Reading a history: a lineage's chunks in `n` order, the chain continuous across them (a chunk's first `prev` = the previous chunk's last hash). `rec_log_load` and everything that reads "the log" (heal, replay, verify, search, rr, hash lookup) go through this.
- Torn tail: only in the open chunk; readers drop it, writers truncate it under the lock (today's rules, per chunk).
- Index (`idx.h`): entries point at (chunk, offset) instead of an offset into one file — it is a cache, change its format freely and bump its magic.
- `lap verify`: walks the chain across chunks; a break inside a sealed chunk is reported as `sealed chunk <name> was modified`.
- `Repo.logpath` and `LAP_LOG_NAME` give way to the log directory; nothing may still read `log.jsonl` except the conversion (T-105).

**Traps**
- `tests/e2e/run.sh` reads and tampers with `.lap/log.jsonl` in ~20 places (`wc -c`, `tail -1`, forged collisions, torn-tail appends). Give the suite one helper for "the open chunk" and "the whole history in order" and move every such line to it; do not weaken what a test checks.
- The stat cache, the per-file scratch arena and the missing-shadow replay (T-97, T-99) must keep their memory behaviour: re-measure `lap status` on a cache-less typec clone (see T-99's comment for the method) and compare.

**Done when**
- lap never creates or reads `.lap/log.jsonl` (except T-105's conversion);
- e2e covers: sealing at the limit (with the test override), a chain across three chunks, a torn tail in the open chunk, `verify` naming a modified sealed chunk;
- unit and e2e suites pass; typec clone `status` timings are in the closing comment next to T-99's;
- `SPEC.md` holds §Chunks (moved from the draft, which keeps the rest).

item.title: Existing logs convert to chunks by themselves; git and the skills follow
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Converting an existing log. Blocked by T-104.

**Goal.** Repositories with a `.lap/log.jsonl` (this one, typec) move to chunks without anyone doing anything, and git keeps tracking the history.

**Build**
- The first **writing** command that finds `.lap/log.jsonl` and no `.lap/log/` splits it at record boundaries into `main.000001.jsonl`, … (at the chunk limit), fsyncs, then removes `log.jsonl`. Under the lock; a crash midway must leave either the old file or a complete set of chunks usable (write chunks first, remove the old file last; a leftover `log.jsonl` next to complete chunks is removed on the next writer).
- Readers read either shape and never convert.
- `.gitignore`: `!**/.lap/log.jsonl` becomes the chunk directory (`!**/.lap/log/`).
- Everything that says to stage or keep `.lap/log.jsonl`: `.claude/skills/tickets/SKILL.md` (step 7: stage the log), `.claude/skills/lap/SKILL.md`, `cli/lap-cli/README.md` (three places), the root README if it names it.

**Done when**
- e2e: a repository with only `log.jsonl` is converted by the first commit; every record's hash is unchanged (compare the chain before and after); a reader on an unconverted repository works and converts nothing;
- converted for real: this repository's and a scratch clone of typec's log (not the user's typec folder), with `lap verify --deep` passing after;
- no skill or README tells anyone to stage `log.jsonl`.

item.title: Convert this repository's own history to chunks
item.description:
This repository records its own work with the installed `lap` (`/usr/local/bin/lap`, the user's build), which knows only `.lap/log.jsonl`. Converting it while the epic is being built would mean recording with a development build and would break the installed `lap` and the installed Lap History extension until both are rebuilt.

So the conversion waits for the end of E-14: once the CLI and the extension that read chunks are final, run the final build's first write here (it converts by itself), check it, and tell the user to `make install` and reinstall the extension.

A scratch copy of this log (3,338 records) was already converted by T-105's build: 12 chunks, byte-identical, `verify --deep` clean.

**Done when:** `.lap/log/` holds this repository's history, `.lap/log.jsonl` is gone from git, `lap verify --deep` passes, and the user knows to install the new CLI and extension.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S106 (L3102–L3126), git `2f89b34`.

**What changed**
- `hist_convert_legacy` (hist.c), called by every writer under the lock before the history is listed: splits `.lap/log.jsonl` at record boundaries into `main.<n>.jsonl` at the limit, then removes it; a torn final line is dropped (reported as a repaired torn tail). Prints `lap: moved .lap/log.jsonl into N chunks in .lap/log/`.
- Crash safety without a staging directory: chunks are written (atomic, fsynced) before the old file is removed. Finding both: chunks that are a prefix of the old file → the split is done again; an old file that is a prefix of the chunks → removed as a leftover; anything else → refused (`both … hold history, and they differ`), both kept.
- Readers: `hist_open` reads a lone `log.jsonl` as a one-chunk legacy history and never converts it.
- `.gitignore` tracks `!**/.lap/log/`; `!**/.lap/log.jsonl` stays (with a comment) until a folder is converted — this one still records to it (T-119).
- The lap skill, the tickets skill (step 7 stages `.lap/log/`) and `cli/lap-cli/README.md` (three places; the merge limitation now talks about the chunk both sides appended to) name the directory. `SPEC.md` §Chunks holds the conversion rules; the draft no longer does.
- `plat_rename` was added and is not used yet (kept for branch start; removed at the end of the epic if it stays unused).

**Tests:** unit 3,965 (new: a lone log.jsonl read as legacy, splitting at boundaries, no-op without an old file, torn line dropped, prefix chunks redone, prefix leftover removed, differing pair refused). e2e 102 (new: readers leave a single-file log untouched and working; the first commit converts it byte for byte (hashes unchanged); `rebuild` converts a larger one at a 600-byte test limit; a leftover old file is removed; a differing one is refused).

**Converted for real**
- typec scratch clone (not the user's folder): 14,616 records → 9 chunks in 8.2 s (inside `lap rebuild`), the chunks' bytes identical to the old file, `verify --deep` 14,547 files, 0 mismatches.
- A scratch copy of this repository's log: 3,338 records → 12 chunks, byte-identical, `verify --deep` 546 files, 0 mismatches.
- **This repository itself is not converted yet** — deliberately: it records with the installed `lap`, which cannot read chunks. T-119 converts it at the end of E-14 with the final build.

item.title: Lap History reads chunked history
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Chunks. Blocked by T-104. Must land with T-104/T-105, or the view goes blank on a converted repository.

**Goal.** Lap History keeps working after the log becomes `.lap/log/`.

`packages/lap-vscode` does not ask the lap CLI for history: it parses the log file itself (`src/model.ts`, `src/extension.ts` around the `logPath`), watches it (`**/.lap/log.jsonl`), and activates on `workspaceContains:.lap/log.jsonl` (also merged into the combined extension's manifest by `packages/combined/scripts/build.mjs`).

**Build**
- Read the `main` lineage's chunks in `n` order as one history (same parser, fed chunk by chunk); fall back to `log.jsonl` for an unconverted repository.
- Watch `.lap/log/**` (a new chunk appearing must refresh too).
- Activation: `workspaceContains:.lap/log` plus the old event, so both shapes activate.
- Keep incremental refresh cheap: only the open chunk grows; sealed chunks never change.

**Done when**
- unit tests: a history split over several chunks parses to the same commits and sessions as the single file; an unconverted repository still parses;
- the view renders on a converted scratch clone of typec (light and dark theme);
- `npm run package` passes its check.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S107 (L3127–L3143), git `5ae35f3`.

**What changed**
- New `src/chunks.ts`: parses chunk names, orders a lineage's chunks (stopping at a gap, other lineages left out), lists the history's files with their sizes — the `main` chunks, or `.lap/log.jsonl` when there is none — and reads a byte range across them (`readStream`).
- `LapLogSource` keeps its incremental offset into the files read as one stream: each refresh lists the files, sums their sizes, and reads only the new bytes (in practice the open chunk's tail, or a new chunk); `consumableBytes` still stops at the last newline, so torn tails and the CLI's repair behave as before. A shrink resets and reparses, as before.
- Repository detection accepts either shape; the watcher is `**/.lap/{log.jsonl,log/*.jsonl}` so a new chunk refreshes; activation adds `workspaceContains:.lap/log/main.000001.jsonl` (the combined manifest merges it: checked in `dist/package.json`).
- README and model header say where the log lives.

**Tests:** lap-vscode 43 pass. New `chunks.test.ts` (6): names, lineage ordering and gaps, a history split over 4 chunks (one empty) parses to the same log as the single file, reads across boundaries at odd offsets, an incremental reader following growth into a new chunk with a torn line, the single-file fallback and chunks winning over it. The host test now drives the real extension over chunks and grows the log by writing a *second* chunk before the watcher fires.

**Combined:** `npm run build --workspace combined` + `check.mjs`: 34 commands, 3 MCP servers, no errors (the pdfjs `require.resolve` warning is old and unrelated).

**Render:** the real host (fake `vscode` module, as in the host test) over the converted typec scratch clone (9 chunks, 14,616 records), its page loaded into the real `lap-history.js` bundle with baukasten CSS, headless Chrome (`HOME` in the scratchpad, mock keychain): light and dark both show S1–S8 and "no session 14,552 commits", footer "1–9 of 9 sessions". Theme colours were set by hand to VS Code's default light/dark values — not a real VS Code window.

item.title: lap branch start: a folder becomes a branch of another
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Terms, §Chunks, §Branches → Starting one. Blocked by M-10 (T-104, T-105).

**Goal.** In a folder made by `git worktree add` or by copying the parent folder, `lap branch start [name] --from <parent folder>` makes it a branch: its history is the parent's up to a base hash, then its own.

**Build**
- Lineage-aware history: a folder's history = its parent's history up to the base (recursively, down to `main`), then its own lineage's chunks. The `branch` record (`{"type":"branch","id","name","parent","base","user","ts","prev"=base}`) is the first record of the lineage's first chunk and is how lap knows a folder's lineage, parent and base.
- The command, in order (SPEC steps 1–5): copy the parent's chunks (no `.lap/`) or check this folder's head is in the parent's history (copied folder) → `unrelated_history`; check every tracked file equals this folder's committed state → `not_clean` listing files; under the **parent's** lock, seal the parent's open chunk (create its empty `n+1`) and copy the sealed version here; write the branch record; add the registry entry (T-108 builds the registry; this ticket can write the entry through the function T-108 provides, or land a minimal writer T-108 then owns).
- Branch id: first 12 hex of SHA-256(base ‖ name ‖ time ‖ random nonce); `name` optional, defaults to the id. Names must be unique among the parent's branches.
- Ids continue the parent's `L`/`S` counters from the base.
- Refuse when the parent cannot be written (read-only), without leaving anything half-made in either folder.
- A branch of a branch: same command, `--from` a branch folder.

**Traps**
- Sealing is not optional: in a git worktree the branch folder's chunks are as git last committed them; without sealing, the parent keeps appending to a chunk the branch also changed, and `git merge` conflicts on it (SPEC §Why a branch start seals…).
- `lap` never writes tracked files (core rule 4): copying chunks writes only under `.lap/`.

**Done when**
- e2e, with real `git worktree add` and with a plain `cp -R`: start a branch, commit in both folders, `git merge` the worktree's git branch into the parent — **no git conflict in `.lap/log/`**; a branch of a branch; `unrelated_history`, `not_clean` and a read-only parent refused cleanly;
- `lap verify` passes in both folders; the parent's history is unchanged apart from the sealing;
- `SPEC.md` holds §Branches → Starting one and the core-rule changes it needs.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S108 (L3144–L3192), git `87ea92f` + `8d599ec`.

**What changed**
- **Branch record** (`REC_BRANCH`): `{"type":"branch","id","name","parent","base","base_chunk","user","ts","prev"=base}`, indexed (`IDX_BRANCH`); the state heal and the index clear the open session at it, so a branch starts with none.
- **Branch-aware history** (`hist_open_folder`): `.lap/lineage` (machine-local) names the folder's lineage, default `main`; a branch folder's history is the parent's chunks `1..base_chunk`, then its own, and appends go only to its own chunk. `repo_open` uses it; `repo_open_at` opens a repository at a given root (how a branch reaches its parent); `repo_abspath` resolves `--from`.
- **Registry** (`branches.{h,c}`): `.lap/branches.json` as hints — a missing or malformed file reads as empty, incomplete entries are skipped. T-108 adds list/forget/move and the pruning rules.
- **`lap branch start [name] --from <folder>`** (`cmd_branch.c`), holding the parent's lock throughout: name and folder checks; refuses `already_branch`, `same_folder`, `no_parent`, `nested_branch`; this folder's history (chunks or single-file log) must be a byte prefix of the parent's (`unrelated_history`); every file must equal the parent's committed state, compared as status does (`not_clean`, listing up to 20 files and naming both usual causes); `name_taken`; then seals the parent's open chunk (no-op when it is empty), registers the branch in the parent **before** writing anything here (`parent_read_only`), copies the parent's chunks up to the base, drops a copied registry, writes the branch record and `.lap/lineage`, and builds caches.
- **Found on the way:** in a git worktree `.git` is a *file*, which lap reported as a new file (and which made every worktree `not_clean`). `.git` is now ignored as a file or a directory (ignore.c, SPEC's .lapignore section, a unit test).
- `SPEC.md`: core rules 4 and 6, the layout (`lineage`, `branches.json`), per-folder linear history, the branch record, a new §Branches (lineages, ids from the base, no session, no nesting, Starting one in five steps, names and ids, the recommended layout, §Registry as hints), and the command with its errors. The draft points there.

**Tests:** unit 4,015 (new: branch record round trip and refusal; lineage file default/validation/write; a branch history read as parent chunks then its own; appends staying in the branch's chunk; missing base chunk and missing branch record refused; the registry: missing, round trip, lookup, malformed and partial). e2e 109, new scenarios (git present): a real `git worktree add` start (record first, `base_chunk`, parent chunk sealed and unchanged byte for byte, registry entry, no session, verify --deep); ids going on from the base in both folders; **`git merge` of the worktree branch into the parent with no conflict in `.lap/log/`**, the parent's chain still whole and the merged edit pending in its status; a second branch sharing the base with no new seal; a plain `cp -R` of the parent (caches and all) becoming a branch; every refusal, with nothing left behind; a read-only parent (skipped when run as root).

**Not done here, by design:** a branch of a branch (refused, per T-118). Found while testing: two repositories initialised in the same second have byte-identical `init` records, so a folder holding only that record passes the prefix check. That is literally a shared history, so it is left as is; the e2e test gives the unrelated folder a record of its own.

item.title: Commits say which branch they go to, where branches exist
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Committing: say where. Blocked by T-107.

**Goal.** An agent cannot record work in the wrong folder by mistake.

**Build**
- In a folder that is a branch, or that has registered branches, `lap commit` and `lap session start` require `--branch <name>` (`--branch main` for the first lineage): missing → `branch_required`; naming another lineage than this folder's → `wrong_branch`. Both errors name this folder's branch, so the fix is in the message.
- A folder with no branches at all: commands unchanged (no flag needed, `--branch main` accepted).
- `--dry-run` applies the same check.
- The lap skill and the tickets skill say when and how to pass `--branch`.

**Done when**
- e2e: required in a branch folder and in a parent with branches; refused with the right name; unchanged in a plain repository;
- skills updated; `SPEC.md` holds the rule.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S109 (L3193–L3218), git `120bb77`.

**What changed**
- `branch_given` (the `--branch` value, else `$LAP_BRANCH`) and `branch_check` in `cmd_common.c`, called by `lap commit` (dry runs included, right after the repository opens) and `lap session start`.
  - A name that is not this folder's → `wrong_branch`, in **any** folder (so `LAP_BRANCH=feat` set for an agent that wandered into the first folder is caught even if the first folder has no branches).
  - No name, in a branch folder or a folder whose registry lists branches → `branch_required`.
  - A branch folder accepts its name or its id; a main folder accepts `main`. Both errors name this folder and its branch (`… records to feat, not other: you may be in the wrong folder; here, pass --branch feat`).
  - A folder with no branches and no name given: unchanged.
- Usage text, `SPEC.md` (§Branches → Committing: say where; the commit synopsis; session start), the draft points there.
- Skills: the lap skill has a "Branches: parallel work in other folders" section (worktree + `branch start`, commit first, `--branch`/`LAP_BRANCH`, read the error as "wrong folder", cite hashes and `<branch>/S<n>` across folders); the tickets skill passes `--branch`/`LAP_BRANCH` on session start and commits in branch folders, and closing comments name sessions as `<branch>/S<n>`.

**Tests:** unit 4,026 (new: `branch_check` in a plain folder, a parent with a registered branch, a branch folder by name and id — its JSON errors print to stdout during the unit run). e2e 110 (new scenario: `branch_required` plain, `--json` and dry run; `wrong_branch` by flag and by environment; name or id accepted; the flag winning over the environment; `LAP_BRANCH` alone starting a session and committing; the parent needing `main`; a folder without branches taking `main` or nothing and refusing another name). Earlier branch scenarios now pass `--branch`/`LAP_BRANCH`.

**For T-110:** coboard starts sessions itself (`packages/coboard/src/lap.ts:223`, `lap session start … --meta ticket=`), so in a folder with branches it needs `LAP_BRANCH` in its environment or its own `--branch`.

item.title: Adoption: place a branch's commits on the parent's version of a file
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Merging (the per-file walk, offsets, conflict). Can start before M-11 is done: it is pure logic.

**Goal.** The algorithm at the heart of `lap merge`, as a pure module with unit tests, before any command uses it.

**Input:** the file at the branch's base (lines), the parent's current version (lines), and the branch's commits to that file in order (each a region: `old_start`, `old_lines`, `old_text`, `new_text`, in the branch's coordinates at that point). **Output:** for each commit, either its region translated to the parent's coordinates (and the parent's text after it), or a conflict — after which the rest of that file's commits are not placed.

**Rules**
- The parent's changes are the diff base → parent (lap's own `diff.c`).
- A branch commit whose region neither overlaps nor touches a parent change moves by the net lines the parent added or removed above it; each placed commit shifts the ones after it.
- Overlap is a conflict. **Touching** is a conflict too: both sides insert at the same point, or one inserts right at the edge of the other's change — either order would be a guess.
- A placed commit's `old_text` must equal the parent's text at the translated position; if it does not, that is a conflict (defensive: it means the mapping is wrong).

**Done when**
- unit tests (in `tests/unit/`): the user's example (parent adds an import at line 4, branch inserts a function at 51 → placed at 52); parent change below the branch's (no shift); deletions on the parent above; several branch commits shifting each other; overlap; both inserting at one point; touching at an edge; a pure insertion at the very top and bottom of a file; CRLF-free comparison as in `file_diff_load`;
- the module has no I/O and does not allocate beyond its arena.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S110 (L3219–L3230), git `da211c0`. From this session on, edits are made one at a time with the Edit tool, each followed by its own lap commit (the user's rule; scripted edits only for rare mechanical changes).

**What changed**
- `src/adopt.{h,c}`: `adopt_place(base, parent, commits[], n) → Placement {placed, start[], eof_nl[], result, why}`. Pure: no I/O; everything in the caller's arena.
  - The parent's changes are `diff_lines(base, parent)` (CR-blind), kept as intervals in the branch's current coordinates.
  - A branch commit `[s, s+old_lines)` conflicts when `s <= pe && ps <= e` for any parent change `[ps, pe)` — this covers overlap, both inserting at one point, and touching at either edge. Otherwise it moves by the net lines of the parent changes wholly above it.
  - Defensive check: the commit's old text must equal the parent's lines where it lands (CR-blind), else a conflict. A delete must cover the whole of the parent's version.
  - Placed commits shift the later parent changes by their own net lines. The end-of-file newline is the commit's when the commit changed it, otherwise the parent's (so a parent that dropped the final newline keeps that through unrelated branch edits).
  - The first conflict stops the file, with a reason in `why`.
- `without_cr` moved from `cmd_common.c` (static) to `str.c` as `lines_without_cr`, so the pure module can share it; `file_diff_load` calls it. No behaviour change: e2e 110 pass, CRLF scenarios included.

**Tests:** unit 4,084 (58 new in `test_adopt.c`): the ticket's example (an import added at line 4 on the parent moves the branch's function from 51 to 52); a parent change below (no shift); deletions above; two branch commits shifting each other and a parent change between them; overlap; both inserting at one point; touching at either edge versus one line away; a conflict stopping the file after one commit placed; insertions at the very top and bottom; CRLF-blind matching; a wrong old text; the parent's missing final newline surviving; a delete on an unchanged file and on a changed one; a file created on the branch alone, and on both sides.

**Noted:** `test_branches.c`'s `branch_check` cases print their JSON errors to stdout during the unit run (harmless, noisy).

item.title: lap merge: adopt a branch into the parent's history
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Merging, §Registry. Blocked by T-107, T-108, T-111.

**Goal.** After `git merge` brought a branch's code into the parent folder, `lap merge <branch> [--dry-run]` brings its history: every commit that can be placed, per file, with what is left shown by `lap status`.

**Build**
- Find the branch's chunks in this folder (a `git merge` brought them) or in its registered folder; else `branch_not_found`. Its base must be in this folder's history, else `unrelated_history`. A branch of a branch whose parent was adopted: resolve its base through the adopted commits' `from` links; if its parent's adoption stopped before that base, refuse and say so.
- Per file, run T-111's placement on: the base version (this history replayed to the base), the parent's shadow, and the branch's commits to that file after the last merge's `head`. Files stopped by an earlier merge of this branch stay stopped.
- Append, under the lock, in the branch's order: each placed commit as an ordinary commit with the next `L` id, translated coordinates, and `"from":"<branch commit hash>"`; each branch session as a new session (new `S` id, same purpose and **meta**, `from`), so `lap session list --meta ticket=T-12` still finds the work. Update shadows as commits do. Never write the working tree.
- Close with the merge record: `{"type":"merge","branch","name","head","adopted","left","stopped":[{"file","at"}],"user","ts","prev"}`.
- Report: adopted N of M; each stopped file and the first commit not adopted; then `lap status` shows the rest to commit by hand.
- `--dry-run`: the report, nothing written.
- Refuse with `branch_required`-style clarity when run in a branch folder against itself, or when the branch is this folder's own parent.

**Done when**
- e2e with real git worktrees: (1) disjoint files → everything adopted, `lap status` clean after; (2) the user's example (import on the parent, function on the branch, same file) → adopted with the shifted line, clean after; (3) a real conflict → that file stops at the right commit, other files adopted, `lap status` shows the resolution to commit, which is committed citing the branch hashes; (4) a second merge after more branch work adopts only the new commits and keeps the stopped file stopped; (5) `--dry-run` writes nothing;
- `lap verify --deep` passes in the parent after each; `lap show` on an adopted commit shows its `from` link;
- `SPEC.md` holds §Merging; `SPEC-branches.md` is down to what the views still need.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S111 (L3231–L3269), git `547d659`.

**What changed**
- **Records:** `from` (the original's hash) on adopted commits, session starts and ends; a new `merge` record (`branch`, `name`, `head`, `adopted`, `left`, `stopped:[{file,at}]`, `user`). Adopted records keep the branch's `ts` and `user` (`repo_append` only stamps a record that has no time). The state heal and the index count adopted sessions' ids but never make one active, nor let an adopted end close the folder's own session.
- **`hist_open_lineage`** (split out of `hist_open_folder`) reads a branch lineage from the chunks a folder holds; **`hist_lineages`** lists the branch lineages present.
- **`lap merge <branch> [--dry-run] [--json]`** (`cmd_merge.c`):
  1. finds the branch by registry or by chunks present;
  2. when its folder is reachable, seals its open chunk under its lock and copies its chunks here;
  3. checks the base;
  4. resumes after the last merge's `head`;
  5. per file, runs `adopt_place` (T-111) against the branch's version at that head and this folder's version now; stopped files stay stopped;
  6. appends new sessions, placed commits and session ends in the branch's order, with `from` links; an already adopted session is reused;
  7. closes with the merge record, updates shadows (never the working tree), and reports.

  `--dry-run` reads the branch folder in place and writes nothing. Errors: `branch_not_found`, `merge_in_branch`, `unrelated_history`, `log_broken`.
- **`lap show`** prints `from: #<short> (adopted … the original is <hash>)`; `from` is in every command's commit JSON.
- `SPEC.md`: record types, §Branches → Merging (five steps, what is left, dry run), the command. The draft points there. The lap skill says how to merge back.

**Tests:** unit 4,106 (new: merge record round trip; `from` on commits, session starts and ends; the effort cap — a parent file rewritten with 1,499 changes diffs as one truncated change, so a branch insertion in it conflicts). e2e 116, on real git worktrees unless said:
1. disjoint files → both adopted as L6, L7; `--dry-run` left `.lap/` byte-identical; `status` clean; the parent's own open session still current; `session list --meta ticket=T-7` finds the adopted session; `show` prints `from`; `verify --deep` ok; a second merge says nothing new.
2. The import-and-function example → adopted at lines 52–53, `status` clean.
3. A real git conflict → `f.txt` stops at the line-10 commit (checked against its hash in the output and the merge record), line 50 and `g.txt` adopted; `status` shows exactly 2 edits left, committed by hand citing the stopped commit's hash; clean after; `verify --deep` ok.
4. A second merge after more work → adopts only the new `g.txt` commit; `f.txt` stays stopped.
5. A plain `cp -R` branch with no git: `lap merge` seals the copy's chunk there and copies it here; the copy folder is deleted and the parent still verifies and knows there is nothing new.
6. The refusals.

**Left to T-113:** `lap show <original hash>` from the parent (hash lookups across lineages) and `verify` walking every lineage present. **Left to T-108:** pruning merged-and-gone registry entries and `branch list` states, now that merge records exist.

item.title: Reading another branch's history: --branch on log, show and rr
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Commands (the `--branch` reading bullet). Blocked by T-107, T-108.

**Goal.** From the parent folder, review a branch's work before or after merging it.

**Build**
- `lap log`, `lap show`, `lap rr` take `--branch <name>` to read another lineage present in this folder (a merged-in branch's chunks) or in a registered branch folder. Without the flag, they read this folder's own lineage, as now.
- `lap show <hash>` finds a commit in any lineage present, so an adopted commit's `from` link can be followed; the output says which branch it belongs to.
- `--json` outputs carry the lineage (`branch`) of each commit.

**Done when**
- e2e: log/show/rr of a branch from its parent, before and after `git merge` brought its chunks; following a `from` link with `show`;
- `SPEC.md` documents the flag and the JSON field.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S112 (L3270–L3313), git `a550c96`.

**What changed**
- **Records know their branch.** A reader-only `lineage` label on records (never encoded), set by `repo_log_load` (records and chunks walked together) and `idx_fetch` from the chunk a record was read from: `main`, or the branch's name (`hist_label`). Commit JSON everywhere now carries `"branch"`.
- **`--branch <name>` on `lap log`, `lap show`, `lap rr`** (`repo_view_branch` in `cmd_common.c`): reads a registered branch from its folder when reachable, else from its chunks here; `--branch main` in a branch folder reads the parent's history to the base; this folder's own name changes nothing; `unknown_branch` otherwise. It is a reader's flag — `LAP_BRANCH` does not set it. The repository is marked `foreign` so the index (which covers only this folder's history) is never used for it.
- `branch_find` / `branch_folder_is` moved from `lap merge` into `cmd_common.c`, shared by merge and the view.
- **`lap show <hash>`** without `--branch` looks in every branch whose chunks are here when this history lacks the hash, so an adopted commit's `from` opens its original; `show` prints `branch: <name>` for a commit that is not main's.
- **`lap rr`** marks adopted commits `(from #<short>)` in its trajectory.
- **`lap verify`** also walks every other branch whose chunks are here: `branch b: chain ok: 8 records` / `CHAIN BROKEN`, and `branches: [{branch, records, chain_ok, chain_error?}]` in JSON; a broken one fails the command. (This was the draft's last "still to come" for chunks.)
- `SPEC.md`: §Branches → Reading another branch, the three synopses, verify. The draft is down to `branch list/forget/move`, the registry rules, the board and the views.

**Tests:** unit 4,109 (new: `hist_label` for parent and branch chunks). e2e 117, new scenario on a git worktree pair:
- **Before `git merge`** (read from the registered folder): `log --branch b --json` carries the branch's behavior and `"branch":"b"`; plain `log` does not; `rr --branch b`; `show L5 --branch b` prints `branch: b`; `unknown_branch`. From the branch folder, `--branch main` shows only base commits with `"branch":"main"`.
- **After `git merge`, with the branch folder moved away:** reads from the chunks here; `lap merge`; `show <from>` (full and `#`-prefixed short) finds the original with `branch: b`; `verify` reports the branch's chain, and fails naming it when one of its records is changed.

Also: `rr` of an adopted session shows `(from #…)`.

item.title: The branch registry: where branches live, as hints
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Registry and §Commands. Works with T-107 (which adds entries).

**Goal.** The parent knows where its branch folders are, for `lap merge` and the views — and never fails because of it.

**Build**
- `.lap/branches.json`: `[{id, name, path (absolute), base, started}]`, machine-local, not committed, written atomically under the lock.
- Checked, never trusted: an entry counts only if its folder exists and that folder's `.lap` is that branch (by the `branch` record's id).
- Pruning, by writers only: an entry whose branch was merged up to its head (T-112's merge record says so) and whose folder is gone is dropped silently. Unmerged or stopped-at-a-conflict and gone: kept, reported as `missing`.
- `lap branch list [--json]`: each branch's state (`active`, `merged`, `partly merged`, `missing`), commits since base and since the last merge, last known path. In a branch folder, also its own name, parent and base.
- `lap branch forget <branch>`, `lap branch move <branch> <path>` (the new path must hold that branch).
- No command fails because of the registry; the one error is `lap merge` finding the branch nowhere (T-112).

**Done when**
- e2e: a deleted unmerged branch shows as `missing` and `forget` removes it; `move` repoints a moved folder; a folder reused for something else is not taken for the branch; a deleted **merged** branch disappears on the next writing command without a message (with a stand-in merge record until T-112 lands, then with a real merge);
- `branch list --json` shape documented in `SPEC.md` (§Registry, §Commands moved from the draft).

item.title: coboard: agents in a branch folder work the parent's board
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §The board. Independent of the lap CLI work.

**Goal.** One board for everyone: an agent in a git worktree or a copied folder moves tickets and comments on the parent folder's board, not on a copy that git would later have to merge.

**Build**
- coboard finds its board by walking up to `.coboard/` (see `packages/coboard/src/store.ts`, `findBoard`). Add an override that points it at another folder's board: an environment variable for the MCP server (e.g. `COBOARD_DIR`) and a setting for the Board view, passed through by the combined extension like `LAP_BIN`.
- Writes keep coboard's existing lock, so several agents in several folders writing one board stay safe.
- When a folder is a lap branch and no override is set, say so where it helps (e.g. the Board view notes that this folder's board is a copy), rather than guessing the parent.
- Docs: the README's Coboard section, and the tickets skill (agents in a branch folder set the override).

**Done when**
- tests: with the override, reads and writes go to the other folder's board; two processes writing through it concurrently lose nothing;
- the combined extension passes the setting to the coboard MCP server; `npm run package` passes its check.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S114 (L3330–L3362), git `73b0b5a`.

**One change to the ticket's approach, and why.** The ticket asked for an override (env + setting) and, without one, only a note in a branch folder "rather than guessing the parent". The override is built as asked. But an agent in a worktree usually cannot set its own MCP server's environment, so a note alone would leave it writing to the copy. So `lap branch start` now also writes the parent folder's path to a machine-local `.lap/parent`, and coboard follows that. It is not a guess: lap recorded it when the branch started, and it is only followed when that folder has a board.

**What changed**
- lap: `branch start` writes `.lap/parent`; `SPEC.md` layout lists it as a hint lap itself never reads. e2e checks it.
- coboard `locateBoard(from, override = COBOARD_DIR)` (store.ts), in order:
  1. the override — a folder holding `.coboard/`, or that `.coboard/` itself;
  2. a lap branch folder's `.lap/parent`, when that folder has a board;
  3. the first `.coboard/` above.

  It returns `via`, and the MCP server uses it for reads, writes and a ticket's sessions. Writes keep the board's existing lock.
- coboard `startSession(cwd, …)` runs in the folder where the work is, and adds `--branch <id>` in a lap branch folder, or `--branch main` where the registry lists branches. It adds nothing when `LAP_BRANCH` is set or there are no branches, so an older lap still works.
- Board view: new setting **Board › Board Folder**. The view's description says whose board it shows when it is not the folder's own ("proj's board (this folder is a lap branch)"). "Start lap Session" now runs in the window's folder, not the board's.
- The combined extension hands Board Folder to the coboard MCP server as `COBOARD_DIR`; `check.mjs` asserts it (and that kb's server does not get it).
- Docs: the root README (Lap: parallel work in branch folders; Coboard: one board per project; the git-branch limitation rewritten), the tickets skill, and the draft's board section marked built.

**Tests:** coboard 29 (5 new in `locate.test.ts`: the lookup order, including a parent without a board not being followed; the MCP tools in a branch folder writing to the parent's board and leaving the copy alone; `COBOARD_DIR` from an unrelated folder, with no board created there; **two processes writing 25 tickets each through the override → 50 tickets, 50 distinct ids**; `branchArgs`). coboard-vscode 36 pass. Combined: build + check — 34 commands, 3 MCP servers, no errors. lap e2e 119.

**Not verified:** the Board view's description in a real VS Code window (compiled and typechecked only).

item.title: Lap History: branches, and adopted commits linking to their originals
item.description:
**Read first:** `cli/lap-cli/SPEC-branches.md` §Views. Blocked by T-106, T-108, T-113.

**Goal.** Watch agents' branches from the parent folder while they work, and see after a merge where each adopted commit came from.

**Build**
- A Branches group in Lap History from `lap branch list --json`: name, state (`active`, `merged`, `partly merged`, `missing`), commits since base / since last merge. Expanding an active or merged branch shows its sessions and commits (read with `--branch`), in the same layout as main's.
- A `missing` branch shows its last path and the two ways to fix it (`lap branch move`, `lap branch forget`), as commands the user can run.
- Adopted commits on main show a link to their original (`from`), which reveals the branch commit; a stopped file after a merge is listed with the first commit not adopted.
- Live refresh when a registered branch folder's open chunk grows (watch registered paths, cheaply).

**Done when**
- unit tests for the branch model built from `branch list --json` and for `from` links;
- rendered in light and dark themes with: an active branch, a merged one, a partly merged one, a missing one.

item.title: Sessions cited on the board name their branch, and lap reads that form
item.description:
**Context.** A ticket finds its sessions through the session's meta (`--meta ticket=T-12`), and adoption copies the meta, so tickets keep their work across a merge — that part is fine. But the tickets skill also has agents write session ids into board comments ("Done in lap session S104"), and in a branch folder those ids are ambiguous:
- a branch continues its parent's counters while the parent keeps counting too, so the branch's `S104` and a later `S104` on the parent can both exist;
- on adoption the branch's session gets a new id on the parent, so a comment written in the branch points at the old one.

**Goal.** A session id written anywhere is unambiguous and can be read back with lap.

**Build**
- The form `<branch>/S<n>` (branch name or id, e.g. `parser-fix/S104`) names a session of that lineage. Wherever a command takes a session (`lap rr`, `lap log --session`, `lap session list`…), accept it, reading the lineage as `--branch` does (T-113). After that branch was adopted, resolving `parser-fix/S104` from the parent also names the adopted session (through its `from` link), so an old comment leads to both.
- A bare `S<n>` keeps meaning this folder's own lineage.
- Output: in a branch folder, and for sessions of other lineages, print sessions as `<branch>/S<n>` (human and `--json`, e.g. a `ref` field), so what agents copy is already qualified.
- Skills: the tickets skill's closing comment cites `<branch>/S<n>` when working in a branch folder (plain `S<n>` on main), or commit hashes, which are unique everywhere; the lap skill explains the form.

**Done when**
- e2e: a branch and its parent each have an `S104`; `lap rr parser-fix/S104` and `lap rr S104` from the parent show different sessions; after `lap merge`, `parser-fix/S104` from the parent shows the adopted session with its `from` link;

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S115 (L3363–L3413), git `c575dea`.

**What changed**
- **Model** (`model.ts`): commits carry `from`; sessions carry their record index and `from`. The history reads the way the CLI does: an adopted session start never becomes active and an adopted end never closes the folder's own session (without this, a merged branch's open session would show as active in the parent). The `branch` record marks where a branch folder's own part starts and clears the active session. Merge records are collected with their stopped files.
- **`branches.ts`** (pure): `parseBranchList` turns `lap branch list --json` into rows; anything else reads as no branches, including an older lap. It attaches each stopped file's first commit not adopted, taken from this folder's merge records. `ownPart` cuts a branch log to what follows its branch record; `branchView` gives a branch's own sessions.
- **`chunks.ts`**: `lineageFiles` (a branch's history: the parent's chunks to its base chunk, then its own, refused unless its first record is its branch record) and `folderFiles`. **This also fixes a gap left by T-106:** in a branch folder, Lap History read only `main`'s chunks and missed the branch's own work.
- **Host**: `BranchSource` runs `lap branch list` asynchronously and reads each branch's log from its folder, else from its chunks here — again only when its files grew. It watches registered folders' `.lap/log/*.jsonl` and pushes a fresh page when lap answers. Two new messages: `original` (opens `lap show <hash>`'s text in a preview editor — lap finds the hash in the branches whose chunks are here) and `branchFix` (Forget with a modal confirmation; Move with a folder picker; then refresh).
- **Webview**:
  - a **Branches** group above the history: state icon (colored), name, state, commit counts;
  - opened: a missing branch's path with **Moved: find it…** / **Forget it** buttons, each stopped file with its first commit not adopted as a link, and the branch's own sessions and commits;
  - branch commits keep their open and selected state under a scoped key (ids repeat across folders) and open no diff, since the diff provider has only this folder's log;
  - an adopted commit's detail shows **From: #<short> (adopted from a branch)**, linking to its original.
  - `lap.css` has the new styles.

**Tests:** lap-vscode 48 pass (new `branches.test.ts`, 5 tests: rows from list JSON including all four states and stopped commits from merge records; malformed lists; `ownPart` and the branch view; `from` links, adopted sessions not active, merges collected, a branch starting with none open; `lineageFiles`/`folderFiles` in a folder and from the parent's chunks, refusing a chunk without its branch record). Combined: build + check, no errors.

**Render:** a scratch project built with the new lap — `parser` active (worktree, 2 commits in an open session), `docs` merged, `cleanup` partly merged (a real git conflict stopped `app.txt`), `spike` missing (plain copy, deleted unmerged). The real host (fake `vscode`, the new `lap` on PATH, waiting for its async answer) fed the real bundle; headless Chrome, light and dark: all four states, the stopped file with `#0d66b70`, the two fixes, and the adopted `L6` showing `From: #b6e8e41`. The first render laid the stopped line out on three lines; it was fixed and rendered again.

**Not verified:** live refresh from a branch folder's writes, Move/Forget and opening an original in a real VS Code window. They are wired and typechecked, but the fake host has no file watching, dialogs or editors.

item.title: Convert this repository's own history to chunks
item.description:
This repository records its own work with the installed `lap` (`/usr/local/bin/lap`, the user's build), which knows only `.lap/log.jsonl`. Converting it while the epic is being built would mean recording with a development build and would break the installed `lap` and the installed Lap History extension until both are rebuilt.

So the conversion waits for the end of E-14: once the CLI and the extension that read chunks are final, run the final build's first write here (it converts by itself), check it, and tell the user to `make install` and reinstall the extension.

A scratch copy of this log (3,338 records) was already converted by T-105's build: 12 chunks, byte-identical, `verify --deep` clean.

**Done when:** `.lap/log/` holds this repository's history, `.lap/log.jsonl` is gone from git, `lap verify --deep` passes, and the user knows to install the new CLI and extension.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S119, git `8f2e54a`, with the final build (`cli/lap-cli/bin/lap`).

- Before: the new build read the old `.lap/log.jsonl` as it is (readers never convert): `verify --deep` → 3,701 records, 567 files, 0 mismatches.
- The first write (`session start` for this ticket) moved it into **12 chunks** in `.lap/log/`. The chunks' bytes are identical to the old file as a prefix, compared with a copy taken just before. `verify --deep` after: 3,702 records (plus the new session start), 567 files, 0 mismatches.
- git: `.lap/log.jsonl` removed from the index, `.lap/log/` added (14 files changed, one commit). `.gitignore` keeps `!**/.lap/log.jsonl` for folders not converted yet.
- The installed `/usr/local/bin/lap` (older) now stops with `cannot read log …/.lap/log.jsonl` and writes nothing: it fails safe.

**For the user:** `make install` in `cli/lap-cli` (or the CMake install) to get the new `lap` on PATH; rebuild and reinstall the procode extension (`npm run package`) so Lap History and the Board read chunks and branches. Until then, record here with `cli/lap-cli/bin/lap`.
