author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S120**, git `75d9cab`.

**What changed**
- A session outside its own folder is named `<branch>/S<n>` (the branch's name or id). `lap rr`, `lap log --session` and `lap search --session` accept it and read that branch as `--branch` does. A bare `S<n>` still means this folder's own session.
- From the parent, after `lap merge`, `<branch>/S<n>` finds the adopted session through its `from` link. rr labels it e.g. `S9 (adopted from feat/S4)`, so a comment written from inside the branch still leads to the work.
- lap prints the qualified name wherever a session belongs to a branch:
  - `session start` / `current` / `list`;
  - log and search rows;
  - `show`;
  - rr headers;
  - histories read with `--branch`.
- JSON adds `ref` (sessions) and `session_ref` (commits); `id` and `session` keep the bare ids, so existing consumers keep working.
- Errors: `unknown_branch` for a name that is no branch here, `unknown_session` for a session the branch doesn't have.
- SPEC.md has a new "Naming sessions" subsection. The lap skill says lap prints the form and accepts it. The tickets skill's step 8 already asked for `<branch>/S<n>` in comments.

**Decided**: I qualified the name rather than renumbering sessions per folder. Ids are a derived count, and renumbering would break every existing citation.

**Tests**: 4,129 unit tests pass (including session_ref). 120 e2e scenarios pass, including "sessions are named <branch>/S<n> where ids repeat across folders".

**Not verified**: the board and extension views still show bare ids plus the branch. They don't read `ref` yet.

item.title: lap: chunked history and branches in other folders
item.description:
Agents cannot work in parallel on one codebase today: lap has one history, one active session, and files on disk are shared. The design discussed with the user on 2026-09-27:

- **Chunks.** The log becomes a directory of chunk files, ordered by the hash chain (a chunk's first record's `prev` is the previous chunk's last hash). A chunk is sealed at a size limit or when a branch starts from it, and never written again. Existing logs split losslessly (no record or hash changes).
- **Branches.** A branch is a lap repository in another folder (a git worktree or a plain copy) whose history shares its parent's up to a base hash. `lap branch start [name] --from <parent>`. With branches, a commit must name its target.
- **Merge = adopt.** git merges the code; `lap merge` adopts the branch's commits into the parent's history with a three-way offset mapping (base / parent / branch), per file, stopping a file at its first conflict. What is left is committed by hand. Adopted commits get the parent's ids and a `from` link.
- **Registry.** The parent records where its branches live (`.lap/branches.json`, machine-local). It is hints, never errors: merged-and-gone branches are pruned silently; unmerged-and-gone ones are shown as missing.
- **The board is not branched**: agents in branch folders write to the parent's board.
- Views show branches.

The SPEC comes first, as a draft reviewed by the user, then chunks, then branches.

item.title: Robustness
item.description: Findings of the E-14 audit (2026-09-27): four read-only audits of chunks, branches and registry, merge by adoption (a property test of ~4,300 real git+lap merges: no wrong placement), and the views/SPEC/docs. The design held; these are the edges — odd paths, failures midway, damaged files, the views. Ranked by severity in each ticket; decisions for the user are marked **Decision**.

item.title: branch start: a folder can become a branch of itself through another spelling of its path
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** `same_folder` compares paths as strings (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_branch.c:152-163`), without resolving them.

**Repro** (macOS, case-insensitive disk): in a lap repo at `/x/s7e-p`, run `lap branch start self --from /x/S7E-P`. Also through a symlink to the folder itself (once the parent's open chunk is empty, e.g. right after another branch start).

**Observed:** `{"ok":true}`; `.lap/lineage` names `self`; `lap branch list` says "this folder is branch self … of main"; `lap commit --branch main` → `wrong_branch`. The registry just written, and every earlier branch entry, is deleted, because "here" and "there" are one folder and the copied-registry cleanup removes it (`cmd_branch.c:306-312`, lineage written at `:332`).

**Fix:** compare canonical paths (realpath, and on Windows the final path of the handle), and also refuse when both folders' `.lap` are the same directory (same device and inode / file id), which catches every spelling.

**Done when:** e2e refuses `same_folder` for a case variant, a symlink, and a `..` path, and nothing in the folder changes.

item.title: board_sessions gives a branch session the parent's commits
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** The `board_sessions` MCP tool calls `sessionCommits(board.root, session.id)` without the session's branch (`packages/coboard/src/mcp.ts:208`). Branch and parent both number sessions from the base, so a session that exists only in a branch gets the parent's session with the same bare id. The Board view already passes it (`packages/coboard-vscode/src/extension.ts:353`).

**Repro:** a branch `feat` has S1 tagged `ticket=T-7`; the parent has its own S1 tagged T-9. `board_sessions T-7` returns session `{id:"S1", branch:"feat"}` with the T-9 commit.

**Fix:** pass `session.branch` (it is already in `ticketSessions`' result).

**Done when:** a coboard test with a branch and a parent sharing a session id returns each session's own commits through `board_sessions`.

item.title: lap merge validates before it writes anything
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** `lap merge` copies the branch's chunks into the parent and seals the branch's chunk (`bring_chunks`, `cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_merge.c:128-132`) before its checks (`:159-176`).

**Repro:** tamper the second line of the branch's `<id>.000001.jsonl`, then `LAP_BRANCH=main lap merge feat` in the parent. Refused with `log_broken`, but the broken chunk is already in the parent's `.lap/log/` and the branch's chunk sealed; the parent's `lap verify` now fails (`branch feat: CHAIN BROKEN`). Same ordering for `unrelated_history`.

**Fix:** read and verify the branch's history (chain, base in this history, lineage) from wherever it is first; bring chunks and seal only once the merge will go ahead.

**Done when:** e2e: a merge refused for a broken branch log, and for `unrelated_history`, leaves both folders' `.lap` byte-identical.

item.title: lap merge recovers from a failure part-way through
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** Adopted records are appended one at a time (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_merge.c:287-348`) and the merge record comes last. A rerun starts again from the previous merge's head; only `session_start` is de-duplicated by `from` (`:296-297`), commits and `session_end` are not.

**Repro:** a branch with 3 commits to `f.txt` (lines 2, 5, 9). In the parent, make `.lap/log` unwritable part-way (e.g. `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES=1400` so a new chunk is needed, then `chmod a-w .lap/log`), `lap merge b` → io_error after appending the session and two commits, no merge record. Restore, rerun: "adopted 0 of 3", `f.txt` stopped at a commit that was already adopted ("overlaps a change the parent made" — lap's own adoption), the third commit never adopted, the branch "partly merged" for good.

**Fix (pick one, say which in the SPEC):** a rerun recognises records already adopted (by `from`) and continues after them; or the merge is made atomic (write the whole run, then publish it). Either way the SPEC's crash-safety section covers merge.

**Done when:** e2e: a merge interrupted at each record boundary, then rerun, ends with the same history (up to ids) as an uninterrupted merge; `verify --deep` passes.

item.title: Adoption tells an empty file from a missing one
item.description:
**Found by the audit's property test (confirmed).** `cmd_merge.c:254-257` computes whether the file exists at the base and on the parent (`base_has`, `parent_has`) but never passes that on; `adopt_place` (`adopt.c:69-74`) sees only 0-line `Lines`, the same for "empty" and "absent".

**Repros:**
- base has an empty `e.txt`; the parent `lap commit`s its deletion; the branch writes `hello\n` into it; `git merge`; `lap merge` → "adopted 1 of 1": the parent's history is create, delete, then an edit of a deleted file. Expected: stop (git reports modify/delete).
- base has no `n.txt`; parent creates it empty, branch creates it with content → a second `create` of an existing file adopted.
- base has an empty `e.txt`, both sides delete it → a second `delete` adopted.

**Fix:** give placement the existence of the file on each side and treat create/delete/edit against existence mismatches as conflicts.

**Done when:** unit tests for the three cases (and their mirror images) in the adoption module, and an e2e case; `verify --deep` passes.

item.title: No git conflict in .lap/log when the branch commits between git merge and lap merge
Branch names stay unique for good, and name/S<n> never means an inherited session
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** After branch `feat` is merged, its folder removed and pruned, a new `lap branch start feat` is accepted: `name_taken` checks only the registry (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_branch.c:241`).

**Observed:** `lap rr feat/S2` in the parent then prints the parent's own pre-base S2 labelled as feat's (instead of the first feat's session). Once the second `feat` is merged and pruned too, the name resolves to whichever lineage sorts first (`branch_find` in `cmd_common.c`: registry, then walk order), so the first feat's sessions are unreachable by name. `session_resolve` searches the branch's whole view, inherited records included.

**Fix:** `name_taken` also covers every lineage whose chunks are present (and adopted `from` references); `name/S<n>` resolves only sessions of that lineage's own records.

**Done when:** e2e: reusing a merged branch's name is refused; `feat/S2` for an id that exists only before the base is `unknown_session`, not the parent's session.

item.title: Paths through a symlink work for branch start, merge and the registry
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** `plat_mkdir` treats an existing symlinked path component as a failure: `EEXIST`, then `plat_is_dir` uses `lstat` (`cli/lap-cli/src/platform.c:205,218`). Reached from `hist.c:336` (new chunk / seal) and `cmd_merge.c:78`; `repo_abspath` does not canonicalise.

**Repros:** `ln -s parent link; cp -R parent w; cd w; lap branch start x --from ../link` → `parent_read_only: cannot create …/link/.lap/log` (the real path works). After `lap branch move feat <symlinked path>`, `lap merge feat` → `io_error: cannot create …/.lap/log`.

**Fix:** follow symlinks when checking an existing directory (`stat`), and canonicalise folder paths where lap stores or compares them (with the self-branch ticket).

**Done when:** e2e passes `--from`, `branch move` and `merge` through a symlinked path.

item.title: A branch folder's identity files never travel through git
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed, design gap).** `.lap/lineage` and `.lap/parent` are machine-local, but lap does nothing to keep them out of git: `lap init` writes no ignore rules, and `cli/lap-cli/README.md:195-202` offers "track it or ignore `.lap/`".

**Repro:** a repo that `git add -A`s without ignoring `.lap/*`; a worktree branch; parent `git merge feat` → clean merge that brings `.lap/lineage`, and the parent silently becomes branch `feat` (`merge_in_branch`, `wrong_branch` on main).

**Fix (decide in the ticket):** `lap init` (and `branch start`) write `.lap/.gitignore` ignoring everything but `log/` — self-contained, needs no change to the project's `.gitignore`; and/or lap refuses to trust a `lineage` whose branch record is not the first record of this folder's own chunks (so a stray file cannot change a folder's identity).

**Done when:** the repro above leaves the parent `main`; README's git advice matches.

item.title: A torn line in a sealed chunk: readers and writers agree, and nothing builds on a broken history
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** Readers look for a torn tail at the end of the whole history stream (`cli/lap-cli/src/rec.c:320-326`); the writer repairs only the last chunk and returns when it is empty (`hist.c:292-301`).

**Repro:** a repo in 5 chunks; `printf '{"type":"commit","partial' >> .lap/log/main.000005.jsonl`; create an empty `main.000006.jsonl`; `lap verify` → "chain ok … note: torn trailing record ignored … the next commit repairs it" (`cmd_verify.c:~258`); commit an edit → succeeds with "index sync: … expected ':'"; `verify` → "main.000005.jsonl line 5: expected ':'" — the torn bytes now run into chunk 6's first line. Not produced by lap itself (seal and merge repair first); it comes from git or copying.

**Related:** cutting 30 bytes off a sealed chunk makes `verify` report a parse error rather than "sealed chunk … was modified", and `commit` still succeeds on the unreadable history, only warning that the index sync failed (`idx.c:334`).

**Fix:** a torn tail outside the open chunk is damage, not a crash: readers report it (naming the chunk), and writers refuse to append on any history that does not read cleanly.

**Done when:** e2e for both repros: `verify` names the damaged sealed chunk, `commit` refuses, nothing is written.

item.title: Readers never see a half-converted history
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** The conversion from `log.jsonl` publishes chunks one at a time (temp file + rename, `cli/lap-cli/src/hist.c:446-467`, `:458`), and readers use the legacy file only when there are no chunks (`hist.c:113`), listing the directory while renames happen (`hist.c:96-108`, `platform.c:566-588`).

**Repros:**
- crash: `log.jsonl` plus only chunks 1–2 of its conversion present → `lap log -n 1` shows L8 as head (real: L20); `lap verify` says "chain ok: 10 records" (real: 22), exit 0, nothing mentions `log.jsonl`.
- live: converting a typec clone with a small `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES` while looping `lap verify` → 39 of 40 runs fail with "history chunk main.001349.jsonl is missing".

The SPEC's "a crash leaves one or the other complete" is false for a split into several chunks.

**Fix:** convert into a temporary directory and publish it with one rename (then remove `log.jsonl`); readers that find both shapes read `log.jsonl` unless the chunks are a complete conversion of it.

**Done when:** e2e: an interrupted conversion at every chunk boundary is either invisible to readers or read in full; the live loop shows no failures.

item.title: Lap History reports a broken history instead of showing part of it
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** `lineageChunks` (`packages/lap-vscode/src/chunks.ts:39`) stops at the first gap in chunk numbers, and `historyFiles` shows that prefix with no warning, as if it were the whole history. The CLI refuses the same state: with chunks 1 and 3 only, `lap log` → `history chunk main.000002.jsonl is missing`.

**Fix:** a gap (or a chain break at a chunk boundary) puts the view in an error state that names the missing chunk, like the CLI.

**Done when:** a unit test with a missing middle chunk gets the error, not a shorter history; rendered once.

item.title: Lap History reads a growing branch incrementally, off the UI's critical path
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).**
- `BranchSource.read` (`packages/lap-vscode/src/extension.ts:201-208`) re-reads and re-parses the branch's whole history — the parent's chunks up to `base_chunk` plus its own; ~12 chunks / 49 MB in this repo — with a SHA-256 per line, synchronously in the extension host, every time its size changes, although only the branch's own part is kept.
- Every change to the main log runs `branches.refresh()` (`extension.ts:634`), which spawns `lap branch list --json`, even in repositories with no branches.
- `lineageFiles` (`chunks.ts:91`) reads the whole first own chunk (up to 4 MB) just to get its first line, on every refresh in a branch folder.

The main folder's own reading is already incremental (readdir + stat per chunk).

**Fix:** read a branch incrementally from the offset already read, and only its own lineage's chunks (the inherited part is main's, already loaded); run `branch list` only when the registry or a registered folder changed; read just the first line of a chunk.

**Done when:** tests for incremental branch reading; a note in the closing comment of the time taken by a refresh on this repo before and after.

item.title: coboard never waits forever for a lock it cannot create
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed, pre-existing, now reachable through the board override).** In `Board.write` (`packages/coboard/src/store.ts:296-305`), when the lock file cannot be created (e.g. a read-only `.coboard/`), `statSync` throws, the loop `continue`s, and the 5 s deadline is never reached: the write hangs forever (`timeout 15 node t.js` → rc 124).

**Fix:** check the deadline on every iteration, and fail at once with a clear error when the lock cannot be created for a reason other than "exists" (EACCES, EROFS, ENOENT of the folder).

**Done when:** a test with an unwritable board folder gets an error promptly; the MCP tool returns it as a refusal.

item.title: lap status without caches still sees files tracked before they were ignored
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed, pre-existing — breaks the cache contract).** With no index, `lap status` builds the tracked set only from the ignore-filtered walk plus the shadow walk (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_status.c:125-135`), so a file lap tracked before it was added to `.lapignore` disappears from the output when the caches are gone.

**Repro:** a typec clone (its `.coboard/log.jsonl` was committed as L52, `.coboard/` is now in `.lapignore`): cold `lap status` → "clean"; after `lap rebuild` → "modified .coboard/log.jsonl [1] lines 18-63". The SPEC says deleting a cache "must change speed only, never output".

**Fix:** without an index, take the tracked set from the history (every file with a live last commit), the same set the index gives.

**Done when:** e2e: a tracked-then-ignored file shows the same status with and without caches (in both directions: modified, and deleted).

item.title: board_get says when lap failed, instead of showing no sessions
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** When lap fails (missing, too old for the repository's history, broken history), `board_get` returns `"sessions": []` because `packages/coboard/src/mcp.ts:146` drops `ticketSessions`' `ok:false` and its error; `board_sessions` does surface it as `lapError`. An agent concludes the ticket has no work. lap-vscode also runs bare `lap` from PATH with no lap-path setting, so its Branches group and "show original" fail quietly in the same case.

**Fix:** `board_get` carries `lapError` like `board_sessions`; lap-vscode shows lap's error (and takes the same lap path setting the Board already has).

**Done when:** tests with a failing lap stand-in: `board_get` returns the error; Lap History shows it.

item.title: Views keep a merged branch's name after it leaves the registry, and see merged-in branches
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** `mergeSessions` marks adopted sessions with their branch only for branches `lap branch list` returns. Merged-and-gone branches are pruned from the registry (by design), after which adopted sessions show without their branch. Likewise, a branch present only as chunks (brought by `git merge`, never registered here) is invisible: neither Lap History nor the board lists its unadopted sessions — consistent with the SPEC, but a gap.

**Fix:** take the branch name of an adopted session from its `from` link / the `merge` record (history, not the registry); list lineages present in `.lap/log/` alongside registered ones (lap's `branch list` could report them as `present`).

**Done when:** tests: an adopted session keeps its branch name after the branch was pruned; a merged-in unregistered branch's sessions are listed.

item.title: verify blames the right chunk, and writers refuse a broken chain
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** When the chain breaks at a chunk's first record, `verify` always blames the previous chunk (`cli/lap-cli/src/repo.c:536-556`).

**Repro:** a repo in 5 chunks; copy `main.000003.jsonl` to `main.000006.jsonl` (a stray chunk) → "sealed chunk main.000005.jsonl was modified: hash chain broken at main.000006.jsonl line 1". Chunk 5 is intact; chunk 6 is the stray. Same when only the open chunk's first `prev` is wrong. The same state also shows readers silently following the stray chunk (`log` shows L12 as head) and a writer healing state and shadows from the broken chain (`repo.c:160-164`) instead of refusing.

**Fix:** a break at a chunk's first record names that chunk ("does not continue main.000005.jsonl"); writers refuse a history whose chain is broken.

**Done when:** e2e for the stray chunk and the wrong first `prev`: verify names the right chunk; commit refuses.

item.title: Conversion refuses an empty legacy log instead of deleting it
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** A 0-byte (or torn-only) `.lap/log.jsonl` converts into 0 chunks and is deleted (`cli/lap-cli/src/hist.c:446-467`, `repo.c:370-374`): "moved .lap/log.jsonl into 0 chunks", then "error: no history in …/log" — and readers, which printed "no commits yet" before, fail too.

**Repro:** `mkdir -p e1/.lap; : > e1/.lap/log.jsonl`, then any writing command.

**Fix:** an empty legacy log is left alone (or treated as a fresh repository with an `init` record, whichever the SPEC says); never a repository with no history.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro leaves a working repository.

item.title: A conversion resumed under another chunk limit keeps the chain whole
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed; reachable only when the limit changes between runs, i.e. with `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES`).** The "already converted" test accepts chunks longer than the old file that start with it (`cli/lap-cli/src/hist.c:421-428`), so leftover higher chunks from a run under another limit survive; stale higher chunks are removed only after the rewrite (`hist.c:468-474`). A crash between the two deletes `log.jsonl` and breaks the chain.

**Repro:** a legacy log, chunks 1–3 converted at limit 4000, leftover chunks 4–5 from a limit-1000 run, then `lap session end` → `log.jsonl` deleted; `verify` → "CHAIN BROKEN: sealed chunk main.000003.jsonl was modified … main.000004.jsonl line 1".

**Fix:** likely solved by publishing the conversion atomically (the half-converted-history ticket); otherwise remove stale chunks before trusting the set.

**Done when:** e2e for the repro keeps a whole chain.

item.title: Leftover temporary files in .lap/log are cleaned up
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** An interrupted conversion leaves `.tmp.<pid>` files in `.lap/log/` that nothing ever removes. They are committed by git if the project tracks `.lap/log/`.

**Fix:** writers remove temporary files in `.lap/log/` whose process is gone (or that are older than the lock's holder), under the lock.

**Done when:** e2e: a leftover temp file disappears on the next writing command and is never read as a chunk.

item.title: Two branch starts in one folder cannot both succeed
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed, 5 of 5 tries).** Two concurrent `lap branch start` in one folder both succeed: the folder gets two `<id>.000001` lineages and the parent's registry a phantom `missing` entry. The `already_branch` check runs before any lock, and the branch folder itself is never locked (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_branch.c:164-177`).

**Fix:** take this folder's lock for the whole of `branch start` (then the parent's for sealing and registration), and check `already_branch` under it.

**Done when:** e2e: concurrent starts in one folder — exactly one succeeds, the other gets `already_branch`, the registry has one entry.

item.title: branch start refusals: the right code, and no chunk left behind
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).**
- A fully read-only parent (`chmod -R a-w parent/.lap`) gives `no_parent: cannot acquire repository lock` instead of `parent_read_only` (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_branch.c:182-185`) — atomic, but the wrong code.
- With `parent/.lap` read-only but `log/` writable, the refusal (`parent_read_only`) comes after the seal already created an empty `main.000002.jsonl` in the parent (`cmd_branch.c:251` before `:275`).

**Fix:** check everything that can refuse (writability of the parent's `.lap` and `log/`, registry) before sealing; map a lock failure caused by permissions to `parent_read_only`.

**Done when:** e2e: both cases refuse with `parent_read_only` and leave the parent byte-identical.

item.title: A merged branch whose folder now holds another branch is pruned
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** The pruning gate only checks that the folder's `.lap` exists (`cli/lap-cli/src/repo.c:306-312`), so a merged branch whose folder was reused for another branch is never pruned: `lap branch list` shows two entries on one path.

**Fix:** an entry is "gone" when its folder is missing **or holds another branch** (by id), as the registry's own validity rule already says.

**Done when:** e2e: merge `a`, reuse its folder for branch `b` → after the next writing command only `b` is listed.

item.title: session end names the session with its branch
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** In a branch folder, `lap session end` prints "session S2 ended" (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_session.c:322` uses `rec.id`), while the naming rule prints sessions of a branch as `feat/S2` so what agents copy is already qualified.

**Fix:** print the qualified form there (and check every other place a session id is printed in a branch folder).

**Done when:** e2e: `session start` and `session end` in a branch folder print `feat/S<n>`.

item.title: --branch accepts --branch=name and refuses a missing value
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** A trailing `--branch` with no value is silently ignored (the command then fails with `branch_required`, pointing at the wrong problem); `--branch=feat` gives `unknown_flag`.

**Fix:** a value-taking flag with no value is `usage` naming the flag; decide whether lap accepts `--flag=value` for value-taking flags generally (the colour flags already use `=`) and apply it to all of them consistently.

**Done when:** e2e for both forms; SPEC's argument-parsing paragraph says which forms are accepted.

item.title: not_clean explains files git tracks but lap never recorded
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed, UX).** Files that git tracks but lap never committed — e.g. `.coboard/log.jsonl`, which the default `.lapignore` doesn't list — show as `new` in a fresh worktree and block every `branch start` with `not_clean`, with no hint why.

**Fix:** the `not_clean` message says which files are new to lap (never recorded) versus changed, and suggests committing them in the parent or adding them to `.lapignore`; consider adding `.coboard/` (and other tools' state folders procode writes) to the starter `.lapignore`.

**Done when:** e2e: the message names the never-recorded files and the two ways out.

item.title: coboard does not silently switch to a branch's board copy when the parent moves
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** If the parent folder moves, `.lap/parent` goes stale and `locateBoard` falls back to the branch's own `.coboard/` copy (`via: "found"`, `packages/coboard/src/store.ts:96-100`), so agents start writing a second board that git would later have to merge.

**Fix:** when this folder is a lap branch and its recorded parent's board cannot be found, refuse writes with a message naming the stale path and how to fix it (`lap branch move` in the parent / `COBOARD_DIR`), rather than falling back.

**Done when:** a test: a branch folder with a stale `.lap/parent` refuses board writes with that message.

item.title: lap merge reports files stopped by an earlier merge
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** A file stopped by an earlier merge is skipped silently: `cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_merge.c:250-253` adds its commits to `left` but no `stopped` entry.

**Repro:** `f.txt` stops in merge 1; the branch then commits to `f.txt` and `g.txt`; `git merge`; `lap merge b` → "adopted 1 of 2 commits (L6)" with no stopped line; JSON and the merge record have `stopped: []` but `left: 1`. SPEC.md:746-747 says each stopped file is printed with its first unadopted commit and the reason; only `branch list` shows it.

**Fix:** report still-stopped files with their reason ("stopped by an earlier merge at #…").

**Done when:** e2e: the second merge prints and records the still-stopped file.

item.title: lap --help lists the branch-reading flags and the branch/S<n> form
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** `lap --help` omits flags the SPEC documents and that work: `--branch` on `log`, `show` and `rr`; `session list --branch` (help says "--branch on start" only — coboard depends on it); the `<branch>/S<n>` session form; and it may lag other E-14 commands.

**Fix:** bring the help text in `cli/lap-cli/src/main.c` in line with SPEC.md's command list.

**Done when:** every command and flag in SPEC.md appears in `lap --help` (an e2e check greps the help for each).

item.title: lap's README describes branches, merges and the stat cache as they are
SPEC matches merge's effort cap, dry-run JSON and the missing-chunk error
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).**
- **Effort cap:** SPEC.md:353 says that for a file the parent rewrote past the diff cap "every branch commit to it conflicts". In practice the capped change covers only the lines between the unchanged top and bottom, and a branch commit below it is still placed — correctly. Repro: 3,000 lines, parent rewrites 2–2600, branch edits 2999 → adopted.
- **Dry run:** `lap merge --dry-run --json` returns `"commits":[]` while `"adopted":1`; SPEC lists `commits` without saying dry runs leave it empty.
- **Missing chunk:** reported with code `no_repo`; SPEC names no code — give it one (e.g. `history_broken`) and document it.

**Fix:** make the SPEC say what lap does (or change lap where the SPEC is the better rule), for each.

**Done when:** SPEC.md and lap agree on all three, with e2e checks for the dry-run JSON and the error code.

item.title: Keep vendored grammar sources out of this repository's lap history
item.description:
**Found during the audit.** About 35 of this repository's 48 MB of lap history are three `create` records of generated, vendored tree-sitter parsers: `cli/kb-cli/src/third_party/tree-sitter-rust/src/parser.c` (L1689, 6.9 MB), `…/tree-sitter-typescript/tsx/src/parser.c` (L1700, 9.3 MB), `…/tree-sitter-typescript/typescript/src/parser.c` (L1705, 9.3 MB) — each a chunk of its own. Nobody edits them by hand; every vendored update would add more.

**Fix:** add `cli/kb-cli/src/third_party/` to this repository's `.lapignore`. The records already written stay (the log is append-only).

**Done when:** `.lapignore` excludes it; `lap status` no longer lists third-party files; the tickets skill or README says vendored code belongs in `.lapignore`.

item.title: Investigate: lap CLI durability and index suspicions from the audit
item.description:
**Suspicions, not reproduced.** Confirm or dismiss each; file a fix where confirmed.
1. **No directory fsync.** `plat_write_file_atomic` (`cli/lap-cli/src/platform.c:476-480`) and `new_chunk` (`hist.c:355`) never fsync `.lap/log/`. On power loss the conversion's renamed chunks or a new chunk's directory entry may not be durable while a later unlink/rename is.
2. **Stale index on a same-size change.** Index freshness is only `covered == size` (`idx.c:88`) / `covered <= size` (`idx.c:300`). A git merge or conflict resolution rewriting a sealed chunk to the same total size would serve stale offsets silently. (When sizes differ, idx_sync fails on every write until `rebuild`.)
3. **Chunk 1,000,000.** `hist_chunk_name` would write `main.1000000.jsonl`, which `hist_parse_name` ignores (exactly 6 digits, `hist.c:26-31, 41-43`). Theoretical at 4 MB per chunk — decide and document.
4. **Unreadable files counted clean.** `pending_against` skips files `file_diff_load` cannot read (e.g. over 64 MB), so they count as clean for `branch start` (`cmd_branch.c:104-105`).
5. **`--branch main` in a branch folder** reads every main chunk present, not only up to `base_chunk` (`repo_view_branch`, `hist_open`). Matters only if later main chunks reach the folder (merging the parent into the branch — unsupported).
6. **`.lap/parent` write unchecked.** Written with `plat_write_file_atomic`, result ignored (`cmd_branch.c`, T-110 hunk); a failed write makes the board fall back silently.
7. **`lap rebuild` peaks near 1.45 GB** on typec (before and after chunks) — not a regression, but large.

**Done when:** each item is confirmed (with a ticket) or dismissed (with the reason) in this ticket's comments.

item.title: Investigate: board and view suspicions from the audit
item.description:
**Suspicions, not reproduced.** Confirm or dismiss each; fix where confirmed.
1. **Relative board folder.** `locateBoard` resolves a relative `coboard.boardFolder` with `path.resolve` against the extension host's cwd, not the workspace (`packages/coboard/src/store.ts`); the MCP server resolves the same value as `COBOARD_DIR` against its own cwd — they may point at different boards; `~` is not expanded.
2. **Watchers outside the workspace.** Branch-folder watchers use `RelativePattern(Uri.file(path))` for folders outside the workspace; whether VS Code delivers those events is unverified (T-114's comment says the same).
3. **Docs gaps.** The tickets skill does not mention the Board › Board Folder setting (the root README does); neither skill mentions `lap branch list`, `forget`/`move`, or `--branch` for reading.

**Done when:** each item is confirmed (and fixed or ticketed) or dismissed with the reason.

item.title: Decision: branches of branches
item.description:
**Decision for the user.** In the design discussion (2026-09-27) branches of branches were to be supported (with adoption resolving a nested branch's base through `from` links). The implementation and the current SPEC refuse them with `nested_branch` (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_branch.c:187`), probably changed in the design-review amendments (T-118).

**Options:** keep the refusal (simpler; a sub-task branches from the parent instead) — then SPEC states it as a decision; or support them as first designed — then this becomes an implementation ticket (branch start from a branch folder, merge into the branch, merge of the nested branch into main after its parent was adopted, refusal when the parent's adoption stopped before the base).

**Done when:** the user chose, and the SPEC (and, if supporting them, a ticket) says so.

item.title: Decision: identical changes on both sides, and where lap's diff differs from git's
item.description:
**Decision for the user.** From the merge audit's property test (~4,300 real merges, no wrong placement):
- **Identical changes stop the file.** Both sides delete a file; both create it with the same content; a rename (branch deletes `f`, creates `f2`) — each is a conflict today, so the rest of the branch's work on that file is never adopted. git merges these cleanly.
- **lap's diff decides conflicts, and differs from git's in rare cases.** 29 of 3,900 cases placed a commit where `git merge-file` reports a conflict (repeated or blank lines aligned differently; files without a final newline, where git counts an end insertion as a change to the last line) — valid merges under lap's own diff. 201 cases stopped where git merged cleanly (the "touching is a conflict" rule, as designed).

**Options:** accept identical changes on both sides as already done (adopt nothing, stop nothing); align end-of-file-without-newline handling with git; or keep the current rules and document them.

**Done when:** the user chose; SPEC §Merging says it; if behaviour changes, a ticket with e2e cases for each.

item.title: Decision: LAP_BRANCH in a repository with no branches
item.description:
**Decision for the user.** With `LAP_BRANCH=feat` set (e.g. globally by an orchestrator), a commit in a plain repository with no branches fails with `wrong_branch`. That follows "a name that is not this folder's branch is `wrong_branch`, in any folder", but contradicts "a folder with no branches keeps its commands unchanged".

**Options:** plain repositories ignore `LAP_BRANCH` (the flag `--branch` still checks); or keep the refusal (safer against an agent in the wrong folder) and document it.

**Done when:** the user chose; SPEC says it; e2e covers it.

item.title: Branches of branches: start one, merge it into its parent branch or into main
item.description:
**Decided by the user (2026-09-27): support branches of branches.** A branch can start from a branch folder, and a nested branch can be merged into its parent branch **or into main** (any ancestor). This replaces the `nested_branch` refusal (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_branch.c:187`) introduced in the design-review amendments (T-118).

**Terms.** B1 is a branch of main; B2 a branch of B1, based at a hash in B1's lineage.

**Build**
1. **Start.** `lap branch start [name] --from <B1 folder>` works as from main: B2's history is main up to B1's base, then B1 up to B2's base, then its own. Sealing and registration happen in B1 (its open chunk sealed, B2 in B1's registry).
2. **Merge into the parent branch.** In B1's folder, `lap merge B2` — today refused with `merge_in_branch` — adopts B2 into B1's lineage exactly as a merge into main does (placement, `from` links, sessions with their meta, merge record, per-file stops). Later, merging B1 into main carries those adopted commits like any of B1's own.
3. **Merge into main directly.** In main's folder, `lap merge B2`:
   - git's merge of B2 brings B1's work up to B2's base too (B2's git branch contains it), so lap adopts the same: **first B1's commits up to B2's base that main has not adopted yet, then B2's own**, each with its `from` link, in history order, with one merge record per lineage (B1's head advances to B2's base).
   - A later `lap merge B1` into main adopts only B1's commits after what was already adopted, and never adopts B2's commits twice (B2's work reached main directly; if B1 also merged B2, skip the commits whose `from` chain leads to ones already adopted).
   - If adopting B1's part stops a file, B2's commits to that file stop too.
4. **Finding the nested branch.** From main, B2's chunks are found locally (after `git merge`) or through B1's registry (main's registry lists B1; B1's lists B2). `lap branch list` in main shows B2 under B1.
5. **Names and sessions.** `B2/S<n>` resolves from any ancestor; after adoption through `from` links (T-120's rules).
6. **Views.** Lap History and the board show nested branches under their parent (tree), with their states.

**Done when**
- e2e with real git worktrees: B1 from main, B2 from B1; (a) merge B2 into B1, then B1 into main → main holds B1's and B2's commits once each; (b) merge B2 directly into main while B1 is unmerged → main holds B1's commits up to B2's base, then B2's, `lap status` clean after a clean git merge; then merge B1 into main → only B1's later commits are adopted, none twice; (c) a conflict in B1's part stops the same file for B2; `verify --deep` passes everywhere;
- no git conflict under `.lap/log/` in any of these flows;
- `SPEC.md` describes nested branches and merging into any ancestor; `nested_branch` and `merge_in_branch` removed (or kept only where still meaningful).

Related robustness tickets that also apply to nested branches: T-124, T-125, T-127, T-128.

author: claude
body: Decision (user, 2026-09-27): support branches of branches, and allow merging a nested branch into its parent branch or into main. The description is now the implementation ticket. Note for whoever builds it: merging B2 straight into main must adopt B1's unadopted commits up to B2's base first — git's merge of B2 brings that code anyway, so lap's history must carry it, or main's files would hold work its history lacks.

author: claude
body:
**I disagree with the first option; it doesn't fix the repro.** The conflict comes from git's snapshot, not from lap's seal. G2 records the branch's chunk as `[br,B1,B2]`, and after step 4 the parent's copy is `[br,B1,B2,B3]`. Against the base `[br,B1]`, both sides append at the same point with different content, so git conflicts whether or not the file is sealed on disk. lap can't seal "at the branch's git-visible points" either, because it never sees a git commit.

Two approaches do work:
- **A merge driver** (the second option). Both versions are prefixes of one chain, so the driver takes the longer one and refuses anything else. It's configured through `.gitattributes` for `.lap/log/*.jsonl`, and it's the only way to handle the case where `git merge` runs first.
- **`lap merge` doesn't overwrite a branch chunk that git already brought.** It reads the branch's records from the branch folder (or from its own copy) and writes only chunks that are missing here, so the parent's tracked file stays whatever git merged. The cost: until the branch's next `git merge`, `show <from hash>` for B3 needs the branch folder.

I'd do the driver. T-157 multiplies this, because nested chunks arrive through two routes.

author: claude
body:
**The second fix doesn't catch this repro.** After the branch's chunks reach the parent (through `git merge` or `lap merge`), the parent holds `<id>.000001.jsonl`, and that file does open with the branch record. So "trust `lineage` only if its branch record is the first record of this folder's chunks" passes, and the parent still becomes `feat`.

A check that does catch it: the `.lap/parent` that came with the leaked file points at this folder itself. Compare canonical paths or device+inode, as T-122 does. So refuse when a folder's recorded parent is itself, and also when no branch record with that id is in this folder's own lineage (as opposed to chunks copied in from elsewhere).

The `.lap/.gitignore` part is the real fix, and I agree with it. It needs to un-ignore `log/` and itself.

author: claude
body:
**Partly.** Blaming the chunk before was deliberate (`repo.c:536-546`, from T-104). A break at chunk N's first record is what you see when chunk N-1 was truncated or appended to, and N-1 really is to blame there. Switching the blame to N would get that case wrong instead.

The boundary alone can't tell which side changed, so use what the chunks show:
- N's first `prev` matches a record inside N-1 that isn't its last → N-1 was appended to: blame N-1.
- N-1's last hash is some other chunk's first `prev` (a duplicate or stray N) → blame N.
- Otherwise, name both: "main.000006.jsonl does not continue main.000005.jsonl".

The Done when should cover a truncated sealed chunk as well as the stray chunk.

"Writers refuse a broken chain" is the same fix as T-131's "writers refuse to append on a history that does not read cleanly". One implementation, one ticket.

author: claude
body:
**Partly: I'd change the fix.**
- **Don't check pids.** `.lap/log/` travels through git, so a pid from another machine means nothing here. Writers already hold the repository lock, so under the lock any `*.tmp.*` in `.lap/log/` is a leftover and can go.
- **Better: keep temp files out of `.lap/log/`.** Write them in `.lap/` (same filesystem, so the rename stays atomic) and rename into `log/`. git never sees them, and readers never have to skip them. T-132's temp-directory conversion does this for conversion; `plat_write_file_atomic` for new chunks and seals should follow.

Cleanup then only matters for leftovers from older versions.

author: claude
body: **Partly.** Refusing writes isn't enough. Reads from the branch's own `.coboard/` copy are stale too: it's the board as of the branch's git base, so an agent would see old statuses and miss tickets created since. When a lap branch's recorded parent has no board, reads should fail with the same message (stale path, `lap branch move` / `COBOARD_DIR`), or at least say in every result that they come from a stale copy.

author: claude
body:
**The design is sound, but there are two dependencies it doesn't name.**

1. **It depends on T-158 (identical changes).** In flow (a), then a later `lap merge B1`, and in flow (b), main already holds B2's change (adopted directly), and B1's history contains the same change again (B1 adopted B2 too, or B1's commits up to B2's base were already adopted). Build step 3 says to skip commits whose `from` chain is already adopted. But their effect is still in the file, and when B1's later commits are placed, main's version differs from the base by that change. adopt.c sees it as a parent change that touches or overlaps the branch's own, which is the "identical changes on both sides stop the file" rule from T-158. Unless skipped commits count as "already applied" in placement (the diff treats their region as common), the files B2 touched will stop. Decide T-158 first, or build that rule here.
2. **No git conflict under `.lap/log/`** in these flows depends on T-127. B1's and B2's chunks reach main both through git (B2's git branch contains B1's chunks) and through `lap merge`. I've commented on T-127 that only the merge driver (or not overwriting git-brought chunks) removes the conflict; sealing earlier doesn't.

Also, B2's branch record can't carry the whole chain in `base`/`base_chunk`. B2's view is main to B1's base, then B1 to B2's base. Each branch record holds one hop, so the reader follows `parent` records up the chain. The SPEC should say so.

item.title: Identical changes on both sides are already done, not a conflict

author: claude
body: Decision (user, 2026-09-27): identical changes on both sides are already done — nothing adopted, nothing stopped. lap's own diff and the touching rule otherwise stay as they are. The description is now the implementation ticket. It is a prerequisite of T-157.

item.title: LAP_BRANCH is ignored in a repository with no branches
item.description:
**Decided by the user (2026-09-27).** In a repository with no branches (not a branch folder, no registered branches), `LAP_BRANCH` is ignored: commands behave as without it. The explicit `--branch <name>` flag still checks everywhere (`wrong_branch` if it names another lineage).

**Why:** orchestrators set `LAP_BRANCH` for a whole run; failing commits in unrelated plain repositories punishes exactly that use. The flag keeps the safety check for whoever asks for it.

**Done when**
- e2e: `LAP_BRANCH=feat` in a plain repository → commit succeeds; `--branch feat` in the same repository → `wrong_branch`; in a branch folder and in a parent with branches, `LAP_BRANCH` keeps its current meaning;
- `SPEC.md` and the lap skill say it.

body: Decision (user, 2026-09-27): plain repositories ignore `LAP_BRANCH`; `--branch` still checks. The description is now the implementation ticket.

author: claude
body:
**Blocked by T-158 and T-127** (as the review comment pointed out):
- T-158 — a nested branch's work reaches main twice (B2→main then B1→main, or B2→B1→main); without "identical changes are already done", the second arrival stops the file.
- T-127 — chunks reach main both through git and through `lap merge`; the git conflict on `.lap/log/` must be fixed first (merge driver keeping the longer version).

Also for the SPEC (from the review): a nested branch's history is found by following the chain of `branch` records, one hop at a time.

item.title: Branches of branches: start one, merge it into its parent branch or into main
item.description:
**Decided by the user (2026-09-27): support branches of branches.** A branch can start from a branch folder, and a nested branch can be merged into its parent branch **or into main** (any ancestor). This replaces the `nested_branch` refusal (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_branch.c:187`) introduced in the design-review amendments (T-118).

**Terms.** B1 is a branch of main; B2 a branch of B1, based at a hash in B1's lineage.

**Build**
1. **Start.** `lap branch start [name] --from <B1 folder>` works as from main: B2's history is main up to B1's base, then B1 up to B2's base, then its own. Sealing and registration happen in B1 (its open chunk sealed, B2 in B1's registry).
2. **Merge into the parent branch.** In B1's folder, `lap merge B2` — today refused with `merge_in_branch` — adopts B2 into B1's lineage exactly as a merge into main does (placement, `from` links, sessions with their meta, merge record, per-file stops). Later, merging B1 into main carries those adopted commits like any of B1's own.
3. **Merge into main directly.** In main's folder, `lap merge B2`:
   - git's merge of B2 brings B1's work up to B2's base too (B2's git branch contains it), so lap adopts the same: **first B1's commits up to B2's base that main has not adopted yet, then B2's own**, each with its `from` link, in history order, with one merge record per lineage (B1's head advances to B2's base).
   - A later `lap merge B1` into main adopts only B1's commits after what was already adopted, and never adopts B2's commits twice (B2's work reached main directly; if B1 also merged B2, skip the commits whose `from` chain leads to ones already adopted).
   - If adopting B1's part stops a file, B2's commits to that file stop too.
4. **Finding the nested branch.** From main, B2's chunks are found locally (after `git merge`) or through B1's registry (main's registry lists B1; B1's lists B2). `lap branch list` in main shows B2 under B1.
5. **Names and sessions.** `B2/S<n>` resolves from any ancestor; after adoption through `from` links (T-120's rules).
6. **Views.** Lap History and the board show nested branches under their parent (tree), with their states.

**Done when**
- e2e with real git worktrees: B1 from main, B2 from B1; (a) merge B2 into B1, then B1 into main → main holds B1's and B2's commits once each; (b) merge B2 directly into main while B1 is unmerged → main holds B1's commits up to B2's base, then B2's, `lap status` clean after a clean git merge; then merge B1 into main → only B1's later commits are adopted, none twice; (c) a conflict in B1's part stops the same file for B2; `verify --deep` passes everywhere;
- no git conflict under `.lap/log/` in any of these flows;
- `SPEC.md` describes nested branches and merging into any ancestor; `nested_branch` and `merge_in_branch` removed (or kept only where still meaningful).

Related robustness tickets that also apply to nested branches: T-124, T-125, T-127, T-128.

item.title: A branch folder's identity files never travel through git
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed, design gap).** `.lap/lineage` and `.lap/parent` are machine-local, but lap does nothing to keep them out of git: `lap init` writes no ignore rules, and `cli/lap-cli/README.md:195-202` offers "track it or ignore `.lap/`".

**Repro:** a repo that `git add -A`s without ignoring `.lap/*`; a worktree branch; parent `git merge feat` → clean merge that brings `.lap/lineage`, and the parent silently becomes branch `feat` (`merge_in_branch`, `wrong_branch` on main).

**Fix** (folded in from the review comment):
1. **The real fix:** `lap init` and `lap branch start` write `.lap/.gitignore` that ignores everything in `.lap/` except `log/` and the `.gitignore` itself — self-contained, no change to the project's `.gitignore`.
2. **Safety net:** refuse to act as a branch when the folder's recorded parent (`.lap/parent`) is this folder itself (compare canonical paths or device + inode, as T-122 does), or when no `branch` record with the lineage's id is in this folder's **own** lineage (as opposed to chunks copied in from elsewhere).

*Not* the check "the branch record opens this folder's chunks": after `git merge` or `lap merge` the parent holds the branch's `<id>.000001.jsonl`, which does open with it, so that check passes in the repro.

**Done when:** the repro above leaves the parent `main` (with the `.gitignore`, and separately with a leaked `lineage`/`parent` pair, caught by the safety net); README's git advice matches.

item.title: verify blames the right chunk at a chunk boundary
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** When the chain breaks at a chunk's first record, `verify` always blames the previous chunk (`cli/lap-cli/src/repo.c:536-556`). That is right when chunk N-1 was truncated or appended to (deliberate since T-104), and wrong for a stray or duplicated chunk N.

**Repro (wrong blame):** a repo in 5 chunks; copy `main.000003.jsonl` to `main.000006.jsonl` → "sealed chunk main.000005.jsonl was modified: hash chain broken at main.000006.jsonl line 1". Chunk 5 is intact; 6 is the stray. Same when only the open chunk's first `prev` is wrong. (Readers also silently follow the stray chunk — `log` shows L12 as head.)

**Fix** (folded in from the review comment) — the boundary alone cannot tell which side changed, so use what the chunks show:
- N's first `prev` matches a record inside N-1 that is not its last → N-1 was appended to: blame N-1;
- N-1's last hash is another chunk's first `prev` (a duplicate or stray N) → blame N;
- otherwise name both: "main.000006.jsonl does not continue main.000005.jsonl".

"Writers refuse a broken chain" is **not** here: it is T-131's fix (one implementation, one ticket).

**Done when:** e2e for a stray chunk (blames N), a sealed chunk appended to (blames N-1), a truncated sealed chunk, and a wrong first `prev` with no other clue (names both).

item.title: A torn line in a sealed chunk: readers and writers agree, and nothing builds on a broken history
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** Readers look for a torn tail at the end of the whole history stream (`cli/lap-cli/src/rec.c:320-326`); the writer repairs only the last chunk and returns when it is empty (`hist.c:292-301`).

**Repro:** a repo in 5 chunks; `printf '{"type":"commit","partial' >> .lap/log/main.000005.jsonl`; create an empty `main.000006.jsonl`; `lap verify` → "chain ok … note: torn trailing record ignored … the next commit repairs it" (`cmd_verify.c:~258`); commit an edit → succeeds with "index sync: … expected ':'"; `verify` → "main.000005.jsonl line 5: expected ':'" — the torn bytes now run into chunk 6's first line. Not produced by lap itself (seal and merge repair first); it comes from git or copying.

**Related:** cutting 30 bytes off a sealed chunk makes `verify` report a parse error rather than "sealed chunk … was modified", and `commit` still succeeds on the unreadable history, only warning that the index sync failed (`idx.c:334`).

**Fix:**
- a torn tail outside the open chunk is damage, not a crash: readers report it, naming the chunk;
- **writers refuse to append on any history that does not read cleanly or whose chain is broken** — this ticket owns that rule for every case (torn sealed chunk, truncated chunk, stray chunk, wrong `prev`); T-139 only fixes which chunk `verify` names.

**Done when:** e2e for both repros and for a broken chain at a chunk boundary: `verify` reports the damage, `commit` refuses, nothing is written.

item.title: Temporary files never land in .lap/log, and old leftovers are cleaned up
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** An interrupted conversion leaves `.tmp.<pid>` files in `.lap/log/` that nothing removes; git commits them if the project tracks `.lap/log/`.

**Fix** (folded in from the review comment):
1. **Keep temp files out of `.lap/log/`:** write them in `.lap/` (same filesystem, so the rename stays atomic) and rename into `log/`. git never sees them and readers never have to skip them. T-132's temp-directory conversion does this for the conversion; `plat_write_file_atomic` for new chunks and seals follows the same rule.
2. **Cleanup only for leftovers from older versions:** a writer holds the repository lock, so any `*.tmp.*` it finds in `.lap/log/` under the lock is a leftover and is removed. **No pid check** — `.lap/log/` travels between machines through git, so a pid means nothing here.

**Done when:** no lap command creates a temp file inside `.lap/log/` (e2e interrupts each writer and checks); a leftover temp file there disappears on the next writing command and is never read as a chunk.

item.title: coboard never uses a branch's stale board copy when the parent moved
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** If the parent folder moves, `.lap/parent` goes stale and `locateBoard` falls back to the branch's own `.coboard/` copy (`via: "found"`, `packages/coboard/src/store.ts:96-100`): writes start a second board that git would later have to merge, and reads show the board as of the branch's git base — old statuses, tickets created since missing.

**Fix** (folded in from the review comment): when this folder is a lap branch and its recorded parent's board cannot be found, **both reads and writes** fail with one message naming the stale path and the ways to fix it (`lap branch move` in the parent, or `COBOARD_DIR`) — never a silent fallback to the copy.

**Done when:** tests: a branch folder with a stale `.lap/parent` refuses a read (`board_list`, `board_get`) and a write (`board_create`, `board_update`) with that message; with `COBOARD_DIR` set, both work.

item.title: lap merge adopts the branch history already in this folder, so .lap/log never conflicts in git

author: claude
body: Decision (user, 2026-09-27): `lap merge` adopts the branch history already present in this folder and reads the branch folder only for what is missing; it never overwrites a branch chunk that is already here. The merge driver is not used (git-only, and needs per-clone configuration that cannot be committed). The description is now the implementation ticket.

item.title: READMEs describe lap as it is: branches, merge, chunks, stat cache, line endings, Windows

author: claude
body:
**One case the rule doesn't cover: `lap merge` before `git merge` in a git repository.** No branch chunk is here yet, so the rule reads the branch folder and writes its chunks, the same path as a plain copy. That brings back both problems this ticket fixes:
- history runs ahead of the files: `lap status` shows the branch's work reversed;
- the next `git merge` brings git's version of those same chunk files, and git conflicts with the ones lap wrote.

Suggestion: when this folder is a git work tree (a `.git` directory or file found at or above the root) and a branch chunk isn't here, `lap merge` refuses with `git_merge_first` ("run git merge <branch> first") instead of copying. `--from-folder` (or a similar flag) forces the plain-copy path. Plain folders keep today's behaviour.

This would add one line to the Done when: e2e, `lap merge` before `git merge` in a worktree is refused, and nothing is written.

item.title: Views: quality of life
item.description: Small improvements to the Board, Lap History and review views that the user asks for while using them day to day. Each ticket is independent and small.

item.title: Board sidebar: the filter bar's padding is 6px 4px 4px
item.description:
The Board sidebar's filter bar (`.sb-filter`, `packages/coboard-vscode/assets/board.css:327-330`) has `padding: 6px 8px 4px`. The user wants `padding: 6px 4px 4px` — the right side's 8px becomes 4px, top and bottom unchanged.

item.title: Lap History: a session row shows its ticket first, the session id and count at the far end
item.description:
**Why.** Agents talk about ticket ids, so the user scans Lap History for them. Today a session row reads `S3  T-1: declare time() on Windows    6 commits` (`packages/lap-vscode/webview/history.tsx:346-352`: `lh-id` = session id, `lh-title` = the purpose's first line, `lh-desc` = count and "active").

**Wanted** (as understood — confirm with the user if in doubt):

```
T-1  declare time() on Windows                 S3 · 6 commits · active
```

- **First:** the session's ticket, from its meta (`ticket`), in the id style. Sessions without a ticket show their session id there as today.
- **Then:** the title — the purpose's first line, with a leading `T-<n>: ` prefix removed when it repeats the ticket already shown.
- **At the far end:** the session id (branch-qualified in a branch folder, e.g. `feat/S3`), the commit count, and "active".
- The tooltip keeps the full purpose, the session id and the times; the filter keeps matching the session id, the ticket and the purpose.

**Done when:** unit tests for the row model (with a ticket, without one, a purpose that repeats the ticket, one that does not, a branch session); rendered in light and dark themes.

item.title: Review timeline: edits open beside the review, one group, a new tab per click
item.description:
**Today.** Clicking an edit in a session's review timeline opens its diff (`showEdit`, `packages/coboard-vscode/src/extension.ts:380-392`) with `vscode.diff` and `preview: true`, in the active editor group — it covers the review tab, and each click replaces the previous diff.

**Wanted:** the review and the diffs side by side.
- **First click:** open the diff in an editor group **to the right of the review** (`ViewColumn.Beside` relative to the review panel's column), creating that group if there is none.
- **Next clicks:** open in **that same right-hand group**, each as a **new tab** (`preview: false`), so several edits can be kept open next to the review. Never a third column; never the review's own group.
- If the user closed the right-hand group or moved the review, the next click again opens beside the review.
- Clicking an edit whose diff is already open in that group focuses its tab instead of opening a duplicate.
- The review panel keeps focus behaviour sensible: the diff is shown without stealing the review's scroll position (use `preserveFocus` where it helps).

**Done when:** tested in the Extension Development Host: first click opens beside, the second adds a tab in the same group, re-clicking focuses the existing tab, closing the group and clicking again reopens beside; the existing review tests pass.

item.title: READMEs and skills describe lap as it is: branches, merge, chunks, stat cache, line endings, Windows
lap merge adopts the branch history already in this folder, so .lap/log never conflicts in git

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S121**, git `b4feaa4`.

**What changed**
- `lap merge` builds the branch's history in memory: the parent's chunks up to the base chunk named by the branch record, then the branch's own chunks, each taken from **this folder's copy** when one is here. Adoption runs as far as those copies reach, and lap never rewrites them. So under git, history and code agree, and the next `git merge` finds `.lap/log/` unchanged on this side.
- **Git checkout** (`.git` entry in the branch folder; lap never runs git) with no chunk of the branch here → **`git_merge_first`**, with nothing written, dry run included. `--copy-from-folder` takes the folder's chunks anyway.
- **Plain folder (no git):** missing chunks come from the folder, as before.
- Nothing in the branch folder is sealed or written any more.
- Chunks taken from the folder are written only after every check passes, and a dry run now reads exactly what the real merge would; before, it had a separate path.
- Documentation:
  - SPEC Merging rule 2 and the command entry (flag, error code);
  - a new "Branches and merging" section in lap's README;
  - both skills: the `git merge` → `lap merge` order, what to do on `git_merge_first`, and never `--copy-from-folder` unless the user asks;
  - `lap --help`.

**Decided while building (please check)**
1. **"A chunk that is not here" refuses only when *no* chunk of the branch is here.** When some are here, later chunks missing here are history that git hasn't brought yet, the same as B3 inside chunk 1 in the repro. They wait for the next `git merge`. Refusing whenever any chunk is missing would leave a merge stuck whenever the branch had passed a chunk boundary without git-committing it: `git merge` would bring nothing new, and the refusal would repeat.
2. **In a plain folder (or with `--copy-from-folder`), a copy here that is a byte prefix of the folder's copy is extended.** This is the one exception to "never overwrite". Merge no longer seals the branch's chunk, so without git nothing else would ever bring the rest of a chunk copied while it was open. Under git, a copy here is never touched.
3. Only complete lines are taken from a folder; a line still being written waits for the next merge.

**Tests**
- Unit: 4,144 pass, including 15 new `own_chunks` assertions in five cases:
  - this folder's copy wins;
  - fill extends a prefix and takes missing chunks, cut to complete lines;
  - a diverging copy here is kept;
  - a torn-only chunk ends the list;
  - nothing anywhere gives none.
- e2e: 122 scenarios pass, 2 new:
  - the ticket's steps 1–5: no git conflict, `status` clean after step 4, B2 adopted and B3 not after step 5, `verify --deep` in both folders;
  - merge before `git merge` → `git_merge_first` (JSON and dry run, bytes unchanged), then `--copy-from-folder` adopts without sealing the branch.
  - The old plain-copy scenario was really a git copy (its `cp -R` carried `.git`). It now removes `.git`, and asserts that merge no longer seals.
- coboard: 33 tests pass against the new lap, including the real before/after/partly-merged test.

**Not done here:** T-124's checks were already covered by the new order, since nothing is written before validation, but its e2e cases (tampered chunk, byte-identical folders) remain on T-124.

Later, merging B1 into main carries those adopted commits like any of B1's own.
3. **Merge into main directly.** In main's folder, `lap merge B2`:
   - git's merge of B2 brings B1's work up to B2's base too (B2's git branch contains it), so lap adopts the same: **first B1's commits up to B2's base that main has not adopted yet, then B2's own**, each with its `from` link, in history order, with one merge record per lineage (B1's head advances to B2's base).
   - A later `lap merge B1` into main adopts only B1's commits after what was already adopted, and never adopts B2's commits twice (B2's work reached main directly; if B1 also merged B2, skip the commits whose `from` chain leads to ones already adopted).
   - If adopting B1's part stops a file, B2's commits to that file stop too.
4. **Finding the nested branch.** From main, B2's chunks are found locally (after `git merge`) or through B1's registry (main's registry lists B1; B1's lists B2). `lap branch list` in main shows B2 under B1.
5. **Names and sessions.** `B2/S<n>` resolves from any ancestor; after adoption through `from` links (T-120's rules).
6. **Views.** Lap History and the board show nested branches under their parent (tree), with their states.

**Done when**
- e2e with real git worktrees: B1 from main, B2 from B1; (a) merge B2 into B1, then B1 into main → main holds B1's and B2's commits once each; (b) merge B2 directly into main while B1 is unmerged → main holds B1's commits up to B2's base, then B2's, `lap status` clean after a clean git merge; then merge B1 into main → only B1's later commits are adopted, none twice; (c) a conflict in B1's part stops the same file for B2; `verify --deep` passes everywhere;
- no git conflict under `.lap/log/` in any of these flows;
- `SPEC.md` describes nested branches and merging into any ancestor; `nested_branch` and `merge_in_branch` removed (or kept only where still meaningful).

Related robustness tickets that also apply to nested branches: T-124, T-125, T-127, T-128.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S123**, git `d12b547`.

**What changed**
- **Reading a nested branch (`hist.c`).**
  - A branch's history is its parent's view up to the base chunk, then its own chunks. The branch records are followed one step at a time up to main; that's the new `hist_open_view`, used by `hist_open_lineage`.
  - A chain deeper than 32 steps is refused as a loop, and the error is reported once, not at every level.
  - Every branch in a view is labelled with its own name, so B1's sessions show as `b1/S1` inside B2, not by B1's id.
- **Start.** The `nested_branch` refusal is gone. The branch record's `parent` is the parent folder's lineage, and B2 is registered in B1's registry.
- **Merge (`cmd_merge.c`).** A branch folder merges its own branches. `lap merge` works out a chain: the branch, then each branch it started from, up to the first whose history this folder already holds.
  - It reads one stream: this folder's history up to the outer base chunk, then each branch's own chunks, this folder's copies first (the T-127 rule holds for every branch in the chain).
  - Adoption starts after the latest head this folder took in for any branch in the chain.
  - The chain's commits are placed as one run, so a conflict in B1's part also stops the file for B2.
  - One merge record per branch with anything new. B1's head moves to B2's base, so a later `lap merge b1` takes only what came after.
  - A session adopted before, directly or through a branch that had adopted it (via its `from`), isn't adopted again, and its end isn't written twice.
  - `merge_in_branch` is kept only for merging a branch whose history this folder already holds.
- **Registry.** `branches_load_deep` also reads the registries of listed branches whose folders are still those branches. It's used by merge, `--branch`/`<branch>/S<n>` and `branch list`, and never saved.
  - `branch list` indents nested branches under their parent, with `(from b)`, and adds `via` to the JSON.
  - A nested branch's state is judged against its parent branch's history, where its merges are recorded.
  - The "this folder is branch X of …" line names the parent branch.
- **coboard.**
  - `locateBoard` follows `.lap/parent` up to main's folder, so B2's agents work main's board and not B1's stale copy.
  - A ticket's sessions list each nested branch's session once: a parent branch's session repeated in the child's history is dropped, and so is a session a branch has adopted.
  - A session still only in B2 is labelled `b1 › b2`.
- **Lap History.**
  - `lineageFiles` follows the same chain.
  - `branchAt` is the last branch record, so B2 shows only its own work.
  - The Branches group is a tree: B2 appears under B1 when B1 is opened.
- **Docs:**
  - SPEC: Branches overview, Merging rules 1–5, Registry, Naming sessions, the `branch start`/`branch list` entries, and "Not in this version";
  - the lap skill has a new bullet on branches of branches.

**Tests**
- Unit: 4,206 pass (+33): nested views, cuts, a missing middle base, loops; the deep registry (via, no repeats, stale folder not followed).
- e2e: 127 pass (+4, with real git worktrees):
  - B2 reads B1's history and shows in B1's and main's branch lists;
  - (a) B2 into B1, then B1 into main: each commit once;
  - (b) B2 straight into main: two merge records, `rr b2/S<n>` finds the adopted session, and B1's later work follows exactly once;
  - (c) a conflict in B1's part stops f.txt in both merge records.

  In all four, no git conflict under `.lap/log/`, and `verify --deep` passes.
- coboard 36 (+3), lap-vscode 50 (+2), coboard-vscode 36: all pass.
- Lap History's nested tree was rendered in headless Chrome over a real nested fixture, in light and dark.

**Not verified / notes**
- The board's `b1 › b2` label was only checked by compiling, not rendered.
- The e2e helper passes `--from ../x` instead of an absolute `/var/...` path. Under a symlinked path, branch start's seal fails with `parent_read_only`; that's T-129's bug, and T-129 should cover this.

item.title: Branches of branches: start one, merge it into its parent branch or into main
item.description:
**Decided by the user (2026-09-27): support branches of branches.** A branch can start from a branch folder, and a nested branch can be merged into its parent branch **or into main** (any ancestor). This replaces the `nested_branch` refusal (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_branch.c:187`) introduced in the design-review amendments (T-118).

**Terms.** B1 is a branch of main; B2 a branch of B1, based at a hash in B1's lineage.

**Build**
1. **Start.** `lap branch start [name] --from <B1 folder>` works as from main: B2's history is main up to B1's base, then B1 up to B2's base, then its own. Sealing and registration happen in B1 (its open chunk sealed, B2 in B1's registry).
2. **Merge into the parent branch.** In B1's folder, `lap merge B2` — today refused with `merge_in_branch` — adopts B2 into B1's lineage exactly as a merge into main does (placement, `from` links, sessions with their meta, merge record, per-file stops). Later, merging B1 into main carries those adopted commits like any of B1's own.
3. **Merge into main directly.** In main's folder, `lap merge B2`:
   - git's merge of B2 brings B1's work up to B2's base too (B2's git branch contains it), so lap adopts the same: **first B1's commits up to B2's base that main has not adopted yet, then B2's own**, each with its `from` link, in history order, with one merge record per lineage (B1's head advances to B2's base).
   - A later `lap merge B1` into main adopts only B1's commits after what was already adopted, and never adopts B2's commits twice (B2's work reached main directly; if B1 also merged B2, skip the commits whose `from` chain leads to ones already adopted).
   - If adopting B1's part stops a file, B2's commits to that file stop too.
4. **Finding the nested branch.** From main, B2's chunks are found locally (after `git merge`) or through B1's registry (main's registry lists B1; B1's lists B2). `lap branch list` in main shows B2 under B1.
5. **Names and sessions.** `B2/S<n>` resolves from any ancestor; after adoption through `from` links (T-120's rules).
6. **Views.** Lap History and the board show nested branches under their parent (tree), with their states.

**Done when**
- e2e with real git worktrees: B1 from main, B2 from B1; (a) merge B2 into B1, then B1 into main → main holds B1's and B2's commits once each; (b) merge B2 directly into main while B1 is unmerged → main holds B1's commits up to B2's base, then B2's, `lap status` clean after a clean git merge; then merge B1 into main → only B1's later commits are adopted, none twice; (c) a conflict in B1's part stops the same file for B2; `verify --deep` passes everywhere;
- no git conflict under `.lap/log/` in any of these flows;
- `SPEC.md` describes nested branches and merging into any ancestor; `nested_branch` and `merge_in_branch` removed (or kept only where still meaningful).

Related robustness tickets that also apply to nested branches: T-124, T-125, T-127, T-128.

item.title: lap amend: correct a commit's intent and behavior without rewriting history
item.description:
**Why.** A commit's intent or behavior is sometimes written wrong. Today it is permanent, so corrections end up in later commits' messages (which should describe only their own edit) or in board comments — and whoever reads the commit with `lap show`, `rr` or Lap History sees the wrong text with nothing pointing to the fix. Seen in practice in the E-14 work.

**Decided with the user (2026-09-27): append-only, never a rewrite.** Rewriting a record (even only its message) changes its hash and every hash after it: branches' bases, `from` and `#hash` links, sealed chunks under git and the chain's tamper evidence would all break. Storing a `forward` field in the original record was also considered and dropped: it edits a line already written (often in a sealed chunk), which conflicts in git and breaks append-only crash safety. The forward pointer is derived instead.

**Build**
- `lap amend <commit> (-i "intent" -b "behavior" | -F <file|->)` appends `{"type":"amend","of":"<amended record's hash>","intent","behavior","user","ts","prev"}`. Either field may be kept by repeating it; both are required, as for commits, and the **same message checks** apply.
- **Messages only.** Code is never touched; a wrong edit is fixed by a new commit.
- **Chains.** An amendment can itself be amended (`of` = the amend record's hash). Reading a commit follows the chain to the **latest** amendment. The forward pointer (commit → latest amendment) is **derived**: built in memory, and cached in the index under the cache contract — never written into the log.
- **Hidden, overriding.** `amend` records do not appear as history entries in `log`, `rr`, `search` results or the views; wherever the commit appears, its latest text is shown, marked "amended" (with the count). `show <commit>` also lists the earlier texts, oldest first. `search --msg` matches the latest text (and optionally earlier ones with a flag, if cheap).
- **Scope.** Only commits of **this folder's own lineage** can be amended: a branch cannot amend what it inherited from its parent (records before its base) → refused (e.g. `not_own_commit`). Amending an amend record directly is allowed only for amends of this lineage too.
- **Merge.** `lap merge` carries a branch's amendments to the adopted commits: each amend of a branch commit is appended in the parent as an amend of the adopted counterpart (found through its `from` link), in order; amendments of commits that were not adopted (stopped files) stay in the branch.
- **Views.** Lap History and the board review show the latest text with an "amended" marker; the earlier texts on demand.
- **Skills.** The lap skill and the tickets skill say: correct a wrong intent or behavior with `lap amend`, not in later commits' messages or board comments.

**Done when**
- e2e: amend, amend again, amend the amendment → `show`/`log`/`rr` show the latest text, `show` lists the earlier ones, no `amend` entry in `log`/`rr`; message checks refuse a weak amendment; amending an inherited commit from a branch is refused; `verify --deep` passes and no existing byte of the log changed (compare before/after); deleting the index changes nothing but speed;
- e2e: a branch amends one of its commits, `git merge` + `lap merge` → the adopted commit shows the amended text on the parent;
- views: unit tests for the latest-text model; rendered once;
- `SPEC.md` (record type, command, scope, merge), lap's README and both skills document it.

Best built after M-14's merge work (T-124, T-125, T-127, T-157), which changes `lap merge`.

- e2e: amend a commit, amend it again → `show`/`log`/`rr` show the latest text, `show` lists the earlier ones, no `amend` entry in `log`/`rr`; message checks refuse a weak amendment; amending an inherited commit from a branch is refused; `verify --deep` passes and no existing byte of the log changed (compare before/after); deleting the index changes nothing but speed;
