item.title: Converting an old log keeps git seeing the history: conversion writes .lap/.gitignore
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** A repository whose root `.gitignore` uses the pattern the docs gave before chunks —

```
.lap/*
!.lap/log.jsonl
```

— (typec has it, line 54; this repo had it until T-105) loses its history from git at conversion:

```
lap commit a.txt …   → lap: moved .lap/log.jsonl into 1 chunk in .lap/log/
git status --short   →  D .lap/log.jsonl       (the chunks do not appear)
git check-ignore -v .lap/log/main.000001.jsonl   → .gitignore:1:.lap/*
```

Committing that deletes the history from git and never adds the chunks. Nothing warns. SPEC says "git sees one deleted file and some new ones".

**Cause.** `.lap/.gitignore` is written only by `lap init` and `branch start` (`cmd_branch.c:327`, and `:332` in the parent), never when an older repository is opened or converted (`hist.c:542-674`, called from `repo.c:436-442`).

**Fix.** The conversion writes lap's standard `.lap/.gitignore` (`/*`, `!/.gitignore`, `!/log/`) when there is none. A root `.lap/*` ignores `.lap`'s children, not `.lap` itself, so git reads that file and its `!/log/` re-includes the chunks (the audit tested it: `.lap/log/` then shows as untracked). lap never runs git, so it does not check what git ignores; the conversion message says to commit `.lap/.gitignore` and `.lap/log/` with the removal of `log.jsonl`. The README's upgrade note says the same.

**Done when:** e2e: a repo with the old root pattern converts, `.lap/.gitignore` exists, and `git status` (run by the test, not lap) lists `.lap/.gitignore` and `.lap/log/`; an existing `.lap/.gitignore` is left as it is; unit test for the write-only-when-absent rule.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S173, git a45f768.

**What changed**
- New `repo_convert_legacy` (repo.c). It wraps `hist_convert_legacy` and is what a writer's open now calls. When a conversion actually happened, it writes lap's standard `.lap/.gitignore` (`/*`, `!/.gitignore`, `!/log/`) through the existing `repo_write_gitignore`, which keeps a file that is already there. It then prints `lap: commit .lap/.gitignore and .lap/log/ to git with the removal of .lap/log.jsonl`. A failed .gitignore write only warns; the conversion itself has already succeeded.
- SPEC (the lineage/.gitignore paragraph) and a new README "Upgrading from the single-file log" note say the same. lap still never runs git.

**Tests**: unit 4456 passed. The new repo_convert_legacy test covers: no conversion writes no .gitignore; a conversion writes it when absent; a conversion keeps an existing one. e2e 156 passed, 0 failed. The new scenario is a git repo with the old root `.lap/*` / `!.lap/log.jsonl` pattern and an old-shaped log committed to git. The first lap write prints the hint and writes `.lap/.gitignore`. The test's own `git status --untracked-files=all` then lists `?? .lap/.gitignore`, `?? .lap/log/main.000001.jsonl` and ` D .lap/log.jsonl`. A copy with its own `.lap/.gitignore` keeps it unchanged.

Checked against the pre-change repo.c: that scenario fails there, and git shows only ` D .lap/log.jsonl`, as the ticket's repro said.

item.title: eggzibit: Artifacts renamed, so Claude never confuses them with its own artifacts
item.description:
Claude has its own "artifacts" (claude.ai pages published with its `Artifact` tool), and procode's local pages share the noun: in one session an agent sees both tools and both skills, and has to guess which is meant. procode's pages become **eggzibit** (the user's name, 2026-09-28; a pun on exhibit, carried by an egg icon).

Decided with the user on 2026-09-28: the name is used everywhere (package, MCP server and tools, store folder, skill, view, spec, docs), never as a brand over plain "artifact" tool names; the MCP server's instructions say in one line that these are local pages, not claude.ai artifacts. Icon options were drawn in the session (ten cracked eggs); the choice is in the ticket.

item.title: A branch name is unique across nested branches, as seen from main
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced, git worktrees).** From main start `b1` and a top-level `x`; from b1's folder start a nested branch also named `x`. It is accepted.

```
main: lap branch list
b1  active …/b1
x   active …/x
  x active …/xn  (from b1)
```

From main, `lap log --branch x` reads the top-level x silently (a commit made in the nested one is not there; it is readable only by its id). The audit also saw `rr x/S1` and `merge x --dry-run` take the top-level one, and coboard's `ticketSessions` run `--branch x` for both rows, reading the same branch twice.

SPEC §Naming sessions: "a branch name names one branch for good", and readers resolve nested names from main.

**Cause.** The `name_taken` check (`cmd_branch.c:257-280`) sees only the parent branch's registry, chunks and merge records.

**Fix.** At start, check the name against every branch main can see: walk up to the top folder through `.lap/parent`, then its registry and down nested registries (as readers do), plus chunk-only and merged names. Where two already share a name (made before the fix), readers refuse with `ambiguous_branch` listing the ids, rather than picking one.

**Done when:** e2e: the nested `x` is refused with `name_taken`; a pre-existing duplicate gives `ambiguous_branch` for `log --branch x`; coboard reads each branch by id when names repeat; unit tests for the name walk.

item.title: Rename Artifacts to eggzibit everywhere, with a whole egg while empty and a hatched one once a page exists
lap log shows each commit's intent and behavior, with --intent-only and --behavior-only
item.description:
**Why.** An agent reviewing history had to read the chunk files by hand: "lap log prints the intent, not the behavior, so I'll check the chunk file instead." The behavior is half of every commit's message, and the text log hides it.

**Today (checked):**
```
$ lap log -n 1
L7     795ad3e 2026-09-28 11:19:44  -      edit     g.txt  line 2 (insertion)
       g edit for the test                     ← intent only
```
`lap log --json` carries both (`intent`, `behavior`); `lap show` prints both; `lap search` prints both. SPEC:876-878 describes the log line as "… intent summary".

**Change.**
- Text `lap log` prints both under each commit line, as `lap show` labels them, one line each (first line of each text, as today's summary):
  ```
  L7     795ad3e 2026-09-28 11:19:44  -      edit     g.txt  line 2 (insertion)
         intent:   g edit for the test
         behavior: the test file changes: g edit
  ```
- `--intent-only` and `--behavior-only` print just that one (the intent line then looks as it does today, without the label); both together → `bad_args`. `--json` unchanged (always both).
- An amended commit shows its latest texts, as today.
- SPEC `lap log`, `lap --help`, the lap skill (where it tells agents how to read history) and the lap-cli README updated.

**Done when:** e2e for the default, `--intent-only`, `--behavior-only`, both flags together (`bad_args`), and an amended commit; unit test for the formatting.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S174, git 9ddfb92.

**What changed**
- `lap branch start` checks the name with the new `branch_name_used(from, name)`. Starting at the parent folder, it goes up through `.lap/parent` while the folder is still a branch (at most 32 levels). In each folder it looks at the deep registry (nested branches included), branch chunks, merge record names, and the folder's own branch name. A hit is `name_taken`, with a message that names the branch and the folder.
- `branch_find` is now built on `branch_find_all`. An id names exactly one branch. A name returns every distinct id that carries it in the registry or in chunk branch records. When several share the name, `branch_find` returns NULL and lists the ids. `--branch` readers (log/show/rr, and `x/S1` refs through `session_resolve`) and `lap merge` then fail with `ambiguous_branch: x names more than one branch (id1, id2): name it by its id`.
- coboard `ticketSessions`: a branch whose name repeats in `lap branch list` is named by its id, both for the `--branch` query and as the session's `branch` (and `via`). The later commits/review calls therefore read the right one.
- SPEC: the naming rules, the upward walk, and `ambiguous_branch`.

**Tests**
- lap unit: 4473 passed. New tests cover `branch_find_all`/`branch_find` on a shared name and on an id, and `branch_name_used` from a nested folder up to the top, including a folder that is no longer a branch (the walk stops there).
- e2e: 157 passed. The new scenario: git worktrees; top-level `x` started from main; a nested `x` from b's folder is `name_taken` and leaves no lineage; a nested `y` is renamed to `x` in b's registry to simulate a duplicate made before this fix. After that, `log --branch x` gives `ambiguous_branch`, `merge x --dry-run` fails, and `log --branch <id>` reads.

item.title: A branch name is unique across nested branches, as seen from main
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced, git worktrees).** From main start `b1` and a top-level `x`; from b1's folder start a nested branch also named `x`. It is accepted.

```
main: lap branch list
b1  active …/b1
x   active …/x
  x active …/xn  (from b1)
```

From main, `lap log --branch x` reads the top-level x silently (a commit made in the nested one is not there; it is readable only by its id). The audit also saw `rr x/S1` and `merge x --dry-run` take the top-level one, and coboard's `ticketSessions` run `--branch x` for both rows, reading the same branch twice.

SPEC §Naming sessions: "a branch name names one branch for good", and readers resolve nested names from main.

**Cause.** The `name_taken` check (`cmd_branch.c:257-280`) sees only the parent branch's registry, chunks and merge records.

**Fix.** At start, check the name against every branch main can see: walk up to the top folder through `.lap/parent`, then its registry and down nested registries (as readers do), plus chunk-only and merged names. Where two already share a name (made before the fix), readers refuse with `ambiguous_branch` listing the ids, rather than picking one.

**Done when:** e2e: the nested `x` is refused with `name_taken`; a pre-existing duplicate gives `ambiguous_branch` for `log --branch x`; coboard reads each branch by id when names repeat; unit tests for the name walk.

item.title: A plain copy of a branch folder is not that branch: two folders never write one lineage
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** A `cp -R` of a branch folder keeps `.lap/lineage` and `.lap/parent`, so the copy *is* that branch:

```
cp -R main b1; cd b1; lap branch start b1 --from ../main
cp -R b1 x2; cd x2
lap branch start x --from ../b1   → error: … is already branch d02033661320; a folder starts one branch
lap commit a.txt … --branch b1    → [L3 …] recorded, into d02033661320.000001.jsonl — the same chunk b1 writes
```

Two folders then append to one lineage's open chunk: diverging copies of the same file name, a git conflict (or a broken chain) as soon as both reach git. And the SPEC's "a branch of a branch starts from a branch folder the same way" (SPEC:352) fails in copy mode with no way out but deleting `.lap/lineage` by hand.

**Cause.** `cmd_branch.c:151` trusts `.lap/lineage`. A copied registry is detected and dropped (`:346-353`), a copied lineage is not, though the parent's registry puts that branch at another path.

**Fix.** A folder whose `.lap/lineage` names a branch that its parent's registry places at a different, existing folder is a copy: `branch start` treats it as a folder copied from that branch (its lineage file dropped, like the registry), and writers refuse to record there with a clear code (e.g. `copied_branch`) naming both folders.

**Done when:** e2e: nested branch start from a copy succeeds; a commit in an un-started copy is refused and writes nothing; a moved branch (old path gone, `branch move` not run yet) is still that branch; unit tests for the copy decision.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S175, git 1992470.

**What changed**
- New `branches_copy_of(lapdir, root, lineage, &original)` (branches.c) decides whether a folder is a copy. It reads the folder's `.lap/parent` and that parent's registry. If the registry places this lineage in *another* folder (compared by path and by `plat_same_file`) that exists and whose `.lap/lineage` is still that id, the folder is a copy of that branch. If the registered folder is this one, or is gone or no longer that branch (a move not yet told with `branch move`), the folder is the branch.
- `repo_open_at` for writers: in a copy it fails with the new code `copied_branch` before anything is written. The message names both folders and says to start a branch there, or record in the original.
- `lap branch start` in a copy prints a note and goes ahead instead of `already_branch`. The start's final lineage/parent writes replace the copied ones. A copied registry was already dropped.
- SPEC: a "plain copy of a branch folder" paragraph under the start, and the error list.

**Tests**: unit 4481 passed. New copy-decision cases: a copy; the branch itself; an unregistered lineage; a branch moved away; no `.lap/parent`. e2e 158 passed. The new scenario runs in copy mode without git. A commit in `cp -R b1 x2` is `copied_branch` and the chunks are byte-identical after it. `branch start x --from ../cp1-b1` then succeeds with a new lineage, and commits in both x and b1 work. After `mv cp1-b1 cp1-b1moved`, a commit there still records as b1, and verify says chain ok.

Checked against the pre-change repo.c/cmd_branch.c: the scenario fails there (the commit lands in b1's chunk, and the start is `already_branch`).

item.title: A lineage leaked through git is ignored in any folder that is not that branch, not only its parent
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** T-130 ignores a leaked `.lap/lineage` only in the folder its `.lap/parent` names. A clone of that folder trusts it:

```
wt (branch feat of main): git add -f .lap/lineage .lap/parent; git commit
main: git merge feat     → main keeps main, with the T-130 note (as designed)
git clone main clone; cd clone
lap session start "…" --branch main   → error: this folder (…/clone) records to feat, not main
```

No note; the clone would write feat's lineage. It needs a forced `git add -f` past `.lap/.gitignore`, or a repo that tracked `.lap/` before T-130 — hence medium, not high.

**Cause.** `hist.c:700-727` fires only when `.lap/parent` resolves to this very folder.

**Fix.** Also ignore (with the same note) a lineage whose `.lap/parent`'s registry does not list this folder for it — a clone, a copy moved elsewhere — and a lineage whose parent folder is missing while this folder is a git checkout of the parent's history. Keep a moved branch working (`branch move` exists for it).

**Done when:** e2e: the clone repro records to main with the note; a real branch folder and a moved-then-`branch move`d one are unaffected; unit test for the decision table.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S176, git c258c8b.

**What changed.** `hist_folder_lineage` now asks the new `hist_lineage_leak(lapdir, lineage)`. If that gives a reason, the folder is main, and the once-a-command note names the reason. The decision table:

| `.lap/parent` | parent's `.lap/lineage` | parent's registry for the id | → |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | | | branch |
| this folder | | | **main** (T-130, unchanged) |
| exists | not this id | any | branch (also T-177's plain copy) |
| exists | **same id** | this folder | branch |
| exists | same id | another folder that is still it | **main** (a checkout of the parent's history, e.g. a clone) |
| exists | same id | another folder no longer it (moved) | branch |
| exists | same id | not listed | **main** |
| gone | | | branch, unless its branch record's parent is main and `main.<base_chunk+1>` exists here → **main** |

**Decision:** the ticket suggested making a folder main whenever the parent's registry doesn't list it. I did not do that, because it would contradict T-177: a `cp -R` of a branch folder would become main instead of being refused with `copied_branch`. It would also break a live branch after `lap branch forget`. The rule is keyed on the parent *carrying the same lineage file*, which only happens when it came through git. So a real branch keeps working even when its parent holds the leak. A clone of a branch folder itself (not of its parent) is T-177's copy: writers refuse with `copied_branch`.

**Tests**: unit 4492 passed (a test for every row of the table). e2e 159 passed.
- The T-130 scenario now forces the leak into git (`git add -f`) and clones the parent. The clone prints "this folder is main", and a session start plus commit with `--branch main` succeed there. The real branch folder still commits as b, with no note.
- A new scenario: a branch folder moved away while its parent carries the leak records as b before `branch move` and after it.

Checked against the pre-change hist.c: the clone checks fail there.

item.title: coboard's session start follows lap on a leaked lineage instead of passing it as --branch
item.description:
**Verified (code and lap run).** `branchArgs` (`packages/coboard/src/lap.ts:333-343`) returns `--branch <the id in .lap/lineage>` whenever the file exists. In a main folder where a lineage leaked through git (the T-130 case, which lap ignores with a note), that is `--branch 426557a1eb8f`, and lap answers:

```
error: this folder (…/main) records to main, not 426557a1eb8f: … pass --branch main
```

So the VS Code "start session" for a ticket fails in exactly the folder lap keeps as main.

**Fix.** Do not second-guess lap: ask it which line this folder records to (e.g. `lap session current --json` or `lap branch list --json` already carry it; add a small field if needed) and pass that, or pass nothing and let `LAP_BRANCH`-less lap decide where it can.

**Done when:** coboard test: in a leaked-lineage main folder, `startSession` succeeds on main; in a real branch folder it records to the branch; in a folder with branches it passes `--branch main`.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S177, git f4f1699.

- A `self` means this folder is a branch, and coboard passes `--branch <self.id>`.
- No self, but some branches listed: `--branch main`.
- No branches, or lap refuses or is too old: nothing.
- `LAP_BRANCH` set: still nothing.

A leaked lineage is exactly the case where lap's `self` is null (T-130 and T-178), so coboard follows lap's decision there. `startSession` awaits it. No new lap field was needed.

**Tests**: coboard 43 passed. The old file-fixture `branchArgs` test in locate.test.ts is removed; it could not tell a leak from a branch. The new lap-backed test in sessions.test.ts covers:
- no branches: no args, and the session starts;
- a branch folder: `--branch <id>`, and the session ref is `feat/S…`;
- the parent with branches: `--branch main`;
- the parent after feat's lineage and parent files were copied into it: still `--branch main`, and the session starts as a main `S…`;
- `LAP_BRANCH` set: no args.

It fails against the old lap.ts. The coboard-vscode type check passes. Not run: the VS Code host tests, or a click on "Start lap Session" in the extension itself.

item.title: lap status and commit report unreadable files and folders, never as deleted or clean
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** The class of bug T-167 fixed for branch start, still in status and commit:

```
commit d/q.txt; chmod 000 d
lap status                         →  deleted   d/q.txt
lap commit d/q.txt … --dry-run     →  would record: delete d/q.txt
(the audit: branch start lists d/q.txt as "changed", not unreadable)

echo 11 >> a.txt; chmod 000 a.txt
lap status                         →  clean: working tree matches the last commit
```

A real commit would record the deletion of a file that is there.

**Cause.** `cmd_common.c:418` takes `plat_is_file` false (EACCES) as "no file"; `cmd_status.c:217-218` skips an unreadable file silently; `platform.c:710` skips an unreadable directory quietly.

**Fix.** Tell "absent" from "cannot read" (stat vs open/opendir errors). Status lists `unreadable <path>`; commit refuses such a file with `unreadable`; an unreadable directory makes its tracked files unreadable, not deleted.

**Done when:** e2e for both repros (status lists them as unreadable, commit refuses, nothing recorded); unit tests for the platform walk reporting unreadable directories.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S178, git 3280ef7.

**What changed**
- New `plat_is_unreachable(path)`: the path's stat fails for a reason other than its absence (POSIX `lstat` errno other than ENOENT/ENOTDIR; Windows attributes error other than not-found). Such a path is neither there nor gone.
- New `plat_walk_report(...)`: `plat_walk` plus the list of folders that could not be opened for a reason other than absence. `plat_walk` keeps the old quiet skip for every other caller.
- `file_diff_load`: a missing regular file whose path is unreachable is no longer "deleted". It fails with `FileDiff.unreadable` set, and so does a file that exists but cannot be read.
- `lap status`: such files show as `unreadable  <path>  (cannot be read: fix its permissions)` (JSON state `unreadable`), and each folder the walk could not open is listed as `unreadable  d/`. Both count as pending, so status is never `clean` over them.
- `lap commit` (and `--dry-run`) of such a file fails with the error code `unreadable` (previously `read_failed`, or a recorded delete).
- Branch start gets the same fix for free: `pending_against` uses `file_diff_load`, so the audit's "d/q.txt listed as changed" is now `unreadable`.
- SPEC: `lap status` and `lap commit`.

**Tests**: unit 4505 passed. New tests: `plat_is_unreachable` on missing, nested-missing and existing paths; `plat_walk_report` with all folders open, and with one at mode 000 (reported as `other`, its file not walked, the path inside unreachable; skipped as root). e2e 160 passed. The new scenario runs both repros: `chmod 000 d` and a changed `a.txt` at mode 000. Status lists them as unreadable, commits are `unreadable`, the chunks are byte-identical, and after `chmod 644` a.txt shows as modified. It is skipped when run as root.

Checked against the pre-change code: 7 checks fail there, including "a refused commit wrote history". The old code really recorded the deletion of `d/q.txt`. Not verified: the Windows branches (no Windows run).

item.title: lap merge keeps a change both sides made when the branch later undid its copy
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** git merges cleanly, nothing stops, yet lap's result differs from git's:

```
b:    insert X after line 5 (commit); delete X (commit)
main: insert the same X after line 5 (commit)
git merge b     → clean, X kept (from base to b nothing changed)
lap merge b     → adopted 1 of 2 commits (L4); already done here: #… (this folder made the same change)
lap status      → modified a.txt [1] line 6 (insertion)
```

lap takes the insertion as already done, then places the branch's deletion on main's X; the shadow lacks X, the file has it.

**Cause.** `adopt.c:103-121` marks the first commit already done and sets the parent's change as used up (`ch[hit].len = -1`), so the region becomes common ground and the revert at `125-167` no longer touches a parent change.

**Decision (user, 2026-09-28): the undoing commit stops the file.** An "already done" commit leaves the parent's change counted: a later branch commit that overlaps or touches that region is a conflict, like any other overlap. Not chosen: adopting commits without applying them — it breaks "replaying the history rebuilds each file" (`verify --deep`) and would be a new kind of record meaning nothing.

With the stop, the reverting commit is not adopted; the shadow keeps main's X, which is git's result, and status is clean. Later branch commits to that file are left to commit by hand (the existing stop behaviour). No new concept, record or flag: a few lines in `adopt.c`. SPEC §Merging says that a change already done still counts as the parent's for the commits after it.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro reports `stopped: a.txt at #<the delete>`, status clean, `verify --deep` ok; adopt unit test for the case, and T-158's tests still green.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S179, git e459633. This implements the recorded decision: the undoing commit stops the file.

**What changed (adopt.c, a few lines).** When a commit is already done (the single identical commit, or the end of a multi-step run from T-173), the parent's change is no longer marked used up (`len = -1`). It stays in the list at the branch's current size with delta 0. Later commits get no extra offset from it, and a later commit that overlaps or touches it is "it overlaps or touches a change the parent made", so the file stops. The identical-insertion path now skips shifting that change's own start (it used to be harmless because the change was dropped). Files created or deleted identically on both sides stay whole-file common ground, unchanged. adopt.h and SPEC merge rule 3 now say an already-done change still counts as the parent's, and the parent's text is kept, as `git merge` keeps it.

**Tests**: unit 4515 passed, including the T-158 and T-173 adopt tests. The new adopt test: undoing an already-done insertion stops the file (placed 1, result = the parent's), undoing after a two-step change stops too, and a commit clear of the change (one unchanged line between) still carries on. e2e 161 passed. The new scenario is the ticket's repro (insert X then remove it on b, the same X on main): git keeps X, and `lap merge b` reports `stopped: f.txt at #<the removal>`; status is clean and `verify --deep` shows 0 mismatches.

Checked against the pre-change adopt.c: 6 of the new unit asserts fail there, and the e2e fails (no stop, status not clean), as the ticket reports.

item.title: lap merge refuses a branch history holding records of a newer type, and verify names them in branches
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** T-164's rule — a writer never builds on records it does not understand — is not applied to the branch history `lap merge` reads:

```
b: commit; append a validly chained {"type":"annotate",…} (a newer lap's record)
b: lap commit …  → error: this history holds 1 record of a type this lap does not know … (correct)
git commit; main: git merge b; lap merge b
→ merged branch b (…): adopted 1 of 1 commit (L3), rc 0, no notice
main: lap verify → "chain ok: 5 records" / "branch b: chain ok: 6 records" — the unknown record not mentioned
```

The merge record's `head` is the unknown record, so it is never looked at again.

**Cause.** `cmd_merge.c:333` parses the branch stream, `685-686` skip unknown types, `713` takes the head. `cmd_verify.c`'s branch pass does not count unknown records; branch JSON has no `unknown_records`.

**Fix.** `lap merge` (and `--dry-run`) refuses with `newer_history` when the branch part it would adopt holds unknown records; `verify` reports them per branch (text note and `unknown_records` in each branch's JSON).

**Done when:** e2e: the repro refuses and writes nothing; verify names the record under branch b; unit test for the branch-part scan.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S180, git a7fed88.

**What changed**
- New `merge_unknown_records(log, lof, &type)` (cmd_merge.c) counts records of type `REC_UNKNOWN` among the records the chain's branches own (`lof >= 0`); this folder's own part is its writers' concern. `lap merge` and `--dry-run` call it right after parsing the branch stream, before any placement. If it finds any, the merge fails with `newer_history: branch b's history holds 1 record of a type this lap does not know ("annotate"): a newer lap wrote it. Update lap before merging it (reading still works)`, and nothing is written.
- `lap verify`: the per-branch pass carries the scan's unknown count. Each branch's JSON entry gets `unknown_records` and `unknown_type`, and the text adds `note: branch b holds 1 record … not interpreted, and lap merge refuses it`.
- SPEC §Records of a newer type: verify reports them per branch, and `lap merge` refuses.

**Tests**: unit 4520 passed. The new `merge_unknown_records` test covers: none; an unknown record in this folder's part is not counted; two in the branch part give 2 and the first one's type. e2e 162 passed. The new scenario appends a validly chained `annotate` record to branch b's open chunk. After git merge, `lap merge b --dry-run --json` gives `newer_history`, `lap merge b` names the record, and the parent's chunks are byte-identical. `verify` prints the note under b, and its JSON has `unknown_records:1, unknown_type:"annotate"` on b's entry.

Checked against the pre-change cmd_merge.c/cmd_verify.c: all 5 checks fail there, and the old merge adopted and wrote history. One caveat: a branch's verify count covers its whole view, which includes the parent part up to its base. An unknown record in this folder's history from before the base would therefore also show under the branch.

```
→ merged branch b (…): adopted 1 of 1 commit (L3), rc 0, no notice
main: lap verify → "chain ok: 5 records" / "branch b: chain ok: 6 records" — the unknown record not mentioned
```

The merge record's `head` is the unknown record, so it is never looked at again.

**Cause.** `cmd_merge.c:333` parses the branch stream, `685-686` skip unknown types, `713` takes the head. `cmd_verify.c`'s branch pass does not count unknown records; branch JSON has no `unknown_records`.

item.title: lap status with only log/ (a fresh clone) sees what it sees with caches
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** T-136 holds only while the shadow store is there. With `.lap/` holding only `log/` — exactly what a `git clone` gives — status misses deletions and edits of files ignored after they were recorded:

```
commit a.txt, b.txt, ig/c.txt; rm b.txt; add ig/ to .lapignore; edit ig/c.txt; commit .lapignore
lap status                      → deleted b.txt; modified ig/c.txt
(.lap/index moved away)         → same (T-136 works)
(.lap/shadow moved away too)    → clean: working tree matches the last commit
```

On a typec clone with every cache removed, status omits `modified .coboard/log.jsonl` (committed at L52, ignored later). The cache contract (SPEC:59-62): deleting any cache changes speed only.

**Cause.** `cmd_status.c:138-145`: with no index, the tracked set comes from walking `.lap/shadow`, never from the log.

**Fix.** When the index is missing or not ready, rebuild it (or derive the tracked set from the log) before status compares — status already reads the log to heal state. A missing shadow for a tracked file is rebuilt from the history.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro gives the same output in all three states and in a fresh `git clone`; the "byte-identical with and without caches" test covers status with only `log/`.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S181, git 2b5ae2d.

**What changed.** Without a ready index, `lap status` no longer walks `.lap/shadow` to find tracked files. It loads the history and takes every file whose last commit is not a delete: the new `log_tracked_files`, which gives exactly the set the index lists. The same join then gives each walked file its place and adds the tracked files the walk did not see: deleted ones, and ones ignored since they were recorded. A missing shadow copy was already rebuilt from the history (`shadow_from_log`), so nothing else was needed there. A history status cannot read is now `log_unreadable`. I did not choose to rebuild the index in status: status is a reader, and deriving the set from the log gives the same answer without writing. SPEC `lap status` says the output is the same with every cache or none.

**Tests**: unit 4526 passed. The new `log_tracked_files` test covers: a later delete untracks a file, a later edit keeps it, and session records are not files. e2e 163 passed.
- The existing "tracked before it was ignored … with and without caches" test now also removes `shadow` and `state.json`, so it checks status with only `log/` (and `.gitignore`) left.
- The new scenario is the ticket's repro (delete b.txt, ignore ig/, edit ig/c.txt). Its status output is identical with caches, without the index, with only `log/`, and in a fresh `git clone` (which carries no shadow or state).

Checked against the pre-change cmd_status.c (fresh build): all 4 checks fail there, reporting clean.

item.title: Writers refuse a hash chain broken inside a chunk, not only between chunks
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).**

```
duplicate the last line of the open chunk (a union-style git resolution does this)
lap verify     → CHAIN BROKEN: hash chain broken at main.000001.jsonl line 4 (record L2)
lap commit …   → [L3 …] recorded, rc 0
lap verify     → still CHAIN BROKEN
```

The writer builds on a history verify rejects, and the damage grows with every record. SPEC:1022 limits the writer's refusal to breaks between chunks; T-131 and the SPEC also say "lap never builds on a history it cannot vouch for".

**Cause.** `hist.c:814-856` checks only each chunk's first record against the previous chunk; `repo.c:458` then opens for writing.

**Fix.** Writers check the open chunk's chain (it is small, at most 4 MB, and the index's last covered hash lets them start there — T-166) and refuse with `history_broken`, naming the line, as verify does. Sealed chunks stay checked at their boundary only (verify covers them).

**Done when:** e2e: the repro's commit is refused and writes nothing; commit speed on a 4 MB open chunk measured before/after (stated in the ticket's comment); SPEC:1022 updated.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S182, git be0ba26.

**What changed.** `hist_check` (the check writers run before writing) now also walks the open chunk's own chain with the new `chain_within`. Each complete line's `prev` must be the hash of the line before it; the first line is already covered by the boundary check, and a torn tail is ignored because the writer cuts it. At the first break the writer fails with `history_broken`, and the message names the line as verify does: `hash chain broken at main.000001.jsonl line 4 (record L2)`. Sealed chunks keep the boundary-only check (verify reads them whole). To stay cheap, `chain_within` reads `prev` from the end of the line when lap wrote it there (`,"prev":"<64 hex>"}`, lap's encoder always puts it last). It hashes each line with SHA-256, and parses JSON only for a line shaped otherwise, or for the line that breaks, to name it.

**Speed (Done-when).** A 4.0 MB open chunk (24,152 chained filler records plus the fixture), 5 commits each after warm caches, measured with `time -p`:
- before: 0.00 s per commit (under the 10 ms resolution);
- after, first version (full JSON decode per record): 0.03 s;
- after, as committed (prev read from the line end, SHA-256 only): **0.02 s**.

So the cost is about 20 ms per commit at the maximum chunk size. It shrinks with the chunk, since only the open chunk is read. I did not start from the index's last covered hash: the index doesn't vouch for the chain, and 20 ms didn't seem worth the extra coupling.

**Tests**: unit 4534 passed. New `hist_check` cases: a whole open chunk passes with a torn tail; a repeated line is refused at line 4 with chain on and passes with chain off; a sealed chunk's inside is not checked. e2e 164 passed. The new scenario repeats the open chunk's last line. `verify` says CHAIN BROKEN at line 4, `commit --json` gives `history_broken` naming line 4, `session start` fails too, and the chunks are byte-identical. SPEC (§Damage is not a crash) updated.

Checked against the pre-change hist.c: the scenario fails there (the commit is recorded).

item.title: verify --deep checks the index instead of trusting it
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** SPEC:932: "Verification never uses the caches it is checking". Since T-170, `--deep` replays file by file along the index's chains and never checks the index itself:

```
set a.txt's entry in .lap/heads to -1; move .lap/shadow/a.txt away
lap verify --deep   → deep check: 1 file, 0 mismatches, rc 0
(.lap/index moved away)
lap verify --deep   → missing shadow: a.txt — deep check: 2 files, 1 mismatch
```

On an untouched typec clone the two agree; the gap is only that a damaged index hides damage.

**Cause.** `cmd_verify.c:365` takes `idx_ready` and `deep_indexed` (`231-322`) walks `idx->paths` and the heads chains as given.

**Fix.** Keep the per-file replay (T-170's bounded memory) but check the index while doing it: the set of files and each file's chain are rebuilt from one streaming pass over the log (paths and record offsets only) and compared with the index; any difference is a mismatch ("index: …"). Or fall back to the whole-log replay when the index disagrees.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro fails with the index present, naming the index; memory on the typec clone stays near T-170's 26 MB; the no-index path unchanged.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S183, git 05effa0.

**What changed**
- New `idx_matches_log(r, idx, why)` (idx.c) makes one pass over the history a chunk at a time, with a scratch arena per record. It checks that each record has its entry at the same offset and length, of the same kind; that each commit's entry names the same file and op; and that its `prev_same_file` is the file's previous commit. At the end, each file's head must be its last commit and the entry count must match. The first difference comes back as `index: …`. Memory is a chunk plus one slot per file.
- `lap verify --deep`: the index leads the file-by-file replay only after it matches. Otherwise the whole history is replayed (the no-index path), and the index is reported as a mismatch of its own: its reason in text, and `.lap/index` in `mismatched_files` in JSON. So a damaged index can no longer hide damage.
- SPEC `lap verify` updated; the branch JSON fields from T-182 were added there too.

**The repro** (a.txt's head cleared in `.lap/heads`, its shadow moved away): before this change, `--deep` said 0 mismatches. Now it lists `missing shadow: a.txt` and `index: the last commit it gives a.txt is not the history's` (2 mismatches) and exits 1. With the index moved away, it still finds the missing shadow, and no index line appears.

**Memory**: `tests/perf/rebuild_memory.sh` on the 500 MB generated history gives `verify --deep` **66 MB** (T-170 measured 65 MB; bound 144 MB), `verify` 10 MB, `rebuild` 114 MB. The typec clone is not on this machine, so I did not measure the ticket's 26 MB figure; the perf fixture is the stand-in.

**Tests**: unit 4546 passed (new: `idx_matches_log` on a rebuild-shaped index, then with a wrong head, chain link, file, offset and entry count). e2e 165 passed (new scenario as above, also checking the JSON list). Checked against the pre-change cmd_verify.c: the scenario fails there.

item.title: A nested branch merged straight into main counts as merged there
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** b1 from main, b2 from b1; b2 commits; main: `git merge b2`, `lap merge b2` → adopted 1 of 1.

```
main: lap branch list --json   → b2 state "active", merged null
(b2's folder removed)
main: lap branch list          → b2 missing (gone) (from b1) — "tend it from b1's folder"
```

It is never pruned, and reads as unmerged work that is lost. This follows SPEC:632-633 (a nested branch "judges its state against that branch's history", b1's, where no merge of b2 is recorded), which contradicts the registry rule (SPEC:427-433 and §Registry: merged-and-gone is pruned silently).

**Cause.** `cmd_branch.c:570-580` judge a nested branch only against its parent branch's merge records.

**Fix.** A nested branch is merged, as listed from a folder, when its head is adopted into that folder or into the branch it started from. State that in SPEC, replacing the "judged against that branch's history" sentence. b1's own list keeps showing b2 active until b1 adopts it (b1 has not got that work).

**Done when:** e2e: after the straight merge, main lists b2 as merged; with b2's folder gone it is pruned from main's view without a word; b1's list still shows it active; unit test for the state rule.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S184, git 991d4db.

**What changed**
- New `branches_status_nearer(via, here)` (branches.c) ranks merged whole over merged in part (a merge record exists) over not merged, and keeps the branch-between's status when the two are level.
- `lap branch list`: a nested branch is now judged against the history of the branch it started from *and* this folder's own merges, and the status that went further is shown. So b2 merged straight into main is `merged` in main's list.
- A nested branch shown as `merged` whose folder is gone is left out of the list without a word, matching how a registered branch of this folder's own is pruned. The registry is untouched: b2's entry is in b1's registry and is b1's to tend.
- JSON commas and the "no branches started from this folder" line now follow the entries actually shown.
- SPEC: the "judges its state against that branch's history" sentence is replaced by the here-or-there rule and the list pruning.

**Tests**: unit 4551 passed (new `branches_status_nearer` cases: level keeps via's; merged here beats active or partly merged there; merged there beats not merged here). e2e 166 passed. The new scenario uses the nest_trio fixture. b2 commits, git merge b2 into main, `lap merge b2` (adopts 2 of 2, since the chain brings b1's earlier commit). Main lists b2 as `merged`, while b's list still shows it `active`. After `git worktree remove` of b2's folder, main's list (text and JSON) no longer mentions b2 but still lists b, and b's list shows b2 `missing`.

Checked against the pre-change cmd_branch.c: the scenario fails there. While writing the test I mis-applied a sed to three existing scenarios' `adopted 1 of 1` lines. I caught it when those scenarios failed and restored them, and the final diff touches no existing scenario.

item.title: --copy-from-folder never rewrites a branch chunk git brought
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).**

```
b: commit B1; git commit; commit B2 (not in git)
main: git merge b (brings b's chunk with B1); lap merge b --copy-from-folder
→ adopted 2 of 2 commits
git status --short .lap →  M .lap/log/<b>.000001.jsonl
```

The chunk git brought was extended with B2 from the folder. SPEC:441-443: "lap never rewrites a copy git brought, so the next `git merge` finds that file unchanged on this side and never conflicts on `.lap/log/`". Here the next `git merge` did not conflict only because b's side then held the same bytes; any difference (b sealed at another point, amended, crashed mid-append) conflicts.

**Cause.** `--copy-from-folder` copies the folder's chunks over whatever is here, including chunks git brought (T-127's "never overwrites a present branch chunk" is bypassed by the flag).

**Fix.** With `--copy-from-folder`, copy only chunks absent here; for a present chunk shorter than the folder's, adopt up to what is here and say that the rest comes with the next `git merge` (or refuse `git_merge_first` for that part). Update SPEC §Merging's flag description.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro leaves the git-brought chunk byte-identical; the SPEC's claim holds; the existing `--copy-from-folder` tests still pass.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S185, git 592be6b.

**What changed**
- `own_chunks` has a new `extend` flag and a `behind` out-flag. The branch folder still fills in chunks missing here whenever `fill` is set. It extends a copy here that is a byte prefix of its own only when `extend` is set, which lap merge passes only when the branch folder has no git (`fill && !git`).
- Under git with `--copy-from-folder`, a present chunk that the folder runs past is taken as it is, as the last chunk: nothing after it is copied, so no chunk sits past a gap. `behind` is set, and the merge prints `note: b's history here stops where git merge left it; what its folder has past that comes with the next git merge`.
- The plain-copy (no git) mode still extends a prefix copy, as before. SPEC §Merging and the `lap merge` flag text say this.

**Tests**: unit 4557 passed. New `own_chunks` case: fill without extend keeps the shorter copy as the only chunk, not written, with behind set; with extend, behind is not set. The existing cases pass extend. e2e 167 passed, and the existing `--copy-from-folder` scenarios are unchanged and green. The new scenario is the ticket's repro: B1 through git, B2 committed after it but not in git. `lap merge b --copy-from-folder` prints the note, b's chunk is byte-identical (cksum) and `git status` shows it unchanged, and main's history holds B1 but not B2.

Checked against the pre-change cmd_merge.c: all 4 checks fail there (the chunk was rewritten, and B2 was adopted).

item.title: verify reports a branch whose first chunk is missing, instead of leaving it out
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced, in part).** With `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES=500`, branch b writes chunks 000001–000005; main `git merge b`; then `<b>.000001.jsonl` is removed in main and b's folder is gone:

```
main: lap verify --json   → {"ok":true,"records":3,"chain_ok":true,"branches":[]}
```

A branch with four chunks here is silently left out. SPEC:274-278: every command refuses a history it cannot open whole — a chunk missing — with `history_broken`.

Part of the audit's claim did **not** hold: `lap log --branch b` does name the problem ("the history of … starts nowhere: …000001.jsonl is missing or empty"), it is not `unknown_branch`.

**Cause.** verify's branch pass lists branches by their first chunk; lineages with chunks but no chunk 1 are never visited.

**Fix.** verify lists every lineage with any chunk here and reports one without chunk 1 (or with a gap) as broken, naming the chunk; `ok:false`.

item.title: Docs say which files in .lap/ are machine-local state, and rebuild notices a branch folder that lost its lineage
item.description:
**Verified.** SPEC:59-60 ("everything in `.lap/` except `log/` is a derived, disposable cache. Any of it may be deleted at any time"), the lap README:207 and the lap skill:241-244 say the same. But `.lap/lineage`, `.lap/parent` and `.lap/branches.json` are not derived from the log.

What deleting `.lap/lineage` does in a branch folder (reproduced):

```
b1 (branch, chunks ed347e15c334.000001-2): mv .lap/lineage away
lap rebuild   → rebuilt all caches from 3 records (chain ok)      — main's 3 records only
lap commit …  → "this folder has branches: … --branch main"       — it now takes itself for main
```

Following the docs turns a branch into main without a word; its own chunks are ignored.

**Fix.**
- SPEC, README and skill: the cache contract names the exceptions — `lineage`, `parent` and `branches.json` are machine-local state (never committed, not rebuilt), with what losing each means.
- `lap rebuild` (and writers) notice a folder that holds another lineage's chunks whose first record is a branch record started from this folder's history, with no `.lap/lineage`: a warning naming the lineage and how to restore the file.

**Done when:** docs updated in all three places; e2e: the repro's rebuild prints the warning; unit test for the detection.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S187, git 7ffec2b.

**Docs (all three places)**
- SPEC's cache contract now excludes `lineage`, `parent` and `branches.json`: they are machine-local state, never derived, rebuilt or put in git. It says what losing each means: without `lineage` the folder takes itself for main, and writers warn; without `parent` a branch folder can't be told from a copy or a clone; without `branches.json` the branches are known only by their chunks, and their folders are no longer found or tended.
- The README paragraph after the cache list says the same.
- The lap skill's Sanity section no longer says to delete "anything under `.lap/` other than `log/`". It names the three files and says never to delete `lineage`.

**Detection.** New `hist_lost_lineage(lapdir)` returns a branch only when `.lap/lineage` is absent and that branch's chunks are here while its parent's chunks here end exactly at its `base_chunk`. That is a branch folder's shape: it copies its parent's chunks up to the base. A parent's own folder always has the next chunk, because the start seals the base chunk and opens an empty one. For a branch of a branch it names the deepest. Every writer (`repo_open_at` for write, which includes `lap rebuild`) prints:

`warning: this folder holds branch b1 (<id>) as its own folder does, main's history here ending at its base, but has no .lap/lineage, so it records to main. If it is that branch's folder, restore the file: printf '<id>\n' > .lap/lineage`

It is a warning only: the command goes on as before.

**Tests**: unit 4567 passed (new: a branch folder without its lineage file is detected; the parent folder past the base is not; a nested chain names the deepest; a folder with the file is not). e2e 169 passed. The new scenario is the repro in copy mode: with b1's lineage moved away, `lap rebuild` and `lap session end` (a writer that writes nothing here) print the warning with the id and the restore command. With the file back, and in main, nothing is printed. Checked against the pre-change repo.c: the scenario fails there.

item.title: Docs say which files in .lap/ are machine-local state, and rebuild notices a branch folder that lost its lineage
item.description:
**Verified.** SPEC:59-60 ("everything in `.lap/` except `log/` is a derived, disposable cache. Any of it may be deleted at any time"), the lap README:207 and the lap skill:241-244 say the same. But `.lap/lineage`, `.lap/parent` and `.lap/branches.json` are not derived from the log.

What deleting `.lap/lineage` does in a branch folder (reproduced):

```
b1 (branch, chunks ed347e15c334.000001-2): mv .lap/lineage away
lap rebuild   → rebuilt all caches from 3 records (chain ok)      — main's 3 records only
lap commit …  → "this folder has branches: … --branch main"       — it now takes itself for main
```

Following the docs turns a branch into main without a word; its own chunks are ignored.

**Fix.**
- SPEC, README and skill: the cache contract names the exceptions — `lineage`, `parent` and `branches.json` are machine-local state (never committed, not rebuilt), with what losing each means.
- `lap rebuild` (and writers) notice a folder that holds another lineage's chunks whose first record is a branch record started from this folder's history, with no `.lap/lineage`: a warning naming the lineage and how to restore the file.

**Done when:** docs updated in all three places; e2e: the repro's rebuild prints the warning; unit test for the detection.

item.title: Docs say .lapignore affects only files not yet recorded
item.description:
**Verified.** T-154 added `cli/kb-cli/src/third_party/tree-sitter*/` and `utf8proc/` to `.lapignore`, but files lap recorded before stay tracked (by design, T-136: `cmd_status.c:57-59`, so edits to a file ignored later are never lost silently). In this repository: 108 vendored paths in the history, 109 files and 38 MB under `.lap/shadow/cli/kb-cli/src/third_party/`. Neither the SPEC, the README nor the skill says that `.lapignore` does not stop tracking a recorded file.

**Decision (user, 2026-09-28): no `lap untrack`.** A new record type (to untrack without rewriting history) was considered and dropped: it touches replay, rebuild, the index's tracked set, status, verify --deep, merge (carrying untracks across branches), the views and the SPEC, and older laps would refuse to write to a repository holding one — too much for a small lap. What it would buy here is 38 MB of cache and a few stat checks the stat cache already makes cheap; the vendored files never change, so they never show as edits. Recording a delete instead was also dropped: a delete carries the whole old text (about 38 MB more log) and would claim the files were deleted.

**What this ticket does.** SPEC (the `.lapignore` section), the lap README and the lap skill say: `.lapignore` keeps lap from recording files it has not recorded yet; a file recorded before it was ignored stays tracked (its edits show in status); to shed tracked files for good, start a new history (rare, blunt, stated as such).

**Done when:** the three places say this in the same words; nothing in lap changes.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S188, git 3f9d845. Docs only; lap is unchanged, per the decision (no `lap untrack`, no recorded deletes).

The same sentence now appears in all three places: the SPEC's `.lapignore` section, the lap README (replacing its one-line "keep their history" remark), and the lap skill under its `.lapignore` advice:

> `.lapignore` keeps lap from recording files it has not recorded yet. A file recorded before it was ignored stays tracked: its edits still show in `lap status`, so none is lost unseen. To shed tracked files for good, start a new history (a fresh `.lap/` from `lap init`): rare, and blunt, since the whole history goes with them.

No tests: nothing in lap changed.

item.title: Lap History retries lap after a failure, and when lap.path changes
item.description:
**Verified (code).** In `packages/lap-vscode/src/extension.ts`, `BranchSource.refresh` stores the new signature (`this.signature = sig`) *before* `lap branch list` answers. When lap fails (not found, wrong `lap.path`, an older lap), the signature already matches, so the list is not asked again until something on disk changes. Nothing listens for configuration changes (no `onDidChangeConfiguration`), and the `lap.refresh` command (line ~732) refreshes the tree and the page but never calls `branches.refresh(true)`.

So after fixing `lap.path`, branches stay empty and the error stays until a commit happens somewhere.

**Fix.** Store the signature only when lap answered; on `lap.path`/`coboard.lapPath` changes and on `lap.refresh`, call `branches.refresh(true)` (and re-read the main log's problem state).

**Done when:** unit test with a fake exec: a failed list is retried on the next refresh; a configuration change and `lap.refresh` force it.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S189, git c08a4fb.

**What changed (lap-vscode)**
- New `ListGate` (branches.ts) decides whether to ask lap for the branch list. It keeps a list's signature only once lap *answered*, so a failed run (no lap, a wrong `lap.path`, an older lap) is asked again on the next refresh. A request still in flight is not started twice unless forced.
- New `askBranchList(gate, sig, force, root, exec, cb)` runs `lap branch list --json` through the gate with an injected exec and hands back lap's failure (`lapFailure`) and the parsed JSON. `BranchSource.refresh` uses it with `execFile`. The no-branches case (signature `""`) goes through the gate too.
- `lap.refresh` now also calls `branches.refresh(true)`.
- A new `onDidChangeConfiguration` listener: when `lap.path` or `coboard.lapPath` changes, it re-reads the tree (the main log's problem state), pushes the page, updates the status bar and forces the branch list.

**Tests**: lap-vscode 60 passed. New fake-exec tests:
- a failed list (ENOENT) is asked again for the same signature;
- once answered, it is not asked again until the signature moves or it is forced (the lap.refresh / new lap.path path); the exec ran exactly 5 times for the 5 asks;
- an in-flight list is not asked twice unless forced, and is asked again after it fails.

The host test's fake `vscode.workspace` gained `onDidChangeConfiguration`. Not verified: the configuration listener in a real VS Code window (the host test only activates the extension).

item.title: Lap History names a broken branch history: a missing first chunk, a gap, a nested branch's missing middle
item.description:
**Verified (code).** T-133 names a missing chunk only in some cases (`packages/lap-vscode/src/chunks.ts`):

- `historyProblem` (`65-84`) checks this folder's own lineage and main only. In a nested branch folder, the middle lineage (the branch it started from) is never checked.
- `missingChunk` (`45-60`) returns null when a lineage has no chunk 1 at all (its highest number counts from 0), so a branch whose first chunk is gone is "fine".
- Branch rows read `ownFiles` → `lineageChunks` (`35-44`, `230-247`), which stops quietly at the first gap: the row shows part of the branch's history with no error.

The CLI refuses all these with `history_broken` (SPEC:274-278); the view shows an empty or partial history instead.

**Fix.** One check, used by the folder's history and by each branch row: every lineage in the chain (own, each ancestor branch, main) must run from chunk 1 without a gap and start with the expected record; otherwise the row or view shows the problem in lap's words, never part of the history.

**Done when:** unit tests for: missing chunk 1, a gap, a nested branch's missing middle chunk, each giving the named problem; a branch row with a gap shows an error, not partial sessions.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap sessions S190 and S191 (a follow-up for one fragment), git 043f20a and 7abe6c7 (lap history only).

**What changed (lap-vscode)**
- New `chainProblem(dir, names, lineage)` in chunks.ts, used by both the folder view and the branch rows. It walks the lineage to main. Each lineage must run from chunk 1 with no gap, as far as the next branch needs (its `base_chunk`). A branch's first chunk must open with its own branch record, and it then continues into the parent. It returns lap's words: `history chunk <name> is missing from <dir>`, `… does not open with branch <id>'s branch record`, or a loop. So a missing first chunk, a gap, and a nested branch's missing middle are each named.
- `historyProblem` (the folder's own history) now uses it, so a nested branch folder's middle lineage is checked too. `branchProblem(lapDir, id)` is exported for rows.
- Branch rows: `BranchSource` checks each row where its history is read (the branch folder while present, else the chunks here). `BranchView` has a new `problem`; with one, the row has **no sessions** (never part of a history). The webview row's description adds "· history broken", and opening the row shows the problem with a warning.

**Tests**: lap-vscode 63 passed. New cases: a gap in b2's own chunks; b1's chunk that b2 started from missing (b1 alone still fine); b1's chunk 1 missing (both broken); a first chunk that isn't the branch record; main's base chunk missing; the folder's own chain through a nested branch. `branchView` with a problem shows no sessions.

**Rendered**: headless Chrome over the built bundle (out/media), light and dark, with one good row and one broken row opened. Both themes show "active · history broken" and the warning line with the chunk. Not rendered in a real VS Code window.

Process note: one lap behavior was refused as too short, which shifted three behaviors onto the wrong fragments. I fixed them with `lap amend` (L4513–L4515) and committed the last fragment (L4521) in S191.

coboard reports a branch it could not read, instead of dropping its sessions
item.description:
**Verified (code, and lap's message by a run).** T-137 reports lap failures for this folder's sessions, not for branches:

- `packages/coboard/src/lap.ts:124-126`: a failed `session list --branch <name>` becomes `sessions: []` in a catch, with no error kept.
- `lap.ts:128`: a failed `lap branch list` is swallowed as "a lap from before branches".
- `mcp.ts:224`: `board_sessions` keeps only `sessionCommits(…).value`, so a failed commit read becomes `commits: []`.

So `board_get`/`board_sessions` show a ticket with fewer sessions or commits and no `lapError`. The lap message for a registered branch whose `.lap/log` is unreadable (chmod 000) is also misleading: "the history of … starts nowhere: …000001.jsonl is missing or empty" — the chunk is there, just unreadable (the audit's "`unknown_branch`" did not reproduce; the message is this one).

**Fix.** Collect per-branch and per-session failures into `lapError` (naming the branch or session); lap says "cannot read" (with the OS reason) when a chunk exists but cannot be opened.

**Done when:** coboard tests: an unreadable branch log gives `lapError` naming the branch, and a failed commit read gives one too; lap e2e: the unreadable-chunk message names the permission problem.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap sessions S193 and S194 (a follow-up for the fragments I had left pending), git 9a579d3 and 8e7e458 (lap history only).

**What changed**
- **coboard `ticketSessions`** now collects what it could not read. A branch whose `session list --branch` fails keeps its row with no sessions and adds `branch <name>: <lap's message>`. A failed `lap branch list` adds `lap branch list: <message>`, except an older lap's `unknown command`, which still means "no branches here". With any failure the result is `ok:false` with the sessions that *were* read and the failures joined as `error`. The VS Code panel already shows `error` when set.
- **`board_sessions`** starts from that error and adds `session [<branch>/]S<n>: <message>` for each session whose commits could not be read; all of them are joined into `lapError`.
- **lap**: `hist_first_record` checks `plat_is_unreachable` first. A branch whose chunks sit behind an unsearchable folder now reads `cannot read the history of <id>: <path> cannot be reached (no permission on its folder)` instead of "starts nowhere … missing or empty". As the ticket noted, the command's own code there is `unknown_branch` (from `repo_view_branch`); only the message changed.

**Tests**
- coboard 45 passed. New: real lap with feat's `.lap/log` at mode 000 gives `ok:false` and an error `branch feat: … cannot be reached (no permission on its folder)`, while main's T-1 session is still returned (skipped as root). A fake lap script that lists a session but fails `lap log` makes `board_sessions` give `lapError: "session S1: history chunk main.000002.jsonl is missing"` with the session kept (empty commits). Both fail against the old lap.ts/mcp.ts.
- lap unit 4572 passed (new: `hist_first_record` behind a mode-000 log folder names it unreachable, not missing).
- lap e2e 170 passed (new: `lap log --branch feat` from main with feat's log unsearchable names the permission problem).

Process note: I first committed fewer lap behaviors than fragments in lap.ts and mcp.ts. I corrected L4534/L4535 with `lap amend` and committed the four remaining fragments in S194.

item.title: Merging a branch with no commits records the merge
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).**

```
worktree one; lap branch start one; git commit
main: git merge one; lap merge one   → "branch one: nothing new to adopt since the last merge"  (there was no earlier merge)
(no merge record written)
remove one's worktree
lap branch list                      → one  missing (gone) — "lap branch move … or lap branch forget …"
lap session start "…"                → this folder has branches: … --branch main
```

A branch started and abandoned without work shows as missing for good, and main keeps requiring `--branch` until `branch forget`.

**Fix.** A merge of a branch whose head is past its base only by its branch record (and sessions, if any) writes a merge record (adopted 0) so it counts as merged; the message says "nothing to adopt: it has no commits".

**Done when:** e2e: the repro prints the new message, the branch lists as merged, and once its folder is gone it is pruned and main no longer needs `--branch`.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S195, git 6cf1069.

**What changed**
- New `merge_nothing_yet(start, count, heads, n, unmerged)` (cmd_merge.c) decides whether a merge that finds nothing to adopt still records itself: when the branch was never merged (no last merged head), which means it has nothing past its branch record. A branch with sessions but no commits still takes the normal path, since its sessions are adopted. `unmerged[k]` marks each branch of the chain with no merge yet.
- `lap merge` then writes a merge record per unmerged branch of the chain, with adopted 0, `head` = its last record (the branch record), and no stops, and saves state and caches. It prints `merged branch one (<id>): nothing to adopt: it has no commits`, or `would merge …` for a dry run, which writes nothing. A second merge says `nothing new to adopt since the last merge`, as before.
- The branch then counts as merged. Once its folder is gone the registry drops it on the next write (existing pruning), so `lap session start` in main no longer needs `--branch`. SPEC `lap merge` says so.

**Tests**: unit 4577 passed (new `merge_nothing_yet` cases: never merged with nothing new → recorded and marked; something new → not this path; merged before → not recorded). e2e 171 passed. The new scenario is the ticket's repro via `merge_pair` with no commits in b. The dry run and the merge print the new message, `branch list --json` shows b `merged`, and a second merge says nothing new. After `git worktree remove`, `session start` without `--branch` succeeds and b is no longer registered or missing.

Checked against the pre-change cmd_merge.c: all 6 checks fail there.

item.title: An empty flag value is refused as a missing one
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** T-147 refuses a missing value ("needs a value"); an empty one passes:

```
lap log -n ""             → no commits yet            (the repo has commits)
lap session list --meta=  → every session, unfiltered
lap log --branch=         → error: no branch  here: not in this folder's registry …
```

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S196, git 0ba1322.

**What changed.** `flags_known` (the shared check every command runs first) now refuses an empty value exactly as a missing one, with `usage: <flag> needs a value`:
- a value flag followed by an empty word (`--branch ""`, `-n ""`, `-i ""`);
- a joined long flag with nothing after `=` (`--branch=`, `--meta=`), named without the `=`.

An empty word after `--` is still a positional argument. The error code stays `usage`, the one T-147 uses for a missing value (the ticket said `bad_args`; I kept the existing code so the two cases match). SPEC's argument-parsing paragraph says this.

**Tests**: unit 4581 passed (new: `--branch=`, `--branch ""` and `-i ""` refused; `-- ""` accepted). e2e 172 passed (new: `log -n ""`, `session list --meta=`, `log --branch=` and `session start … --branch=` each give `usage` naming the flag). The three repros from the ticket print `-n needs a value`, `--meta needs a value` and `--branch needs a value`. No existing test passed an empty value, and the full suites are green.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S197, git b0cbf93. This implements the decision: skip, don't refuse.

**What changed**
- New `repo_nested(root, rel_dir)` (repo.c): the folder holds its own `.lap/`, so it is another repository.
- `lap status` (its working-tree walk) and branch start's working-tree check don't descend into such a folder.
- `repo_relpath`, which `lap commit` and every other path argument go through, refuses a path whose folders include one with its own `.lap/`: `path sub/a.txt is outside this repository: sub has its own .lap/, so its files are that repository's`.
- SPEC `lap status` gains a paragraph: a folder with its own `.lap/` is another repository, as git skips a nested repository. It is the downward half of "the nearest `.lap/` owns a file". Files recorded there before it got its own `.lap/` stay tracked, as ignored-after-recording files do.

**Tests**: unit 4589 passed (new: `repo_nested` for a folder with and without `.lap/`, and a missing one; `repo_relpath` refuses `sub/a.txt` under the nested folder and accepts `plain/deeper/b.txt`). e2e 173 passed. The new scenario runs `git worktree add sub -b sub` inside main and `lap branch start sub --from ..` there, then edits `sub/a.txt`. Main's `lap status` doesn't mention `sub/` and is clean, `lap commit sub/a.txt --branch main` is refused as outside this repository, and the branch's own status shows `modified a.txt`.

Checked against the pre-change code: the scenario fails there (status lists sub/ files, and the commit is not refused).

item.title: A folder with its own .lap/ inside the repository is skipped by the parent, as git skips nested repositories
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** Tools put worktrees inside the repository (Claude Code's `.claude/worktrees/`, `git worktree add sub`). lap accepts a branch there, and the parent then sees every branch file as its own:

```
main: git worktree add sub -b sub; cd sub; lap branch start sub --from ..
main: lap status   → new sub/.lapignore (6 lines), new sub/a.txt (10 lines)
```

A parent commit of those would record the branch's files into main's history.

**Decision (user, 2026-09-28): skip, do not refuse.** The folder walk that status and commit use does not descend into a subfolder holding its own `.lap/`. This is the downward half of the rule lap already has upward: every command works in the nearest `.lap/`, so files under `sub/` are recorded by sub's repository, never the parent's. It keeps `.claude/worktrees/` and `git worktree add sub` working, and covers an unrelated nested lap repository too. Not chosen: refusing such a branch start (it would block those layouts).

Files the parent recorded under that subfolder before it got its own `.lap/` stay tracked, like files ignored after they were recorded (no new rule).

item.title: "Already done" requires the same final newline
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** b changes the last line `10` to `TEN` keeping the final newline; main changes it to `TEN` with no final newline. git conflicts; resolved keeping main's side; then:

```
lap merge b   → adopted 0 of 1 commit; already done here: #… (this folder made the same change)
```

T-158/SPEC: already done means the same text *and* the same final newline.

**Cause.** `adopt.c:108-109`: `(c->eof_nl == branch.eof_nl || c->eof_nl == merged.eof_nl)` accepts either.

**Fix.** Require the commit's final newline to equal the parent's (`merged.eof_nl`) when the change touches the last line; otherwise it is a conflict.

**Done when:** adopt unit test for the case (conflict), and one where the newline matches (already done).

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S198, git 3558559.

**What changed (adopt.c).** New `same_eof(eof, at_end, branch_eof, parent_eof)`. When the change reaches the file's last line, its final newline is part of the change and must equal the parent's. Elsewhere either side's is accepted, as before, since the newline is not that change's. Both "already done" paths use it: the single identical commit (reaches the end when its old region runs past the branch's last line, `e > branch.count`) and the multi-step run from T-173 (when the reached region ends the file). The ticket's case (b `10→TEN` keeping the newline, main `TEN` with none) is therefore a conflict. SPEC merge rule 3 says so.

**Tests**: unit 4594 passed. New adopt cases: at the last line a different final newline gives a conflict (placed 0, `why` set) and the same one is already done; a mid-file identical change with a different final newline elsewhere is still already done. e2e 173 passed. Checked against the pre-change adopt.c: 2 of the new asserts fail there.

item.title: lap amend says not_a_commit for a session or amendment, as the SPEC does
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** SPEC:853 lists `not_a_commit` ("the reference names another record"). It can never be emitted:

```
lap amend <a session_start record's hash> … --json → {"error":"unknown_ref","message":"no commit has a hash starting cf94a79c0f90"}
lap amend S1 … --json                              → {"error":"unknown_ref","message":"S1 is not a commit: …"}
```

**Cause.** `ref_find` (`cmd_common.c:244-290`) resolves only commits, so the `c->type != REC_COMMIT` branch in `cmd_amend.c:50-53` is dead code.

**Fix.** Let `ref_find` resolve a hash to any record (reporting its type) and have amend refuse non-commits with `not_a_commit`; `S<n>` given to amend gives `not_a_commit` too. Or drop the code from the SPEC and the dead branch — choose one; the first matches the SPEC.

**Done when:** e2e for both lines above giving `not_a_commit`.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S199, git e2a9532. I took the first option, matching the SPEC.

**What changed.** `ref_find` becomes `find_ref(…, any)`. The new `ref_find_record` resolves over every record: a hash (or unique prefix) names whatever record it is, and `S<n>` names a session's start. `ref_find` stays commits-only for show/rr. `lap amend` uses `ref_find_record`, so its `not_a_commit` branch is live and names the type: `S1 is not a commit: it names a session_start record; lap amend corrects commits`. Ambiguity and no-match messages say "records" in this mode. New `rec_type_name` exposes the log's type names. SPEC's amend errors say what `not_a_commit` covers.

**Tests**: unit 4602 passed (new: `ref_find_record` finds a session start and an amendment by hash (any case, with `#`), S1, and L1 by id, and refuses S9 with `unknown_ref`; `ref_find` still finds only the commit). e2e 174 passed (new: `lap amend <session_start hash prefix>` and `lap amend S1` give `not_a_commit`, and `lap amend L1` still works). Before this change both gave `unknown_ref`, as the ticket shows.

item.title: Leftovers outside .lap/log are cleared too: chunk temps in .lap/, shadow temps, log.replaced
item.description:
**Verified (code; the audit reproduced each by a crash or a hand-built state).**

- `hist_clear_tmp` (`hist.c:745-759`, called from `repo.c:442`) walks only `.lap/log/`. But since T-142 chunk temps are written in `.lap/` itself (`hist.c:741`, `tmpdir = .lap`), e.g. `.lap/main.000130.jsonl.tmp.4243`, and shadow temps next to their file (`platform.c:583-585`, e.g. `.lap/shadow/f04.txt.tmp.<pid>`, left by a merge killed during the shadow update — 3 of 40 kill trials). Neither the heal nor `lap rebuild` removes them.
- `hist_convert_legacy` returns early when the conversion already finished (`hist.c:572-577`) or when there is no `log.jsonl` (`547-548`), before clearing `log.replaced/` and `log.converting/`; a crash after publishing leaves `log.replaced/` for good.

Records, verify and status are unaffected; it is disk litter (a shadow temp can be megabytes).

**Fix.** Under the lock, writers clear `*.tmp.<pid>` names directly in `.lap/` and in the shadow tree (whose pid is not alive, or all of them — writers hold the lock), and `log.replaced/`/`log.converting/` whenever `log/` is complete; rebuild does the same.

**Done when:** e2e: hand-made leftovers of each kind are gone after one commit and after `lap rebuild`.

item.title: branch start reports why the parent could not be opened, with its own code
item.description:
**Verified (code).** `cmd_branch.c:175-177`:

```c
if (!repo_open_at(a, &pr, there, true, err, sizeof err)) {
    err_out(json, "no_parent", "%s", err);
```

Every failure to open the parent — `newer_history`, `history_broken`, a lock it cannot take — is reported as `no_parent` with another failure's message (the audit: a parent with a newer history gives `no_parent` carrying the `newer_history` text).

**Fix.** Use `repo_error_code()` (as other commands do) and keep `no_parent` for "no lap repository there".

**Done when:** e2e: a parent with an unknown record type gives `newer_history`; a missing parent still gives `no_parent`.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S201, git 7ebcdd5.

**What changed.** When branch start cannot open the parent, it reports `repo_error_code()`, the failure's own code (`newer_history`, `history_broken`, …), with its message. `no_parent` is kept only for `no_repo`, meaning no lap repository is there. `repo_open_at` now resets the code to `no_repo` on entry, so a caller that opens a folder directly (as branch start does) never reads a stale code from an earlier open. SPEC's branch start errors say so.

**Tests**: e2e 176 passed. The new scenario appends a validly chained `annotate` record to the parent's open chunk: `branch start` gives `newer_history` and leaves no lineage. A folder with no `.lap/` still gives `no_parent`. Unit 4607 passed; there is no new unit test here, since the change is a code choice at the call site, covered by the e2e. Checked against the pre-change cmd_branch.c: the `newer_history` check fails there (it said `no_parent`).

item.title: The newer-history check trusts the index only as far as its last covered hash
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** `newer_check` (`repo.c:356-360`) takes the index header's unknown-record count and `covered` whenever `covered <= size`, without T-166's check of the last covered record's hash (`idx_ready`/`tail_matches`, `idx.c:115-128`).

```
session start; commit; lap status (index built)
replace the last record with a validly chained {"type":"future_op",…} of the same length
lap session end   → note: this history has records of a newer type … ; session S1 ended, rc 0 — session_end appended after future_op
(.lap/index moved away) → error: this history holds 1 record of a type this lap does not know ("future_op") … (correct)
```

Low: it needs a record rewritten in place at the same size; a newer lap appends, and appended bytes are past `covered`, so they are scanned.

**Fix.** Trust the header only when the tail check passes (`idx_ready`-style); otherwise scan from 0.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro refuses with `newer_history` with the index present.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S202, git d4ad966.

**What changed.** New `idx_header_trusted` (idx.c) returns the index header only when it covers no more than the history *and* its last covered record still hashes as recorded (T-166's `tail_matches`). `newer_check` takes the index's unknown-record count and `covered` only from a trusted header. Otherwise it scans the whole history, as with no index.

**Tests**: e2e 177 passed. The new scenario is the repro: session start, a commit, then status (which builds the index). The last record is then rewritten in place, at exactly the same length, as a validly chained `future_op` record. `lap session end --json` now refuses with `newer_history` while the index is present. Unit 4607 passed; no new unit test, because `tail_matches` needs a real index on disk, which the e2e builds. Checked against the pre-change repo.c: the scenario fails there (the session ended).
