item.title: A reader racing a conversion's publish never sees "no history"
item.description:
**Verified (code; the audit hit it with a pause added in a scratch build — unmodified stress runs were clean).** `hist_open` (`hist.c:119-127`):

1. `list_chunks` finds no chunks in `.lap/log/` (not published yet);
2. the conversion renames `log.converting` → `log/` and removes `log.jsonl`;
3. `plat_file_size(legacy)` fails → `return true` with zero chunks.

The reader gets an empty history: `lap verify --json` → `{"ok":false,"error":"history_broken","message":"no history in …/.lap/log (expected log/main.000001.jsonl)"}`. The later path at `hist.c:152-155` already re-lists the chunks when the old file vanished; this one does not.

**Fix.** When the legacy file is gone and no chunk was found, list the chunks again before returning.

**Done when:** unit test with an injected step between the two checks (a test hook) showing the second listing is used.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S203, git db30c16.

**What changed.** In `hist_open`, when the first listing found no chunks and the old `log.jsonl` is gone by the time it is looked for, a conversion published its chunks in between. The chunks are then listed again instead of returning an empty history. A test hook `hist_open_between` (NULL in lap itself, declared in hist.h as tests only) runs between the two looks.

**Tests**: unit 4612 passed. New: a history that is only the old log, with the hook publishing `main.000001.jsonl` and removing the old file between the looks, opens as one chunk holding the published text, not legacy and not empty. With the re-listing removed (a scratch build keeping the hook), that test fails, so it exercises the fix. e2e 177 passed.

item.title: verify reports an old log.jsonl that differs from the chunks beside it
item.description:
**Verified (code; the audit reproduced it).** When a `log.jsonl` comes back next to converted chunks and the chunks do not hold all of it (e.g. restored from a backup with one different record), readers read the old file silently (`hist.c:141-146`, per SPEC), writers refuse ("both … hold history, and they differ", `hist.c:579-586`) — but `lap verify` says `ok:true` over the old file's records, and `session list` misses what the chunks hold (S3 in the audit's run).

**Fix.** verify (and the reader notice) says both shapes are present and differ, naming both, with `ok:false` — what the writer refuses, verify reports.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro fails verify with that message; the "conversion finished, old file left" case (chunks hold all of it) stays ok.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S204, git fc3584a.

**What changed.** `hist_open`, finding an old `log.jsonl` beside chunks that don't hold all of it, now tells two cases apart. If the chunks are a start of it (an interrupted conversion), the old file is read as before. If they are not, they differ, and `Hist.differ` is set; the old file is still read, per the SPEC. With `differ` set:
- `lap verify` fails, printing `HISTORY IN TWO SHAPES: both …/log.jsonl and …/log hold history, and they differ: keep the one that is right and move the other away` (the writer's words), with `ok:false` and `history_error` in JSON;
- readers print a note once per command saying the old file is being read;
- writers refuse, as before.

SPEC's two-shapes paragraph says so.

**Tests**: unit 4618 passed (new: chunks that are a start of the old file → read, not differ; chunks of another history → differ; chunks holding all of it → chunks read). e2e 177 passed. The existing "a single-file log that differs from the chunks is refused" scenario now also checks that verify fails with the message in text and JSON and that `lap log` prints the note. A leftover old file the chunks hold whole verifies ok with no such line. Checked against the pre-change code: the three new checks fail there.

item.title: Broken-history messages name the chunk and blame it the same way everywhere
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced with `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES=400`).**

- A sealed chunk reduced to a blank line (main.000003): verify → "chunk main.000004 does not continue sealed chunk main.000003"; a writer → "main.000003 does not continue main.000002". Two different blames for one fault.
- A sealed chunk emptied (main.000003): verify → "main.000004 does not continue sealed chunk main.000002" — chunk 3 is never named.
- A malformed record met by a reader's in-memory heal is named "log line %d" (`repo.c:200`), not chunk and line.
- (From the audit, same family) verify on an unknown record with a bad `prev` says "(record init)"; an edited sealed branch chunk is reported two ways.
- `lap merge` of amendments only prints "adopted 0 of 0 commits" before "amendments carried: 1".

**Fix.** One blame rule (the first chunk whose content is wrong: empty/blank/torn sealed chunk → that chunk) used by verify and writers; chunk-and-line in every message; merge says "no commits to adopt; amendments carried: n".

**Done when:** e2e for the blank and emptied chunk (both commands name main.000003) and the heal message; merge message test.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S205, git c5c264f and 7dfe1da (lap history only: two SPEC behaviors I had swapped, fixed with `lap amend`).

**What changed**
- **One blame rule, in `hist_check`**, which every command runs. A sealed chunk that is empty, or that does not open with a record (a blank line left in it), is itself to blame: `sealed chunk main.000003.jsonl is empty: it was emptied or copied short …` or `sealed chunk main.000003.jsonl holds no record where it starts (…): it was changed …`. Readers, verify and writers now all name the same chunk, instead of blaming the chunk after it (verify) or the one before (writers). An empty *open* chunk is still fine.
- **The heal** (a reader rebuilding its state) names a malformed record as `<chunk> line <n>: …` through `hist_where`, as other readers do, not `log line n`.
- **`lap merge`** that brings only sessions or amendments says `merged branch b (<id>): no commits to adopt`, followed by `amendments carried: n`, never `0 of 0`.
- SPEC: the "Damage is not a crash" bullet and the merge messages.

Not done from the ticket's "same family" list: verify's "(record init)" wording for an unknown record with a bad `prev`, and the two reports for an edited sealed *branch* chunk. The Done-when didn't require them, so they are unchanged.

**Tests**: unit 4626 passed (new: an emptied sealed chunk and a blank one are refused naming themselves, with or without the chain check, and chunk 1 emptied too). e2e 178 passed. New scenario with `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES=400` and ≥4 chunks: chunk 3 made blank, then emptied, is named by `verify` and by a commit alike. A malformed record appended to the open chunk with `state.json` removed makes `lap log` name `<chunk> line <n>`. item.title: On macOS, a chunk's seal and a conversion use F_FULLFSYNC
item.description:
**Verified (code).** `platform.c:485, 500, 601, 640` call plain `fsync`. On macOS, `fsync` hands data to the drive but does not flush the drive's cache; only `fcntl(fd, F_FULLFSYNC)` does. So T-165's power-loss ordering holds on Linux but is weaker on macOS.

**Decision (user, 2026-09-28): minimal form.** `F_FULLFSYNC` only where a crash would cost history structure — sealing a chunk (and creating the next) and publishing a conversion — not on every commit's append, so commit speed is unchanged and there is nothing to measure. A per-commit full flush is a durability refinement lap can live without; an interrupted append is already handled as a torn tail.

**Fix.** One helper, `plat_fsync_full`, on `__APPLE__` `fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC)` falling back to `fsync` when refused, elsewhere `fsync`; used at the seal and conversion sites only.

**Done when:** builds on macOS and Linux; a unit test that the helper succeeds on a regular file in TMPDIR; the SPEC's durability note says which writes get the full flush.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S206, git 69ecef2. This is the minimal form, as decided.

**What changed.** New `plat_fsync_full(path)` (platform.c) opens a file or folder. On `__APPLE__` it calls `fcntl(fd, F_FULLFSYNC)`, falling back to `fsync` when refused. Elsewhere it calls `fsync`; a folder that can't be synced (`EINVAL`) passes, and on Windows it behaves as `plat_fsync_dir` does. It is used at three places only:
- the seal: creating the next chunk syncs the log folder fully. Since `F_FULLFSYNC` empties the drive's whole cache, the sealed chunk's data goes through with it;
- a conversion: the written chunks' folder before publishing, then `.lap/` after the rename.

A commit's append keeps plain `fsync`, so commit speed is unchanged. SPEC's durability bullet says which writes get the full flush and why the append does not.

**Tests**: unit 4630 passed (new: `plat_fsync_full` succeeds on a regular file in `$TMPDIR` and on a folder, and refuses a missing path). e2e 178 passed.

**Not verified: a Linux build.** Docker is installed here but its daemon isn't running, so I built and tested on macOS only. The Linux path is plain `fsync` behind `#ifdef __APPLE__`, a line lap already had in `plat_fsync_dir`.

item.title: Lap History in a branch folder does not run lap branch list on every commit
item.description:
**Verified (code).** `listSignature` (`packages/lap-vscode/src/extension.ts:188-213`) includes every non-`main` chunk with its size. In a branch folder the folder's *own* lineage is not `main`, so each commit changes the signature and spawns `lap branch list --json`. The per-branch watchers (`286-292`) also force a refresh on every change. And `refresh` has no in-flight guard: two lists can run at once and the older answer can land last, overwriting the newer views.

**Fix.** Leave this folder's own lineage out of the signature (the list does not depend on it); keep one list in flight and drop answers older than the latest request.

**Done when:** unit test: committing in a branch folder does not change the signature; two overlapping refreshes apply only the newer answer.

author: claude
body:
Done. Code in git 53bd803; lap history in session S208, git d7bb15a.

**What changed (lap-vscode)**
- `listSignature` moved to chunks.ts (branches.ts must stay browser-safe for the webview's type check). It leaves out this folder's *own* lineage (read from `.lap/lineage`) as well as main. In a branch folder, a commit no longer changes the signature or runs `lap branch list`.
- `ListGate` numbers its requests (`begin`/`isLatest`). `askBranchList` passes the number to `done` and drops an answer when a newer request has been made, so an older answer landing last never overwrites newer views. A signature counts as answered only for the newest request. The per-branch-folder watchers still force a refresh, since a branch's own commits do change its counts.

**Tests**: lap-vscode 66 passed. New: in a branch folder, its own commits (a grown chunk, a new chunk) leave the signature unchanged, while another branch's growth and a merge change it. With two overlapping requests answered newest-first, only the newer answer is used, and its signature is the one remembered.

**Incident during this ticket.** The lap commits were refused: `packages/lap-vscode/.lap/log.jsonl`, the package's frozen pre-restructure history (145 records, last 2026-09-21, tracked in git), made lap treat the package as a nested repository under T-197's rule. My command chain let the git commit (53bd803) go through without the lap history. On your decision, that file was removed from git and disk (f2be984). I then recorded the 11 fragments in follow-up session S208.

item.title: Lap History tends a missing nested branch in its parent branch's folder, and notices a deleted branch folder
item.description:
**Verified (code).**

- **Move/Forget for a nested branch.** The buttons (`webview/history.tsx:443-455`) send only the name, and the extension runs `lap branch move|forget` in the workspace root (`extension.ts:~400-415`, `cwd: root`). A nested branch is tended in the folder of the branch it started from (SPEC:634; lap itself says "tend it from b1's folder"), so from the root lap answers `unknown_branch`.
- **A deleted branch folder is not noticed.** The watchers (`extension.ts:280-292`) listen to `onDidChange` and `onDidCreate` only; removing a branch folder leaves the row "active" until something else changes.

**Fix.** Send the branch's `via` (or its parent folder) with the message and run lap there; add `onDidDelete` to the watchers.

**Done when:** unit tests: the fix message for a nested row runs in the parent branch's folder; a delete event triggers a refresh.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S209, git e842eb2.

**What changed (lap-vscode)**
- New `tendFolder(root, rows, name)`: a branch listed with `via` is tended in the folder of the branch it started from while that folder is present; otherwise, and for this folder's own branches, in the workspace root, whose lap then says what it can. `fixBranch` runs `lap branch move|forget` there, so Move/Forget on a nested row no longer gets `unknown_branch`. The webview message is unchanged: the host looks the row up by name (names are unique since T-176).
- New `onAnyChange(watcher, fn)` wires change, create *and delete*. The branch-folder watchers use it, so removing a branch folder triggers a refresh, and the row turns missing instead of staying active.

**Tests**: lap-vscode 68 passed (new: `tendFolder` gives the parent branch's folder for a nested branch, and root for this folder's own branch, an unknown name, or a nested one whose parent folder is gone; `onAnyChange` calls the refresh on delete as on change and create). item.title: lap branch list indents a nested branch under the branch it started from
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** main has `b1` and `x`; a nested `x` starts from b1. `lap branch list` in main prints:

```
b1   active …/b1
x    active …/x
  x  active …/xn  (from b1)
```

The nested one is indented under the top-level `x`, not under `b1` — it follows the registry's order (`cmd_branch.c:566`), not its parent. With T-176 the names will differ, but the placement is still wrong for any order.

**Fix.** Print each nested branch right after the branch it started from (by `via`), recursively.

**Done when:** e2e: a nested branch started after another top-level branch prints under its parent.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S210, git 319a568.

**What changed.** New `branches_tree_order(a, reg, out)` (branches.c) orders the listed entries. Roots come in registry order: this folder's own branches, and any whose parent is not listed. Each is followed, depth first, by the branches started from it (`via` = its id). A loop of vias, which should never happen, is still shown once. `lap branch list` walks this order, so a nested branch is printed and indented right under its parent, whatever order the registries hold. JSON follows the same order.

**Tests**: unit 4636 passed (new: b1, x2, n1-from-b1, m1-from-n1, and an entry whose parent is not listed order as b1, n1, m1, x2, then the unlisted one). e2e 179 passed (new: copy mode, b1 then top-level x2 then n1 from b1 lists as `b1 n1 x2` with n1 indented). item.title: SPEC lists every error code and JSON field lap emits; merge says history_broken
item.description:
**Verified.**

- **Error codes.** Of 56 codes passed to `err_out` in `cli/lap-cli/src`, 25 appear nowhere in SPEC.md: `append_failed bad_args bad_edit_index bad_line bad_lineage bad_lines bad_meta bad_path chain_broken empty_range init_failed io_error lines_mismatch log_unreadable message_required no_active_session no_session no_target read_failed rebuild_failed replay_failed session_active shadow_failed state_failed unknown_file`. (The audit also found merge's list omitting `parent_read_only`/`log_unreadable`, and amend's `branch_required`/`wrong_branch`.)
- **Two names for one thing.** `lap merge` reports a broken history as `log_broken` (`cmd_merge.c:258, 357, 373`); every other command says `history_broken`.
- **JSON fields.** `verify --deep --json` returns `deep_checked`, `deep_mismatched`, `mismatched_files`, none in the SPEC. SPEC:575 does document `ref` for sessions. (The audit's claim of a `root` field in `status --json` did not reproduce.)

**Decision (user, 2026-09-28): minimal form.** A table in the SPEC (code, commands, meaning), written by hand — no test that greps the source against it. Where two codes mean the same thing, one is kept (merge uses `history_broken`); where a code is internal-only, the table says so.

**Done when:** every code `err_out` passes appears in the table; merge emits `history_broken` (e2e updated); verify's `--deep` JSON fields listed under verify.

item.title: Robustness, round 2
item.description:
Findings of the second audit (2026-09-28) of the M-14 work: merge, nested branches, amend, chunks and caches, branches and the registry, coboard, the views, SPEC and docs. The audit's agents reported them; every ticket here was then **reproduced or confirmed in the code by hand** (scratch repos under the session scratchpad, `verify/`). A ticket says when a part of the original claim did not hold.

What held up (not ticketed): no git conflict in `.lap/log/` in any layout tried (worktree, copy, lagging parent, siblings, nested, 460 random merge cases); `verify --deep` passed and `--dry-run` changed no byte in every merge; crash reruns matched; the M-14 fixes T-122..T-170 pass their original repros; suites unit 4411, e2e 149, coboard 42, npm 554 all green; no performance regression on a typec clone.

Not ticketed, on purpose: a refused `lap merge` repairs a torn tail (the writer repair every command does, of bytes never acknowledged); case-sensitive branch names (allowed by the SPEC); the conversion's chunk cap (only reachable at about 4 TB); two view suspicions (offset on a lineage change, the first whole read) and one unclear view claim that did not reproduce.

item.title: Skills catch up with M-15: worktrees inside the project, copied_branch, unreadable files, unique branch names
item.description:
**Why.** M-15 changed things an agent now meets that the skills do not mention. T-189 and T-190 updated the skills for their own changes and T-212 did amend's `--branch`; these four were left out (checked against `.claude/skills/lap/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/tickets/SKILL.md` after M-15 closed).

**Add to the lap skill's Branches section (and the tickets skill where it sends agents to branch folders):**
1. **A worktree inside the project works (T-197).** The skill shows only `git worktree add ../proj-parser`. Say that a branch folder may also live inside the project (e.g. Claude Code's `.claude/worktrees/<name>`): the parent skips any subfolder with its own `.lap/`, so its files never show in the parent's `lap status`.
2. **`copied_branch` (T-177).** In a plain copy of a branch folder, writers refuse: "<folder> is a copy of branch <name>, which is <original>: two folders never record to one branch". Say what to do: start a branch of its own there (`lap branch start <name> --from <original>`) — the way to make a branch of a branch by copying — or do the work in the original folder.
3. **`unreadable` in `lap status` (T-180).** Files lap cannot read are listed as `unreadable`, never as deleted or clean, and commit refuses them. Say: fix the permissions (or ask the user) — never commit around them.
4. **Branch names are unique across nested branches (T-176), and a folder with branches cannot become a branch (T-171).** One line each: `name_taken`/`ambiguous_branch` mean pick another name (or name the branch by its id); `has_branches` means the command was run in the wrong folder — run `branch start` in the new folder, with `--from` naming this one.

Keep it short: the error messages already say most of this; the skill says only what to do next.

**Done when:** both skills say the four points, in the words lap's messages use; nothing in lap changes.

item.title: Generated merge cases in the suite: fixed seeds, deterministic, the audit's invariants checked on every run
item.description:
**Why.** Every merge test in the repository is hand-picked (73 e2e scenarios, the adopt unit groups). The two audits' generated merge runs (460 cases in round 2, which found T-172, T-173 and T-181) lived in scratch scripts and were never added to the suite, so nothing guards the merge engine against the next change. The user rates this critical.

**Deterministic, not random at run time (user's requirement, 2026-09-28).**
- A fixed list of seeds: `make test` runs seeds 1–60 (seconds); `make prop` runs 1–500 (before a release). Same seeds, same cases, same results, every run and every machine. Nothing is taken from the clock.
- The driver carries its own PRNG (e.g. splitmix64), never the system's `rand()`, whose sequence differs between platforms.
- A failure prints its seed and keeps its folder; `LAP_PROP_SEED=<n>` replays exactly that case. Any bug found also gets a named hand-written scenario.

**What a case is.** A base file; the parent and the branch each make several lap commits of random edits (insertions, deletions, replacements, at the top and bottom, blank and repeated lines), including identical changes on both sides, a change made in several steps, and a change undone. Real `git worktree`, `git merge`, `lap branch start`, `lap merge`, in a folder under `$TMPDIR` (falling back to `/tmp`), never under the home folder. A third of the cases are nested (b1 from main, b2 from b1), merged in the four orders the audit used (b2→b1→main; b2→main then b1; b2→b1, b2→main, then b1; b2→b1→main then b2→main). Some cases run with a small `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES` so chunks seal mid-case.

**Checked after every merge:**
- no git conflict under `.lap/log/`;
- when git merged cleanly and nothing stopped: `lap status` clean, and the parent's recorded text equals git's merge;
- `lap verify --deep` passes;
- no branch commit, session or amendment adopted twice (each `from` original at most once);
- `--dry-run` changes no byte (tree hash before and after) and predicts exactly what the real merge then does.

**Crash loop.** For a fixed subset of seeds (flat and nested), rerun the merge interrupted after each record (`LAP_TEST_MERGE_FAIL_AFTER=1..n`) and require the rerun's records, ids and shadow to equal the uninterrupted run's.

**Where.** The driver in C, as its own test binary beside the unit tests (it needs a PRNG and to run git; a shell script is awkward for both), built by `make test`; it passes `HOME` and `TMPDIR` inside its own work folder to every git and lap it runs. Removes its own case folders on success (paths it made with `mkdtemp`); keeps a failing one and prints its path. Skipped with a message when git is missing (Windows CI without git).

**Done when:** `make test` runs the 60 seeds and the crash subset, green; `make prop` runs 500, green; replaying a seed is documented in the lap-cli README's test section; a deliberately broken placement (e.g. an off-by-one in the shift, in a scratch build) is caught by at least one seed — say which in the ticket's comment.

item.title: Merge scenarios not covered yet: sibling branches on one file, delete against edit, long-lived branches, nested crashes, merging the parent into a branch
item.description:
**Why.** Reviewing the 73 branch/merge e2e scenarios and the adopt unit tests with the user (2026-09-28) found these hand-picked cases missing. Each becomes a named e2e scenario (real git worktrees, in `$TMPDIR`), with unit tests where the logic is adopt's.

1. **Sibling branches on one file.** a and b from one base both change the same file in different places; merge a, then b: b's commits are placed on top of a's adopted work. And the overlapping variant: b stops where it touches a's change.
2. **Delete against edit.** The branch deletes a file the parent edited (adopt's "it deletes a file the parent changed"), and the parent deletes a file the branch edited: each stops the file, nothing else is lost.
3. **A long-lived branch.** Four rounds of: work on both sides, `git merge`, `lap merge`. Each round adopts only what is new, ids and `from` links stay right, `verify --deep` passes at the end.
4. **Crashes in a nested merge.** The interrupt-after-every-record loop (as in "a merge stopped after any record is redone exactly") for a branch of a branch merged straight into main.
5. **Merging the parent into a branch** (SPEC "Not in this version": merge back, then start a fresh branch). Agents often `git merge main` in a worktree to stay current; pin down what lap does then: the parent's changes show in the branch's `lap status` as its own pending edits. **Decision needed:** at least a warning from lap when a branch folder's files match newer parent commits (e.g. status notes "these changes are main's L…, not yours: merging the parent into a branch is not supported"), and the lap skill says never to commit them. The test fixes whatever is decided.

Also: the unit tests in `test_branches.c` that build `.own_unit_here/`, `.own_unit_there/` and `.deep_unit_b1/` in the current directory (they are left in `cli/lap-cli/`) use a temp folder instead.

**Done when:** the five scenarios (and the temp-folder fix) are in the suites and green; for 5, the decision is recorded here and in the SPEC.

item.title: Board view: a row reads icon, id, title — no status text, the icon says it
item.description:
**Why.** In the Board view's tree a row already shows its status as an icon (todo ○, doing ▶, blocked ⊗, review 👁, done ✓), yet a ticket also spells it out at the end, and the id sits there too, where it is hard to scan. The user wants the id up front, as in T-161 for Lap History.

**Today** (`packages/coboard-vscode/webview/sidebar.tsx:250-253`):

```
○  declare time() on Windows                    T-12 · todo
◇  Robustness, round 2                          M-15
```

icon (`iconOf`), `sb-title`, then `sb-desc` = `T-12 · todo` for a ticket, the id alone for an epic or milestone.

**Wanted** (user, 2026-09-28):

```
○  T-12  declare time() on Windows
◇  M-15  Robustness, round 2
▣  E-15  Views: quality of life
```

- **Order:** the icon, then the id, then the title — for tickets, milestones and epics alike.
- **The id keeps today's look** (the muted `sb-desc` style, not the title's), just moved before the title.
- **No status text:** the icon carries it. The tooltip keeps it (today's `"<id> — <title>\n<kind>, <status>"`), and the status filter is unchanged.

item.title: lap and kb CLIs: help agents can rely on
item.description: Agents drive the CLIs, and they reach for `<command> --help` as they would with any command-line program. The help must exist for every command and never fall behind the code.

item.title: lap and kb: --help on every command, from one source of truth, with a test that it covers every flag
item.description:
**Why.** Agents run `<command> --help` first, as with any CLI. Today neither CLI has it (checked 2026-09-28):

```
$ lap commit --help   → error: unknown flag --help (lap --help lists each command's flags)
$ lap merge -h        → error: unknown flag -h (…)
$ kb search --help    → error: unknown option "--help"
```

Only the top-level `lap --help` and `kb --help` exist. This reverses T-211's cut (it kept per-command `--help` out); the user decided agents need it.

**The help is also slightly behind the code** (every `"--flag"` string in `src/*.c` compared with the top-level help):
- **kb:** `search` accepts `--fusion`, `--rerank-depth` and `--rerank-tokens` (`cli/kb-cli/src/cmd_search.c:39`), which the help never mentions.
- **lap:** `--intent` and `--behavior`, the long forms of `-i`/`-b`, are not in the help.
- Every kb command is listed; every lap command is listed.

**Change, both CLIs:**
- `lap <cmd> --help`, `lap <cmd> -h`, `lap help <cmd>` (and the same for kb, including subcommands such as `kb collections rename`, `lap session start`, `lap branch start`) print that command's help to stdout and exit 0, before any other argument checking or repository lookup (they work outside a repository).
- **One source of truth:** the top-level help and each command's help come from the same table (command, synopsis, flags with one line each), so they cannot drift apart; a usage error prints that command's synopsis from the same table.
- Bring the help up to date: the kb search options above, lap's long forms, and anything else the test below finds.

**The guard that keeps it current:** a test in each CLI's suite that fails when a flag the parser accepts is missing from that command's help (a table of accepted flags per command, compared with the help table; or the parser reads its flags from the help table itself). Adding a flag without help then fails `make test`. T-214's `--intent-only`/`--behavior-only` will be caught by it.

**Done when:** `--help`/`-h`/`help <cmd>` work for every lap and kb command and subcommand (e2e loops over the command list); the coverage test is in both suites and green; the gaps above are filled; the README command tables still match (checked once by hand, said in the comment).

item.title: lap commit never ignores --lines or --edit on a new file
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced, 2026-09-28).** On a file lap has never recorded, `--lines` is silently ignored and the whole file is committed under a message meant for part of it:

```
f.c: f1 (lines 1-3), blank, f2 (5-7), blank, f3 (9-11) — never committed
lap commit f.c --lines 5-7 -i "add f2 alone" -b "f2 returns two to its callers" --no-session
→ [L1 c6dc336] (no session) f.c: lines 1-11 (insertion)  "add f2 alone"     rc 0
```

The message now describes f2 but the commit holds f1, f2 and f3 — for good (only `lap amend` can repair the text). SPEC §`lap commit`: a new file is one `create` of its whole content; nothing says `--lines`/`--edit` are dropped. `--edit N` on a new file is likely ignored the same way (check).

**Fix (until T-221 lands):** on a new file, `--lines` or `--edit` → `bad_lines` / `bad_edit_index`: "f.c is a new file: it is committed whole (no --lines/--edit)". T-221 then gives `--lines` its meaning there.

**Done when:** e2e: both flags on a new file are refused and nothing is written; unit test for the check.

item.title: A new file can be committed in parts (--lines picks any range), and a large one must be
item.description:
**Why (user, 2026-09-28).** Agents create files whole: a first commit of a 300-line file with three functions is one `create` whose message cannot say what each part does. The lap skill only advises building large files in increments; lap does not help. Decided with the user:

**1. `--lines A-B` on a new file creates it with just those lines.**
- Applies only while lap has never recorded the file (the commit would be its `create`). E.g. f1 (1-3), f2 (5-7), f3 (9-11): `lap commit f.c --lines 5-7 …` records a `create` holding f2 only.
- From then on the file is known: `lap status` compares it with that version and lists the rest as ordinary pending edits (f1 above, f3 below), committed with `--edit`/`--lines` as today — where `--lines` keeps its usual meaning (exactly one listed edit's range).
- Blank lines between parts join the neighbouring edit, as lap's diff already merges whitespace-only gap lines; no one-line blank commits.
- Any range is allowed on a new file, not only a region; the recorded create's text is exactly those lines (plus the file's final-newline state if the range ends the file).

**2. A large new file is refused whole by default.**
- A whole-file create of more than **50 lines** (a SPEC constant) → `large_create`: "f.c is a new file of 312 lines: commit it in parts with --lines A-B, or pass --whole-file".
- `--whole-file` commits it whole (a dedicated flag; `--force-message` stays about message checks only). Generated files, fixtures and data that are one piece use it, or belong in `.lapignore`.
- Only creates: a large insertion into a file lap already records stays one edit, as today (not in scope).

**Docs.** SPEC §`lap commit` (the new-file rule, the constant, `large_create`, `--whole-file`), `lap --help`, the lap skill (replace "prefer building it in meaningful increments" with how to commit a new file in parts) and the tickets skill's "A new file is one commit" line.

**Done when:** e2e: the f1/f2/f3 file committed as f2 (`--lines 5-7`), then f1 and f3 as edits, three commits, status clean, `verify --deep` ok; a 51-line create refused, `--whole-file` commits it; a 50-line create goes through; unit tests for the range-to-create logic (a range at the top, the middle, the end with and without a final newline); docs updated.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S215, git 722dc56.

**What's in the suite.** `tests/prop/prop.c` is the driver, built as `bin/lap-prop` (Makefile and CMake, POSIX). `make test` runs seeds 1–60 (about 14 s: cases run side by side in child processes, reported in seed order); `make prop` runs 1–500 (about 100 s).
- **Determinism:** splitmix64 seeded from the seed; nothing from the clock or `rand()`.
- **What a seed decides:**
  - four files;
  - edits covering insert, delete and replace, top and bottom, blank and `dup` lines;
  - the same change made on both sides, a change in two steps, a change undone;
  - branch amendments, and sessions opened and closed.
- **Case mix:** a third of the seeds are nested, in the four orders. A quarter use a small `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES`. Every tenth runs the crash loop on its merge into main. In seeds 1–60 that is 10, 20, 40 and 50 flat, and 30 and 60 nested.
- **Isolation:** HOME and TMPDIR sit inside an mkdtemp folder under `$TMPDIR`. A passing case's folder is removed; a failure prints its seed, keeps its folder and prints `LAP_PROP_SEED=<n> make prop`. `LAP_PROP_TRACE=1` prints every command. With no git, it says it skipped.

**Checked after every merge:**
- no git conflict under `.lap/`;
- `--dry-run` changes no byte (tree hash) and reports exactly what the real merge then reports, ids aside;
- `lap verify --deep` passes;
- no original record reaches the history twice (from links followed back to the original);
- the crash loop: the merge is cut after each record (`LAP_TEST_MERGE_FAIL_AFTER=0..`) and rerun, and the history (times and hashes cut out, ids kept) and the shadows must equal the whole run's.

**Two decisions on the "clean when git was clean" invariant:**
- **Checked per file.** Where git merged cleanly, every file lap did not stop must be recorded as git merged it. As a whole-status check it skipped about 10% of merges, because lap's stopped-for-good rule stops files git merged fine.
- **Skipped when the merge reports `already`.** Seed 333: both sides inserted the same blank line. git merges from a base before both and, among blank lines, kept both insertions. lap records the line once. git's text is no reference there.

**Four lap bugs found and fixed**, each with a named e2e scenario that fails on the old code:
1. **`--dry-run` never counted amendments.** It reported 0 carried and 0 left while the real merge carried them (seeds 1, 2, 4, 5). `amend_target` is now shared, and a dry run counts amendments with the commits it would adopt standing in for their copies. e2e: "lap merge --dry-run counts the amendments…".
2. **A cut chain merge, run again, did not end where the whole run did** (seeds 30 and 450, nested, b2 straight into main). After a cut, the rerun read the outer branch's merge record, which the interrupted run had written, as an earlier merge. It then placed b2's part from a later base. With an already-done change that the parent keeps (T-181), that placement differs.
   - Fix: new `merge_cut_start` finds the trailing merge records the chain wrote for its outer branches at the heads it writes. Earlier merges are read from the history before them, and the rerun does not write them again. Unit tested in test_branches.c.
   - Also, an inner branch's record now names the commit where the outer part stopped the file, as a later merge does. SPEC is updated.
   - e2e: "a nested branch's merge record stops a file at the commit…" and "a chain merge cut after its outer branch's merge record ends, run again, where the whole run does".
3. **A file stopped for b2 was not stopped for b1 after b1 took b2 in** (seed 54). Both made the same change. The parent resolved b2's conflict by keeping its own text, and git keeps it on merging b1. lap placed b1's copy of the change, so status was left dirty.
   - Fix: a file an earlier merge stopped for a branch that the merged stream's own merges took in stays stopped. The reason given is "stopped here for b2, whose work this branch took in".
   - e2e: "a file stopped for a branch stays stopped when another branch brings that branch's work".
4. The driver's own amendment texts could repeat (seeds 526 and 804). That was a driver bug, fixed in the driver.

**Deliberately broken placement.** In a scratch build, `adopt.c` placed commits at `s + offset - (offset > 0)`, off by one whenever the parent's changes above shift the commit. Seed 19 catches it in `make test` (g.txt not recorded as git merged it). Over 500 seeds, 15 catch it. item.title: Merge scenarios not covered yet: sibling branches on one file, delete against edit, long-lived branches, nested crashes; merging the parent into a branch documented as unsupported
item.description:
**Why.** Reviewing the 73 branch/merge e2e scenarios and the adopt unit tests with the user (2026-09-28) found these hand-picked cases missing. Each becomes a named e2e scenario (real git worktrees, in `$TMPDIR`), with unit tests where the logic is adopt's.

1. **Sibling branches on one file.** a and b from one base both change the same file in different places; merge a, then b: b's commits are placed on top of a's adopted work. And the overlapping variant: b stops where it touches a's change.
2. **Delete against edit.** The branch deletes a file the parent edited (adopt's "it deletes a file the parent changed"), and the parent deletes a file the branch edited: each stops the file, nothing else is lost.
3. **A long-lived branch.** Four rounds of: work on both sides, `git merge`, `lap merge`. Each round adopts only what is new, ids and `from` links stay right, `verify --deep` passes at the end.
4. **Crashes in a nested merge.** The interrupt-after-every-record loop (as in "a merge stopped after any record is redone exactly") for a branch of a branch merged straight into main.
5. **Merging the parent into a branch — not supported, documented (decision, user, 2026-09-28).** lap does nothing about it: no detection, no warning, no test. It is stated plainly as a limitation:
   - **lap skill** (Branches section), in the rules an agent follows: never `git merge` the parent (main) into a branch folder to stay current — its changes would show as the branch's own pending edits and, if committed, come back to main as branch work. To take in the parent's newer work: merge the branch back, then start a fresh branch.
   - **tickets skill**, one line where it sends agents to branch folders.
   - **Limitations** of the root README and of `cli/lap-cli/README.md`: the same, in one sentence each, matching SPEC "Not in this version".

Also: the unit tests in `test_branches.c` that build `.own_unit_here/`, `.own_unit_there/` and `.deep_unit_b1/` in the current directory (they are left in `cli/lap-cli/`) use a temp folder instead.

**Done when:** scenarios 1–4 (and the temp-folder fix) are in the suites and green; item 5 is in both skills and both READMEs' limitations, in the same words; nothing in lap changes for item 5.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S216, git cd4b7cc. No lap code changed.

**e2e scenarios** (all green, 190 in total; each case runs in real git worktrees under `$TMPDIR`):
1. **Siblings on one file.** A new helper, `sib_pair`, adds a sibling `a` beside `b`.
   - "…the second's commits land on top of the first's adopted work": a's insertion moves b's line 40 to 41, checked in `lap log`.
   - "…the second stops where it touches the first's adopted change": b's line 21, next to a's line 20, stops f.txt ("overlaps or touches"). b's earlier commit and its g.txt work are adopted, and the leftover is committed by hand to a clean status.
2. **Delete against edit, both ways.** In each case the file stops and the branch's other file is adopted.
   - The branch deletes g.txt that the parent edited. The parent keeps g.txt; `adopted 1, left 1`.
   - The parent deletes g.txt that the branch edited. The reason is "the parent deleted the file" and g.txt stays gone.
3. **A long-lived branch, four rounds.** Each round adopts exactly one new commit with the predicted id (L6, L8, L10, L12). Each copy's `from` equals the branch commit's hash, each behavior is in the history once, and `verify --deep` passes at the end.
4. **Nested crash loop.** "a branch of a branch merged straight into main and cut after any record…": b2 is merged straight into main and cut after each record. Every rerun matches the whole run's history (times and hashes cut out), is clean and passes `verify --deep`. T-216's n9 scenario covers the already-done variant.

**adopt unit tests** (test_adopt.c): a sibling's commits placed past the other sibling's adopted work; the touching variant stopping with the earlier commit kept; the branch deleting a file the parent edited (stops, parent's text kept); the parent deleting a file the branch edited (stops, stays deleted).

**Fixtures.** `test_branches.c` builds `deep_unit_b1`, `own_unit_here` and `own_unit_there` under `$TMPDIR` (named with the pid; the current folder on Windows) and removes them afterwards. I removed the old empty copies from `cli/lap-cli/` by their literal names.

**Item 5**, one paragraph, word for word, in the lap skill (Branches), the tickets skill (beside "Bringing a branch folder's work back") and both READMEs' Limitations. It matches SPEC "Not in this version":
> **Merging the parent into a branch is not supported.** Never `git merge` the parent (main) into a branch folder to stay current: its changes would show as the branch's own pending edits and, if committed, come back to the parent as branch work. To take in the parent's newer work, merge the branch back, then start a fresh branch.

The ticket asked for one line in the tickets skill. I used the whole paragraph so the words are the same everywhere.

**Tests:** unit 4660, e2e 190, prop seeds 1–60 ok.

item.title: Docs: the test suites need git, and without it the merge tests are skipped yet the run is green
item.description:

- e2e: `tests/e2e/run.sh:1353` runs the branch scenarios only when `command -v git` finds git; otherwise `:3239` prints `skip: git not found, the branch scenarios did not run`.

- Already documented: `cli/lap-cli/README.md` says the generated cases need git and skip without it, and that e2e and those cases run on macOS and Linux only.

**Missing — add:**
1. **Root `README.md`, Requirements:** git is needed to run the tests (not to use lap); without it the branch and merge tests are skipped.
2. **`cli/lap-cli/README.md`, the test section:** the e2e branch scenarios also need git and skip without it (only the generated cases are mentioned today); and the warning: **a skip counts as a pass** — a run on a machine without git is green without having tested any merge, so CI must have git installed.

**Done when:** the three places say it, in the same words; nothing in lap or the tests changes.

item.title: Review timeline: edits open beside the review, one group, a new tab per click
item.description:
**Today.** Clicking an edit in a session's review timeline opens its diff (`showEdit`, `packages/coboard-vscode/src/extension.ts:380-392`) with `vscode.diff` and `preview: true`, in the active editor group — it covers the review tab, and each click replaces the previous diff.

**Wanted:** the review and the diffs side by side.
- **First click:** open the diff in an editor group **to the right of the review** (`ViewColumn.Beside` relative to the review panel's column), creating that group if there is none.
- **Next clicks:** open in **that same right-hand group**, each as a **new tab** (`preview: false`), so several edits can be kept open next to the review. Never a third column; never the review's own group.
- If the user closed the right-hand group or moved the review, the next click again opens beside the review.
- Clicking an edit whose diff is already open in that group focuses its tab instead of opening a duplicate.
- The review panel keeps focus behaviour sensible: the diff is shown without stealing the review's scroll position (use `preserveFocus` where it helps).

**Done when:** tested in the Extension Development Host: first click opens beside, the second adds a tab in the same group, re-clicking focuses the existing tab, closing the group and clicking again reopens beside; the existing review tests pass.

author: claude
body:
Implemented in lap session S221, git d2458b7. **The Extension Development Host check in *Done when* was not done** (see below).

**What changed**
- Clicking an edit opens its diff in the column just **right of the panel that asked**: `panel.viewColumn + 1`, which VS Code creates when no such group exists.
- Every later click lands in that same group. Diffs open as kept tabs (`preview: false`), never in the review's own group and never in a new third column.
- The target is worked out from where the panel is *now*. So if the diff group was closed, or the review was moved, the next click opens beside the review again.
- `preserveFocus: true` when a panel asked, so the review keeps focus and its scroll position while you click down the timeline.
- **Re-clicking an edit** opens the same diff input in the same group. VS Code brings the existing tab forward rather than duplicating it, so there is no explicit tab search.
- **A link inside a diff's comment** (`coboard.showEdit`, no panel) opens in the group the last diff landed in while it is still open, otherwise beside the active editor, and takes focus. Where the last diff landed is read back from `window.tabGroups`.
- This applies to the ticket page's commit list too, since it sends the same `showEdit` message as the review. That seemed the consistent choice.
- The rule is a pure `diffColumn()` in the new `src/placement.ts`.

**Tests**
- `placement.test.ts` (3 tests): first click, next clicks, closed group, moved review, unknown column, links inside a diff.
- The host test's fake `vscode` now models editor groups. It checks column 2 with preview off and focus kept, the same edit not duplicated, a second edit as a second tab in the same group, and a link inside a diff reusing the group, then opening beside once the group is gone.
- coboard-vscode: 45/45.

**Not verified:** clicking in a real Extension Development Host. The fake only mimics VS Code, so real behaviour still needs a manual check: that `vscode.diff` with an explicit column one past the last group creates it on the right, and that re-opening focuses the existing tab. Please run the four clicks from *Done when* in the EDH.

item.title: lap and kb: --help on every command, from one source of truth, with a test that it covers every flag
item.description:
**Why.** Agents run `<command> --help` first, as with any CLI. Today neither CLI has it (checked 2026-09-28):

```
$ lap commit --help   → error: unknown flag --help (lap --help lists each command's flags)
$ lap merge -h        → error: unknown flag -h (…)
$ kb search --help    → error: unknown option "--help"
```

Only the top-level `lap --help` and `kb --help` exist. This reverses T-211's cut (it kept per-command `--help` out); the user decided agents need it.

**The help is also slightly behind the code** (every `"--flag"` string in `src/*.c` compared with the top-level help):
- **kb:** `search` accepts `--fusion`, `--rerank-depth` and `--rerank-tokens` (`cli/kb-cli/src/cmd_search.c:39`), which the help never mentions.
- **lap:** `--intent` and `--behavior`, the long forms of `-i`/`-b`, are not in the help.
- Every kb command is listed; every lap command is listed.

**Change, both CLIs:**
- `lap <cmd> --help`, `lap <cmd> -h`, `lap help <cmd>` (and the same for kb, including subcommands such as `kb collections rename`, `lap session start`, `lap branch start`) print that command's help to stdout and exit 0, before any other argument checking or repository lookup (they work outside a repository).
- **One source of truth:** the top-level help and each command's help come from the same table (command, synopsis, flags with one line each), so they cannot drift apart; a usage error prints that command's synopsis from the same table.
- Bring the help up to date: the kb search options above, lap's long forms, and anything else the test below finds.

**The guard that keeps it current:** a test in each CLI's suite that fails when a flag the parser accepts is missing from that command's help (a table of accepted flags per command, compared with the help table; or the parser reads its flags from the help table itself). Adding a flag without help then fails `make test`. T-214's `--intent-only`/`--behavior-only` will be caught by it.

**Done when:** `--help`/`-h`/`help <cmd>` work for every lap and kb command and subcommand (e2e loops over the command list); the coverage test is in both suites and green; the gaps above are filled; the README command tables still match (checked once by hand, said in the comment).

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S222, git 9033310.

**What changed, both CLIs**
- `<cmd> --help`, `<cmd> -h` and `help <cmd> [<sub>]` print that command's synopsis, a summary and every flag with one line each, to stdout, exit 0. They answer before any other checking and need no repository or store. `-h` given as a flag's value (`kb ls --q -h`) or after `--` is not treated as help.
- A group (`lap session`, `lap branch`, `kb collections`, `kb sources`, `kb links`) answers for the subcommand named on the line (`lap session start --meta x -h`), or else for itself, listing its subcommands.
- **One source of truth:** `src/help.c` in each CLI holds a table of every command and subcommand with its synopsis, summary, flags (both spellings) and handler. From it come:
  - top-level `--help`;
  - per-command `--help`;
  - the dispatch in `main` (the strcmp chains are gone);
  - **the flags each command accepts**: the parser reads its value and switch lists from the table, so a flag missing from the help is refused at runtime;
  - usage synopses. lap's `usage:` errors print the table's synopsis, and for a group, all its subcommands' joined by ` | `. kb's specific usage messages are kept (its e2e matches them); in human mode the running command's synopsis now follows on the next line. JSON errors are unchanged in both.
- **Gaps filled:** kb `search --fusion`, `--rerank-depth`, `--rerank-tokens`; lap `--intent`/`--behavior`. kb's camelCase spellings (`--olderThan`, `--minScore`) are listed as aliases, since the parser accepts them. kb's help also no longer suggests `6m` for `--older-than`: `m` is minutes there.
- lap's unknown-flag message now reads `unknown flag X (the command's --help lists its flags)`.

**Guards**
- Unit (`tests/unit/test_help.c` in each CLI): every entry has a synopsis, a summary and a line per flag; every flag is named in a synopsis that `--help` prints; a group accepts its subcommands' flags (lap: exactly them); the dispatch invariants; flag sets carry both spellings; `--help` is not read from a flag's value or after `--`.
- e2e: loops over every command, alias and subcommand × `--help`/`-h`/`help`, outside a repository or store: exit 0, stdout only, starts with `usage:`, has `flags:`, creates nothing. Plus a **source scan**: every flag literal in each `src/cmd_*.c` must appear in the `--help` of a command that file runs. I checked the scan with one planted fake flag per file: all 13 lap files and all 14 kb files were caught, with no real misses.

**Tests**
- lap `make test`: unit 5005/5005, e2e 192 scenarios with 0 failures, prop seeds 1–60 ok.
- kb, with `HOME` in the scratchpad: unit 3095/3095, e2e 183 with 0 failures.
- Both CMake builds compile.
- The packages that drive the CLIs also pass: kb-js 128 (it checks its spellings against `kb --help`), kb-mcp 147, coboard 45, lap-vscode 74, coboard-vscode 45.

**Docs:** new paragraphs in `cli/lap-cli/README.md`, `cli/lap-cli/SPEC.md` (Commands) and `specs/index-api.md` §11. I checked the lap README command table by hand against the table: same commands, and the flags it names are all still valid (it names highlights, by design). kb has no README command table in this repo.

**Not done:** T-214's `--intent-only`/`--behavior-only` don't exist yet. When they're added to a parser without a table entry, both the runtime check and the scan will refuse them. The installed `/usr/local/bin/lap` and `kb` are still the old builds; installing is yours.

item.title: lap and kb: --help on every command, from one source of truth, with a test that it covers every flag
item.description:
**Why.** Agents run `<command> --help` first, as with any CLI. Today neither CLI has it (checked 2026-09-28):

```
$ lap commit --help   → error: unknown flag --help (lap --help lists each command's flags)
$ lap merge -h        → error: unknown flag -h (…)
$ kb search --help    → error: unknown option "--help"
```

Only the top-level `lap --help` and `kb --help` exist. This reverses T-211's cut (it kept per-command `--help` out); the user decided agents need it.

**The help is also slightly behind the code** (every `"--flag"` string in `src/*.c` compared with the top-level help):
- **kb:** `search` accepts `--fusion`, `--rerank-depth` and `--rerank-tokens` (`cli/kb-cli/src/cmd_search.c:39`), which the help never mentions.
- **lap:** `--intent` and `--behavior`, the long forms of `-i`/`-b`, are not in the help.
- Every kb command is listed; every lap command is listed.

**Change, both CLIs:**
- `lap <cmd> --help`, `lap <cmd> -h`, `lap help <cmd>` (and the same for kb, including subcommands such as `kb collections rename`, `lap session start`, `lap branch start`) print that command's help to stdout and exit 0, before any other argument checking or repository lookup (they work outside a repository).
- **One source of truth:** the top-level help and each command's help come from the same table (command, synopsis, flags with one line each), so they cannot drift apart; a usage error prints that command's synopsis from the same table.
- Bring the help up to date: the kb search options above, lap's long forms, and anything else the test below finds.

**The guard that keeps it current:** a test in each CLI's suite that fails when a flag the parser accepts is missing from that command's help (a table of accepted flags per command, compared with the help table; or the parser reads its flags from the help table itself). Adding a flag without help then fails `make test`. T-214's `--intent-only`/`--behavior-only` will be caught by it.

**Done when:** `--help`/`-h`/`help <cmd>` work for every lap and kb command and subcommand (e2e loops over the command list); the coverage test is in both suites and green; the gaps above are filled; the README command tables still match (checked once by hand, said in the comment).

item.title: lap commit never ignores --lines or --edit on a new file
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced, 2026-09-28).** On a file lap has never recorded, `--lines` is silently ignored and the whole file is committed under a message meant for part of it:

```
f.c: f1 (lines 1-3), blank, f2 (5-7), blank, f3 (9-11) — never committed
lap commit f.c --lines 5-7 -i "add f2 alone" -b "f2 returns two to its callers" --no-session
→ [L1 c6dc336] (no session) f.c: lines 1-11 (insertion)  "add f2 alone"     rc 0
```

The message now describes f2 but the commit holds f1, f2 and f3 — for good (only `lap amend` can repair the text). SPEC §`lap commit`: a new file is one `create` of its whole content; nothing says `--lines`/`--edit` are dropped. `--edit N` on a new file is likely ignored the same way (check).

**Fix (until T-221 lands):** on a new file, `--lines` or `--edit` → `bad_lines` / `bad_edit_index`: "f.c is a new file: it is committed whole (no --lines/--edit)". T-221 then gives `--lines` its meaning there.

**Done when:** e2e: both flags on a new file are refused and nothing is written; unit test for the check; **Docs & skills must be updated as well:** the SPEC's `lap commit` section, the lap-cli README and the lap skill say it — the ticket is not done without them.

procode: Add Skills for Claude Code — the extension ships the skills and adds them to the project's .claude/skills, never replacing others
item.description:
**Why (user, 2026-09-28).** **procode: Set Up MCP for Claude Code** (`procode.setUpClaudeMcp`, `packages/combined/scripts/build.mjs:89`, `src/extension.ts`, `src/claude.ts`) gives Claude the tools; nothing gives it the skills that teach it to use them — today users copy `.claude/skills/*` by hand (root README). A second command does that.

**Build.** `packages/combined/scripts/build.mjs` copies the repository's skills (`.claude/skills/lap`, `tickets`, `artifacts` — eggzibit's after T-213 — with every file in each folder, e.g. `lap/references/` after T-227) into the extension package, so the shipped skills always match the extension's version of the tools.

**The command: procode: Add Skills for Claude Code** (declared like `setUpClaudeMcp`, category procode).
- **Pick list** (multi-select) of the shipped skills: lap and artifacts ticked by default; **tickets unticked** (it is this repository's workflow, which the README says to adapt).
- **Writes into the open project's `.claude/skills/<name>/`** (the workspace folder, as the MCP command picks it); creates `.claude/` and `.claude/skills/` when absent. **Project only** — never `~/.claude` (as the MCP command, whose user scope was removed).
- **Adds, never replaces others:** other skills, and everything else in `.claude/` (settings, other users' files), are left untouched; only folders named like ours are written.
- **One of ours already there:** never overwritten silently. If it is identical, nothing to do. Otherwise ask per skill: **Update** (replace the folder with the shipped one), **Keep mine**, **Show differences** (open a diff of `SKILL.md`, then ask again).
- A closing message says what was added, updated or kept, and to restart Claude Code (or run `/skills`) to pick them up.

**Versions and the update notice.**
- Each skill's frontmatter carries `metadata: version: "<n>"` (the Agent Skills spec's `metadata` field; T-228 adds its checks), bumped when a skill changes.
- On activation, like the stale `.mcp.json` warning (`src/extension.ts:174`), the extension compares the project's copies of our skills with the shipped ones: a lower version whose content otherwise matches an older shipped one → "Newer procode skills are available" with **Update**; a copy the user edited is only mentioned, never replaced without asking.

**Done when:**
- `build.mjs` packages the skills (all files of each folder); `check.mjs` asserts they are in the package and that the command is declared;
- tests (with the `vscode` stand-in) for: a project with no `.claude/` (created, chosen skills written); a `.claude/` holding other skills and settings (untouched); an identical copy of ours (nothing done); a different copy (asked; Update replaces, Keep mine leaves it); tickets not written unless picked; nothing written outside the workspace folder;
- the update notice appears for an older shipped version and not for a user-edited copy;
- `npm run package --workspace combined` passes;
- **Docs & skills must be updated as well:** the root README's skills paragraph and Build and install step 3 (Agents) name the command beside the MCP one; each skill gets its `metadata.version` — the ticket is not done without them.

item.title: Knowledge sidebar opens on the collections (paged); a collection opens its documents with their details
item.description:
**Why (user, 2026-09-28).** Clicking the Knowledge icon should show the collections, not a flat list of every document; a collection then opens its documents with their details. Collections are reached today through a separate button and editor tab (`kb:/collections`).

**Today.** `packages/index-vscode/webview/Sidebar.tsx`: a search `Input` and a collection `Select`; with no query, every document newest first — a written decision, `specs/index-ui.md` §2 ("browsing is the default state"). `webview/Collections.tsx`: the `kb:/collections` editor page (counts, bytes, oldest fetch, via `src/view/facts.ts`), the only place rename and delete live (§4, "and nowhere else").

**Wanted (decided with the user):**
1. **Sidebar default = the collections**, each row with its document count, size and last fetch (the rows `Collections.tsx`/`facts.ts` already compute). **The search bar stays on top:** with a query, results — across the store, or within the collection that is open; without one, the collections (or the open collection's documents).
2. **A collection opens its documents in the sidebar** (a back control returns to the collections). Each row shows the document's **name/title, size, type, fetched date**, and a **description** when there is one: taken from `meta` (e.g. a paper's abstract, or a `description` key) — documents have no description field (`packages/kb-js/src/types.ts:44`: title, path, locator, mime, bytes, fetchedAt, indexedAt, chunkCount, meta); no new kb field in this ticket. Clicking a document opens it as today.
3. **Delete stays safe.** Rename and delete are not on the sidebar's rows (the spec's reason stands: one mis-click from losing a topic). They stay on the Collections page, reached by a link at the top of the collections list.
4. **Paging.** `kb ls` has only `--limit` (`cli/kb-cli/src/cmd_ls.c:24`), no way to continue. Add a cursor to kb — `kb ls --after <D-n>` (documents after that one in the list's order), and the same for collections if their list can grow long — carried through kb-js to the view. The sidebar pages with **"Load more"** at the bottom (not page numbers), for both the collections and a collection's documents.

**Spec.** `specs/index-ui.md` §2 (sidebar) and §4 (collections) rewritten for the new default and navigation; `specs/index-api.md` documents the cursor.

**Done when:**
- kb: `--after` on `kb ls` with unit/e2e tests (stable order, a cursor past the end, a deleted cursor document), in `kb --help` (T-219's table);
- kb-js: the cursor in the list call, with a test;
- index-vscode: tests for the view model (collections default, open a collection, back, search in and out of a collection, Load more, description from `meta` or none); rendered light and dark in a narrow sidebar;
- rename and delete reachable only from the Collections page, as before;
- **Docs & skills must be updated as well:** `specs/index-ui.md` §2 and §4, `specs/index-api.md`, the root README's KB paragraph, and the lap/tickets skills only if they describe the Knowledge view — the ticket is not done without them.

item.title: A new file can be committed in parts (--lines picks any range), and a large one must be
item.description:
**Why (user, 2026-09-28).** Agents create files whole: a first commit of a 300-line file with three functions is one `create` whose message cannot say what each part does. The lap skill only advises building large files in increments; lap does not help. Decided with the user:

**1. `--lines A-B` on a new file creates it with just those lines.**
- Applies only while lap has never recorded the file (the commit would be its `create`). E.g. f1 (1-3), f2 (5-7), f3 (9-11): `lap commit f.c --lines 5-7 …` records a `create` holding f2 only.
- From then on the file is known: `lap status` compares it with that version and lists the rest as ordinary pending edits (f1 above, f3 below), committed with `--edit`/`--lines` as today — where `--lines` keeps its usual meaning (exactly one listed edit's range).
- Blank lines between parts join the neighbouring edit, as lap's diff already merges whitespace-only gap lines; no one-line blank commits.
- Any range is allowed on a new file, not only a region; the recorded create's text is exactly those lines (plus the file's final-newline state if the range ends the file).

**2. A large new file is refused whole by default.**
- A whole-file create of more than **50 lines** (a SPEC constant) → `large_create`: "f.c is a new file of 312 lines: commit it in parts with --lines A-B, or pass --whole-file".
- `--whole-file` commits it whole (a dedicated flag; `--force-message` stays about message checks only). Generated files, fixtures and data that are one piece use it, or belong in `.lapignore`.
- Only creates: a large insertion into a file lap already records stays one edit, as today (not in scope).

**Done when (all required — the ticket is not done with code alone):**
- **Tests:** e2e: the f1/f2/f3 file committed as f2 (`--lines 5-7`), then f1 and f3 as edits, three commits, status clean, `verify --deep` ok; a 51-line create refused, `--whole-file` commits it; a 50-line create goes through. Unit tests for the range-to-create logic (a range at the top, the middle, the end with and without a final newline).
- **SPEC** (`cli/lap-cli/SPEC.md`): §`lap commit` states the new-file rule (`--lines` on a create, any range), the 50-line constant, `large_create` and `--whole-file`; the error-code table lists `large_create`.
- **Skills:** the lap skill replaces "prefer building it in meaningful increments" with how to commit a new file in parts (`--lines`, then the rest as edits; `--whole-file` only for files that are one piece); the tickets skill's "A new file is one commit" line says the same in one sentence.
- **READMEs:** `cli/lap-cli/README.md` (the commit section and its command table) and the root `README.md` wherever it describes committing, updated to match; `lap --help` lists `--whole-file` and the new-file meaning of `--lines`.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S225, git d84b596.

**Behaviour**
- **`--lines A-B` on a new file** records a `create` of exactly lines A–B, any range inside the file (`bad_lines` otherwise). The part ends with a newline unless B is the file's last line, where it takes the file's own final-newline state. From then on the rest shows as ordinary pending edits (blank gap lines join their neighbours, as the diff already does), committed with `--edit`/`--lines` as usual. Storage needed no change: the shadow is built by replaying the record's lines onto an empty file, so a partial create replays like any other.
- **Large creates:** a whole create of more than 50 lines (`LAP_LARGE_CREATE_LINES` in `lap.h`) is refused with `large_create` and the ticket's message. `--whole-file` commits it anyway.
- **`--whole-file` elsewhere** (with `--lines`/`--edit`, or on a file that isn't new) is refused as `usage` rather than ignored, in line with T-220.
- `--edit` stays refused on a new file; a deleted file refuses both flags (from T-220).

**Tests**
- Unit (`test_args.c`): `create_part` at the top, the middle and the end, with and without a final newline, plus the whole file and three out-of-range cases; `whole_file_pick_error` now passes `--lines` on a create.
- e2e: f2 created with `--lines 5-7` (op `create`, shadow is f2 alone, 2 pending edits), then f1 and f3 as edits: three commits, nothing pending for f.c, `verify --deep` ok. Also: an out-of-range `--lines` and `--edit` on a new file are refused and write nothing; `--lines` on a delete is refused; 51 lines are refused and go through with `--whole-file`; 50 lines go through; `--whole-file` with `--lines` and on an edit are refused.
- Two fixtures that seed large files (the many-files scenario's 150-line files, `merge_pair`'s 60-line `f.txt`) now pass `--whole-file`.
- Results: lap unit 5027/5027, e2e 195 with 0 failures, prop seeds 1–60 ok. The packages that drive lap (coboard 45, lap-vscode 74, coboard-vscode 45) pass unchanged.

**Docs & skills:** SPEC §`lap commit` (the new-file rule, the 50-line constant, `large_create`, `--whole-file`; heading and error table incl. `large_create`); the lap skill ("build in increments" replaced by committing in parts); the tickets skill's new-file sentence; lap-cli README (Use section example and the command row); root README; `lap commit --help` (`--whole-file` line, the new-file meaning of `--lines`, the synopsis).

**Note:** this changes how agents (me included) create files. A new file over 50 lines now needs `--lines` parts or `--whole-file`, or lap refuses the commit.

item.title: lap log shows each commit's intent and behavior, with --intent-only and --behavior-only
item.description:
**Why.** An agent reviewing history had to read the chunk files by hand: "lap log prints the intent, not the behavior, so I'll check the chunk file instead." The behavior is half of every commit's message, and the text log hides it.

**Today (checked):**
```
$ lap log -n 1
L7     795ad3e 2026-09-28 11:19:44  -      edit     g.txt  line 2 (insertion)
       g edit for the test                     ← intent only
```
`lap log --json` carries both (`intent`, `behavior`); `lap show` prints both; `lap search` prints both. SPEC:876-878 describes the log line as "… intent summary".

**Change.**
- Text `lap log` prints both under each commit line, as `lap show` labels them, one line each (first line of each text, as today's summary):
  ```
  L7     795ad3e 2026-09-28 11:19:44  -      edit     g.txt  line 2 (insertion)
         intent:   g edit for the test
         behavior: the test file changes: g edit
  ```
- `--intent-only` and `--behavior-only` print just that one (the intent line then looks as it does today, without the label); both together → `bad_args`. `--json` unchanged (always both).
- An amended commit shows its latest texts, as today.
- SPEC `lap log`, `lap --help`, the lap skill (where it tells agents how to read history) and the lap-cli README updated.

**Done when:** e2e for the default, `--intent-only`, `--behavior-only`, both flags together (`bad_args`), and an amended commit; unit test for the formatting.

item.title: Docs: the test suites need git, and without it the merge tests are skipped yet the run is green
item.description:
**Why (user, 2026-09-28).** The branch and merge tests build real repositories with git; without git they skip, and a skip counts as a pass, so `make test`/`ctest` come out green having checked no merge. lap itself never needs git at run time.

**Checked:**
- e2e: `tests/e2e/run.sh:1353` runs the branch scenarios only when `command -v git` finds git; otherwise `:3239` prints `skip: git not found, the branch scenarios did not run`.
- generated merge cases: `tests/prop/prop.c:941` prints `lap-prop: skipped: git is not installed`. CMake registers them on POSIX only (`cli/lap-cli/CMakeLists.txt`, "it runs git through a shell").
- Already documented: `cli/lap-cli/README.md` says the generated cases need git and skip without it, and that e2e and those cases run on macOS and Linux only.

**Missing — add:**
1. **Root `README.md`, Requirements:** git is needed to run the tests (not to use lap); without it the branch and merge tests are skipped.
2. **`cli/lap-cli/README.md`, the test section:** the e2e branch scenarios also need git and skip without it (only the generated cases are mentioned today); and the warning: **a skip counts as a pass** — a run on a machine without git is green without having tested any merge, so CI must have git installed.
3. **Root `README.md`, Build and install**, next to `ctest --test-dir build`: one line pointing at that warning.

**Done when:** the three places say it, in the same words; nothing in lap or the tests changes.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S229, git b46aa20.

- **`compatibility` lines** in the three skills' frontmatter:
  - lap: "Requires the lap CLI (cli/lap-cli) on PATH."

  - artifacts: "Requires the artifacts MCP server (packages/artifacts)." T-213 will rename it.
- **`scripts/skills.mjs`** has two pieces:
  - A flat frontmatter reader: `key: value` lines, a `metadata:` block and quoted values; anything else is reported, not guessed. There is no YAML dependency.
  - `checkSkill(dir)`, which reports problems as sentences. It checks the `---` frontmatter, the name (1–64 characters, `a-z0-9` with single hyphens, equal to the folder), the description (1–1024), `compatibility` (1–500), metadata values being strings, and a body under 500 lines. Every relative link outside code fences must stay in the folder, go at most one folder deep, and point to a file that exists.
- **`scripts/skills.test.mjs`**, run first by the root `npm test` (`package.json`):
  - The real skills pass and each has a compatibility line.
  - Fixture skills in a temp folder fail as they should: bad name, name unlike its folder, a 1025-character description, missing / outside / too-deep links, a 501-character compatibility, no frontmatter, a 500-line body.
  - `links()` skips URLs, anchors and fenced code.
  - `skills-ref validate` runs when it's on `PATH`; it isn't here, so that test reports a skip, as intended. So `skills-ref` itself was not run.

Knowledge's search bar looks like the Board's and Lap History's filter bars
item.description:
**Why (user, 2026-09-28).** The filter bar's background in Knowledge does not match the rest.

**Checked.** Board and Lap History share one bar: a 24px row on the input background with a 1px input border, a focus border, the filters chevron, the field and the clear cross (`packages/coboard-vscode/assets/board.css:334` `.sb-bar`, `packages/lap-vscode/assets/lap.css:31` `.lh-bar`; markup `coboard-vscode/webview/sidebar.tsx:80`, `lap-vscode/webview/history.tsx:121`). Knowledge builds its own from baukasten's `Input` and `Select` (`packages/index-vscode/webview/Sidebar.tsx:238-289`), laid out by `.kb-bar` (`index-vscode/assets/knowledge.css:89`, sticky, padded, wrapping), so its field, background and height differ.

**Change.** Knowledge's search uses the same bar as the other two: same background, border, height, focus border and clear cross, built from the same styles (the two views' identical CSS could move into one shared stylesheet while at it). Keep what Knowledge needs: the collection choice (as the bar's filters chevron, the way Board and Lap History put their field filters there, or kept beside the bar in the same style — pick whichever reads better, say which), the search-as-you-type behaviour, and the wrap at narrow widths.

**Done when:** the three bars rendered side by side (headless Chrome over the real bundles, light and dark) look the same; Knowledge's search and collection filter work as before (existing tests green, one for the collection choice if it moves).

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S230, git c1c9f75.

**The background you saw:** `.kb-bar` painted `--bk-color-background`, which baukasten maps to `--vscode-editor-background`, while the page and the other two bars show the sidebar's colour. The bar now has no fill of its own, and its bottom line is the divider the other bars use. `.kb-scroll` is the scroller and the bar sits outside it, so nothing passes under it.

**The bar:** Knowledge's search is now drawn like `.lh-bar`/`.sb-bar`: 24px, input background, 1px input border, the focus colour on `:focus-within`. The field is a plain borderless `<input>` instead of baukasten's `Input`, and the ✕ sits inline in the bar at the right, muted, foreground on hover. Search-as-you-type, Escape to clear, and the wrap at narrow widths (`.kb-bar` still wraps) are unchanged.

**The collection choice:** kept beside the bar as a `Select`, the way Lap History keeps its time range. Knowledge has no field filters, so there's no chevron; a chevron that only opened one choice would read worse.
- I measured the rendered controls: Knowledge's `Select` was 20.5px tall with 9.75px text, against Lap History's 24px and 12px. Knowledge's root font is 13px and baukasten sizes the control in rem.
- Rather than change the root, which would resize every rem control in Knowledge's views, `.kb-narrow [role="combobox"]` is set to 24px and 12px.
- The dropdown's menu is still rem-sized, since it's portalled outside the bar.

item.title: Pages carry keywords: set on publish (MCP), listed and filtered by them
item.description:

**MCP.** (`packages/artifacts/src/mcp.ts`; names become eggzibit's with T-213, whichever lands first)

item.title: MCP definitions refresh when the CLI settings or the workspace folders change
Check the CLI before VS Code starts the coboard or kb MCP server
item.description:
The kb server needs `kb`, and coboard's lap-backed tools need `lap`. When the CLI a setting names cannot be found, the server still starts, and the agent only meets the failure on its first tool call.

Implement `resolveMcpServerDefinition` (called just before a server starts, and allowed to interact with the user). For kb and coboard, resolve the CLI with the existing `resolveCli`, as `checkClis` does. When it is missing, show the same message `checkClis` shows (`missingMessage`, with **Open Setting**).

To decide in the ticket, and record in the closing comment:
- **kb without `kb`:** stop the server (return undefined) — every one of its tools needs the CLI.
- **coboard without `lap`:** start it anyway and only warn — the board works without lap; only `board_sessions` needs it.
- **artifacts:** needs no CLI; returned unchanged.

**Done when:**
- `check.mjs` covers a missing `kb` (not started, message shown), a missing `lap` (started, warned), and both present (started, no message);
- `npm run package --workspace combined` passes;
- **Docs & skills must be updated as well:** the READMEs (Build and install, what happens when a CLI is missing) and the skills wherever they describe it — the ticket is not done without them.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S237, git 9613f90.

**Decisions:** kept as the ticket proposed. They're recorded in `serverNeeds` in `clis.ts`.
- **kb without `kb`:** the server isn't started (`resolveMcpServerDefinition` returns `undefined`), because every one of its tools needs the CLI.
- **coboard without `lap`:** started anyway, with the warning; the board works without lap, and only its sessions need it.
- **artifacts:** needs no CLI and is returned unchanged.

**How:**
- The provider's `resolveMcpServerDefinition` finds the server by its label and looks up the CLI it needs, resolving the setting's command with the existing `resolveCli`. When the CLI is missing it shows the same `missingMessage` with **Open Setting** as the startup check.

**check.mjs:**

- A fake `kb` and `lap` in the temp folder make "present" independent of the machine's PATH.
- Both present: all three servers resolve as defined and nothing is said.
- `kb` missing: kb's resolves to nothing, with one warning naming `/nowhere/kb`; coboard's and artifacts' start.
- `lap` missing: coboard's starts, with one warning naming `/nowhere/lap`; kb's is unaffected.
- Result: 35 commands, 3 MCP servers, no errors.

`npm run package --workspace combined` passes.

**Docs:** the README's install step says a missing CLI is reported once per window and again before VS Code starts the server that needs it, and what happens to each server. No skill describes this.

**Not verified:** in a real VS Code. `resolveMcpServerDefinition` is VS Code's hook, and only the stand-in exercised it here.
