item.title: procode: Add Skills for Claude Code — the extension ships the skills and adds them to the project's .claude/skills, never replacing others
item.description:
**Why (user, 2026-09-28).** **procode: Set Up MCP for Claude Code** (`procode.setUpClaudeMcp`, `packages/combined/scripts/build.mjs:89`, `src/extension.ts`, `src/claude.ts`) gives Claude the tools; nothing gives it the skills that teach it to use them — today users copy `.claude/skills/*` by hand (root README). A second command does that.

**Build.** `packages/combined/scripts/build.mjs` copies the repository's skills (`.claude/skills/lap`, `tickets`, `artifacts` — eggzibit's after T-213 — with every file in each folder, e.g. `lap/references/` after T-227) into the extension package, so the shipped skills always match the extension's version of the tools.

**The command: procode: Add Skills for Claude Code** (declared like `setUpClaudeMcp`, category procode).
- **Pick list** (multi-select) of the shipped skills: lap and artifacts ticked by default; **tickets unticked** (it is this repository's workflow, which the README says to adapt).
- **Writes into the open project's `.claude/skills/<name>/`** (the workspace folder, as the MCP command picks it); creates `.claude/` and `.claude/skills/` when absent. **Project only** — never `~/.claude` (as the MCP command, whose user scope was removed).
- **Adds, never replaces others:** other skills, and everything else in `.claude/` (settings, other users' files), are left untouched; only folders named like ours are written.
- **One of ours already there:** never overwritten silently. If it is identical, nothing to do. Otherwise ask per skill: **Update** (replace the folder with the shipped one), **Keep mine**, **Show differences** (open a diff of `SKILL.md`, then ask again).
- A closing message says what was added, updated or kept, and to restart Claude Code (or run `/skills`) to pick them up.

**Versions and the update notice.**
- Each skill's frontmatter carries `metadata: version: "<n>"` (the Agent Skills spec's `metadata` field; T-228 adds its checks), bumped when a skill changes.
- On activation, like the stale `.mcp.json` warning (`src/extension.ts:174`), the extension compares the project's copies of our skills with the shipped ones: a lower version whose content otherwise matches an older shipped one → "Newer procode skills are available" with **Update**; a copy the user edited is only mentioned, never replaced without asking.

**Done when:**
- `build.mjs` packages the skills (all files of each folder); `check.mjs` asserts they are in the package and that the command is declared;
- tests (with the `vscode` stand-in) for: a project with no `.claude/` (created, chosen skills written); a `.claude/` holding other skills and settings (untouched); an identical copy of ours (nothing done); a different copy (asked; Update replaces, Keep mine leaves it); tickets not written unless picked; nothing written outside the workspace folder;
- the update notice appears for an older shipped version and not for a user-edited copy;
- `npm run package --workspace combined` passes;

item.description:

author: claude
body:
**Decided with the user (2026-09-28) — unblocked.**

1. **Yes, sessions get an optional end summary.** Its job is the short factual record of the session; in the tickets workflow the closing board comment may quote it and adds what only the board needs (git hash, test counts, what was not verified). The tickets skill says so.

2. **Shape: three sections, mirroring `lap commit`.**
   - `lap session end --done "…" --decided "…" --left "…"`, or `-F <file|->` with `Done:`, `Decided:` and `Left:` sections (as commit takes `-i`/`-b` or `-F` with `Intent:`/`Behavior:`).
   - Every section optional; ending with none is fine, as today. **No free-form `--summary`.**
   - What each is for: **Done** — what the session actually achieved (the purpose at `session start` is the plan, Done is the outcome). **Decided** — choices made along the way that someone might question later, with the reason (visible in no single commit). **Left** — what is unfinished, known broken, or deliberately not done.

3. **Where it shows first:**
   - `lap rr`: at the top of a session's review;
   - Lap History: in the session's tooltip and at the top of the expanded session (the row itself stays one line);
   - the Board's session review (a ticket's sessions): above each session's commits.

**Storage (checked 2026-09-28):** new fields on the existing `session_end` record, not a new record type. A scratch repo with an extra field on `session_end`: `lap verify` → chain ok, `session list` reads it, a new session starts after it — so laps from before this feature keep reading and writing, they just do not show the summary (no `newer_history` needed, unlike `amend`).

The ticket's "Docs & skills must be updated as well" line stands: SPEC (`session end`, the record fields), `lap --help`, the READMEs, the lap skill (when and how to write the three sections) and the tickets skill (the board comment may quote it).

item.title: Optional: a summary when a session ends
item.description:
Idea from the lap audit: coming back to work done while multitasking, the first question is "what was this session trying to do, and how did it end?". Today a session has a purpose at `start` and ends silently.

`lap session end` may take a summary (Done / Decided / Left, e.g. through `-F` with those sections); it is **optional** — a session ended without one is fine. `rr` and the review views show it first when present.

Ordering (the user's condition) holds already: only one session is active at a time (`session start` refuses with `session_active`), and `session end` closes the active one, so a summary always belongs to the session just before it.

Not scheduled; decide before starting.

**Docs & skills must be updated as well:** the SPEC, the READMEs, `lap --help` and the skills (lap, tickets) wherever they describe this behaviour — the ticket is not done without them.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S239, git 4f14c1e.

**kb** (`cmd_ls.c`)
- `kb ls` lists in the store's order, which is the documents' id order, oldest first: ids only grow, and a forgotten document leaves its place.
- `--after D-n` continues after that document by its **number**, so a cursor whose document was forgotten since still continues where it was.
- `--reverse` reads newest first, and `--after` then continues backwards. A cursor that isn't a document id is `usage`.
- The help table has both flags, and the ls summary now tells the truth about the order: it used to say "newest first", which the command never did.
- e2e on five documents covers the order (stable), pages, a cursor at and past the end, reverse, a forgotten cursor both ways, and a bad cursor: 184 with 0 failures.

**Not done — collection paging in kb:** collections are few, and `kb collections` returns them all with their oldest fetch, so the sidebar pages them itself with Load more. kb got no collections cursor.

**kb-js:** `LsOptions.after` and `reverse` map to `--after` and `--reverse`, with a new argv test. The CLI-spelling test now passes both flags, so `kb --help` must name them. kb-js 129/129.
- That test picks up the root CMake build first, and `build/` held an older `kb`, so I rebuilt it (`cmake --build build`, no install).

**Knowledge sidebar**
- **Default:** the collections by name, each with its document count, size and oldest fetch (what `kb collections` carries). A **Manage collections…** link at the top opens `kb:/collections`. Rename and delete remain only there.
- **A collection** opens its documents in the sidebar, newest first, under a "← Collections" back control. Each row shows the title, a description when `meta` has `description`, `abstract` or `summary`, then size, type and fetched date; clicking opens the document as before.
- **Load more** at the foot of both lists: documents come a page (50) at a time through the cursor, one row over so the list knows there's more, and each press chains the next page.
- **Search:** the bar stays on top and searches the store from the collections, or the open collection from inside it (the placeholder says which). The collection `Select` beside the bar is gone, since opening a collection now scopes the search; its CSS and T-224's sizing rule went with it.
- The host's scope event, from a collection row on the Collections page, now opens that collection.
- The view model is a pure `src/view/rail.ts`, with 5 new tests: home/open/back, search scope, the documents query and its cursor, collections paging, and document rows with the description sources or none.
- Two guard tests pinned the old design and now pin the new one: "every document when the query is empty" became the collections-first branch plus Load more and the Manage link in the bundle; the Select width-floor test became "the rail holds no Select".
- index-vscode 128/128.

**Render:** headless Chrome over the built bundle, light and dark, 600px wide (headless won't lay out narrower): the collections list, and a collection's documents after clicking one. The harness answers every collection with the same stub documents. Not checked in VS Code itself.

**Docs:**
- `specs/index-ui.md` §2 is rewritten (default, navigation, rows, paging, search scope), and §4 says the sidebar links to the page.
- `specs/index-api.md` §2's `GET /documents` gives the order and the cursor.
- The root README's KB paragraph is updated.
- The lap and tickets skills don't describe the Knowledge view, so they're unchanged.

procode: MCP servers in VS Code, done as the API intends
Knowledge: a collection's files show as a folder tree
item.description:
**Why (user, 2026-09-28, with a screenshot).** Opening a collection filed from a folder (`kb add --dir`) shows a flat list of full paths — `kb-cli/tests/fixtures/syntax/strings.s`, `kb-cli/tests/fixtures/syntax/ring.go`, … — which is a file tree written out line by line. Show it as a tree.

**Today (T-230, git `4f14c1e`).** A collection opens its documents in the Knowledge sidebar newest first, 50 at a time with **Load more**, each row: title (here the path), size, type, date (`packages/index-vscode/src/view/rail.ts`). Documents carry `path` (`packages/kb-js/src/types.ts:48`), set for files filed with `--dir`.

**Wanted.**
- In a collection, documents with a `path` are shown as a **tree of folders and files**, like VS Code's Explorer: folders first, then files, each alphabetically; folders collapsible (collapsed by default below the top level), with their file count.
- **Compact folders:** a chain of folders holding only one folder each shows as one row (`kb-cli/tests/fixtures`), as VS Code's Explorer does; the common root (`kb-cli/` here) is not a row of its own when everything is under it.
- **File rows** show the file name (not the full path), with size, type and fetched date as today; the full path in the tooltip; clicking opens the document as today.
- **Documents without a `path`** (web pages, papers, anything filed without `--dir`) stay a flat list, under their own heading after the tree; a collection with no paths looks as it does today.
- Expanded folders are remembered while the sidebar stays open.
- **Search inside the collection** shows results as today (flat, with their paths), not as a tree.

**Paging.** A tree cannot page newest first — files would land in half-built folders as pages load. In a collection that has paths, the view lists the whole collection at once (through T-230's cursor, page after page until done, before drawing) and draws the tree; **Load more** stays for the flat list only. Measure on the largest collection at hand (e.g. kb's own sources) and state the time in the closing comment; if a collection is too large to list at once (thousands of files), say so and propose lazy loading per folder (a `--path-prefix` filter in `kb ls`) as a follow-up ticket rather than building it here.

**Done when:** view-model tests (a pure tree builder: folders and files ordered, compact chains, common root, documents without a path apart, file counts; search stays flat); rendered light and dark on a real `--dir` collection; **Docs & skills must be updated as well:** `specs/index-ui.md` §2 (a collection's documents as a tree) — the ticket is not done without it.

author: claude
body:
**Done in lap S240, git a10d286. Blocked on a visual check in the real activity bar.**

**What changed**
- **Everywhere:** Artifacts is renamed **eggzibit**. That covers:
  - the packages `packages/eggzibit` and `packages/eggzibit-vscode`, and the npm workspaces;
  - the MCP server `eggzibit` and its tools `eggzibit_publish`, `_template`, `_list` and `_get`;
  - the commands `eggzibit.*` and the panel type `eggzibit.view`;
  - the skill: `.claude/skills/eggzibit`, with `name: eggzibit` matching its folder, and version 2 so an installed copy is flagged as behind;
  - the spec `specs/eggzibit.md`, the README, launch/tasks, the playground, `.gitignore` and `.lapignore`.
- **MCP instructions:** they now open with "These are local pages shown in VS Code by procode's eggzibit — not claude.ai artifacts, and not your own Artifact tool". The skill's description says the same.
- **Store:** it lives in `.eggzibit/`, with each page's metadata in `page.json`. A store from before the rename (`.artifact/` with `artifact.json`) is found and read where it is. The first write moves it: the folder is renamed, each `artifact.json` becomes `page.json`, and the ids, dates and counter are kept. When both folders exist, `.eggzibit/` wins. The view watches both folders.
- **Icon:** the icon is an egg: whole ("Crack line") while there is no page, split open once there is one. VS Code fixes a container's icon, so there are two containers with the view under two ids (`eggzibit.list`, `eggzibit.listOpen`). One provider serves both, and each refresh sets `eggzibit.hasPages`, which chooses the view. A refresh at activation sets the icon before either view is opened.
- **`.mcp.json`:** procode drops an `artifacts` entry it wrote before (its script ends in `/out/mcp/artifacts.js`) and writes `eggzibit` in its place. An entry the person set up by hand is left alone. `outdated()` reports procode's old entry, so the Update notice fires for such projects.

**Decisions**
- Ids stay `A-<n>`, so existing links and board mentions still resolve.
- The metadata file is `page.json`: the word "artifact" is gone from the format.
- Migration happens on first write, not on read, so looking at a page never changes the workspace.
- The API returns `{ page }` instead of `{ artifact }`, and list returns `{ pages, count }`.

**Tests**
- eggzibit: 16/16, including a new migration test (found from a subfolder, read in place, moved on publish with the counter kept) and a test that the instructions' first line carries the disclaimer.
- eggzibit-vscode: 11/11.
- skills: 3/3.
- Combined check: 36 commands and 3 MCP servers. It now also checks that an old `artifacts` entry procode wrote is removed from `.mcp.json` by Set Up, and that `outdated`/`withServers` ignore and keep a hand-made one.
- `npm run package`: the vsix now ships no `artifact*` files. A stale `out/media/artifact.css` that had moved along with the folder was deleted.

**Not verified; this is why it is blocked**
- The icons and the swap have not been seen in VS Code's real activity bar: light and dark themes, inactive state, with a badge, and the switch when the first page is published or the last one deleted. The containers and `when` clauses are checked only by the manifest and the combined check.

**Left as is**
- This repository's own `.mcp.json` still has the old `artifacts` entry, left for the Update notice to handle.
- `node_modules/artifacts-vscode` is a stale symlink left by the rename; a clean `npm install` drops it.
- The README screenshot is still `assets/artifact-extension.webp` and shows the old view.

item.title: Knowledge: a document filed from a local file or folder opens its original file in VS Code
item.description:
**Why (user, 2026-09-28, with a screenshot).** Clicking the source link of `kb-cli/src/simd.h` (D-121) gives: "Knowledge did not open that link. Only http, https and mailto locators open externally, and this one is not a URL at all."

**Checked.**
- The header links the **source's locator** (`webview/Document.tsx:91-100`), and for a folder source that is the folder's absolute path, e.g. `/Users/…/cli/kb-cli` — not the file, and not a `file://` URL.
- For a `dir` source, the file is the locator joined with the document's `path` (`specs/index-api.md` §2.1: one document per file "at its path under the folder", titled `<folder name>/<path>`): here `/Users/…/cli/kb-cli` + `src/simd.h`. A `file` source's locator is the file itself.

author: claude
body:
**Done in lap S241, git e612b4d.**

**What changed**
- **Tree:** the tree builder is `packages/index-vscode/src/view/tree.ts` (pure). It orders folders first, then files, each in natural order ignoring case (`a2` before `a10`). A chain of one-folder folders is one row, so `fixtures/syntax` shows as a single row. The folder every path shares is not a row; it is said once above the tree as "in kb-cli/". Each folder carries its file count. Documents without a `path` are kept apart, in order. Backslash and `./` paths are handled.
- **Sidebar:** when the collection's first page has a document with a path (`showsTree`), the collection is listed whole and drawn as a tree.
  - Top-level folders start open and deeper ones closed.
  - What the reader opens or closes is kept per collection while the sidebar is open, so going back and returning finds it as it was.
  - Documents without a path follow under **Documents without a path**, a page at a time with Load more.
  - A search inside the collection stays the flat result list.
- **Rows** (changed after your review of the first render): every row is one line at the same size and weight. A file shows its name with its size · type · date muted right after it; a folder shows its name with its file count. The full path is on hover.
- `specs/index-ui.md` §2 describes the tree.

**Decisions**
- **One unlimited `kb ls`, not a cursor loop.** kb ls has no default limit, so the whole collection comes in one process rather than one per page.
  - Measured on a scratch store: kb-cli's sources (`--dir`, 117 files) list in **29 ms**, 112 KB of JSON.
  - The whole repository (402 files) lists in **28 ms**, 366 KB.
  - At these sizes, listing the collection at once is not a concern, so no lazy loading per folder is proposed.
- **The first page decides.** Whether a collection is a tree is decided from its newest page. A collection whose newest 51 documents all lack a path, but whose older ones have one, is drawn flat. The spec says what triggers the tree.

**Tests**
- index-vscode: 134/134, including 6 new tests of the builder: ordering, compacted chains and shared root, path-less documents, separators, open/closed defaults and choices, and search staying flat.
- Rendered headless, light and dark, over the real bundle, with kb-cli's real `--dir` listing plus one path-less document.

**Not verified**

item.description:

**Checked.**
- The header links the **source's locator** (`webview/Document.tsx:91-100`), and for a folder source that is the folder's absolute path, e.g. `/Users/…/cli/kb-cli` — not the file, and not a `file://` URL.
- For a `dir` source, the file is the locator joined with the document's `path` (`specs/index-api.md` §2.1: one document per file "at its path under the folder", titled `<folder name>/<path>`): here `/Users/…/cli/kb-cli` + `src/simd.h`. A `file` source's locator is the file itself.
- `openLink` (`packages/index-vscode/src/host.ts:375-395`) accepts only `http`, `https` and `mailto`, and those already go through a modal confirmation naming the host ("Open … in your browser?") — that stays.

**Change.**
- **Local sources** (`kind` `file` or `dir`; a locator that is an absolute path or a `file://` URL): the link opens the **original file in VS Code** (`vscode.open` on the file URI) — for `dir`, locator + `path`; for `file`, the locator. No confirmation needed: it opens a file for reading, runs nothing. Accept both a bare absolute path and `file://`, so existing stores work without re-filing (kb keeps storing paths as it does).

- **The header shows the file's own location** for local documents (locator + path), not just the folder, so what is shown is what opens.

**Done when:** tests for the locator-to-target logic (dir + path, file, `file://`, bare path, missing file, http, a refused scheme); clicking D-121's link opens `cli/kb-cli/src/simd.h` in an editor (checked in VS Code, said in the comment); **Docs & skills must be updated as well:** `specs/index-ui.md` §3.1 (what the locator link does for local documents) — the ticket is not done without it.

author: claude
body:
**Done in lap S243, git 77f4249. Blocked only on the in-VS Code click.**

**What changed**
- **`packages/index-vscode/src/view/locator.ts` (pure):**
  - `localPath` reads a bare absolute path (POSIX, a drive letter, a UNC share) or a `file://` URL (`file:///C:/…` and `file://host/…` included) as local.
  - `documentLocation(locator, path)` is what the header shows and the link carries: for a local folder source, the locator joined with the document's path. A trailing or leading separator is not doubled, and a Windows-style locator gets `\` separators. For a file source it is the locator; a web locator is kept as filed.
  - `linkTarget(href, exists)` gives `file`, `missing`, `web` (http, https, mailto) or `refused`.
- **Host `openLink`:**
  - A local file opens with `vscode.open`, without a confirmation.
  - A missing one says "The original is no longer at …; the copy kb stored is what you are reading."
  - Web links keep the modal confirmation naming the host.
  - Anything else is refused as before, now naming local files as allowed.
- **Header:** it shows and sends the file's own location, with a go-to-file icon when local (external-link otherwise). For D-121 that is `…/cli/kb-cli/src/simd.h`, not the folder.
- `specs/index-ui.md` §3.1 describes where the link goes.

**Decisions**
- Whether a document is local is decided from the locator, not the source's `kind`, which a document does not carry. A folder's documents have a path; a file's does not. Existing stores work without re-filing.

**Tests**
- index-vscode: 139, including 5 new tests of the locator logic: dir + path (POSIX, `file://`, Windows), file, bare path and URL, present and missing file, http and mailto, a refused scheme, a relative path.
- The combined check passes.

**Not verified; why blocked**
- The link has not been clicked in a real VS Code, so D-121 opening `cli/kb-cli/src/simd.h` in an editor is unchecked.
- The header change (icon and text) was not rendered either.

**Build**

- Anything that opens a view by its old container id (`workbench.view.extension.<id>`) still works in the combined extension.
- Users can still drag any view out to its own container, the panel or the secondary sidebar (VS Code's default).

**Done when**

- `npm run build --workspace combined && node packages/combined/scripts/check.mjs` passes;

item.title: procode ships its CLIs: one package per platform, built by CI
item.description:
Installing procode should not require building lap and kb. CI builds static CLIs for every platform and packages one .vsix per platform with them inside. The extension installs them to `~/.procode/bin`, a path that is the same for every user and every version, and the skills name that path, so Claude's Bash finds them too.

Decided with the user (2026-09-29):
- **Publishing:** a GitHub Release on a version tag; the Marketplace later.
- **Path:** skills name `~/.procode/bin/<cli>`, injected when the skill is installed; the repository's own skills keep plain `lap`.
- **kb:** gets a basic skill with the same injected path.

item.title: combined build: package prebuilt CLIs for one platform target
item.description:
**Goal.** `packages/combined/scripts/build.mjs` can make a platform-specific .vsix carrying lap and kb.

**Build**
- `--target <vsce target>` (darwin-arm64, linux-x64, win32-x64, …) and `--bin <dir>` holding prebuilt `lap` and `kb` (`.exe` on win32). The binaries go in `dist/bin/`, and vsce packages with `--target`; the .vsix is named `procode-<version>-<target>.vsix`.
- Without these flags, the build is exactly today's: one .vsix for every platform, no binaries.

author: claude
body:

item.title: lap's property tests: path buffers sized PATH_MAX, not 1024
item.description:
**Bug (reported by the user).** `cli/lap-cli/tests/prop/prop.c` sizes its path buffers with `#define PATHSZ 1024`, and passes one (`lap_bin`) to `realpath()`, which needs `PATH_MAX` bytes: 4096 on Linux. glibc's fortified `realpath` rejects the 1024-byte buffer; macOS never showed it because its `PATH_MAX` is 1024. It blocks the Linux CI runs (T-239).

**Fix.** Include `<limits.h>` and size the buffers with `PATH_MAX`, dropping `PATHSZ` (the file already defines `_DEFAULT_SOURCE`, so glibc exposes it; musl and macOS always do). The file is POSIX-only, so MSVC's lack of `PATH_MAX` does not matter.

**Done when**
- no `PATHSZ` is left; `lap-prop` builds and `ctest -R lap.prop` passes on macOS;
- the Linux build is verified by the user or by CI.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S258 (L5911–L5932), git `1ec60db`.

- `cli/lap-cli/tests/prop/prop.c` includes `<limits.h>` and sizes all 21 path buffers with `PATH_MAX`. `#define PATHSZ 1024` is gone, and no `PATHSZ` is left. The one that broke was `lap_bin`, which `realpath()` fills: glibc needs `PATH_MAX` (4096) bytes there. macOS's `PATH_MAX` is 1024, which is why it never showed.
- **Windows:** not affected. `lap-prop` is built only under `if(UNIX)` in `cli/lap-cli/CMakeLists.txt`, and the file is POSIX-only (`popen`, `sys/wait.h`).

**Tests (macOS):** `lap-prop` builds with no warnings; `ctest -R lap.prop` passes.

**Not verified:** a Linux build. Docker's daemon isn't running here, so that's for the Linux CI (T-239) or the user.

author: claude
body:
Written in lap session S263 (L5957–L5960), git `45d21ae`. **Not run on GitHub yet.**

- **`ci.yml`** runs on every push to master and every pull request, on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows: CMake Release build of both CLIs, `ctest`, then `npm ci`, `npm run build` and `npm test`. The package tests find the CLIs under `build/` (including MSVC's `Release/`).
- **`release.yml`** runs on a `v*` tag, or by hand:
  - **plan:** fails if the tag doesn't match `packages/combined/package.json`'s version, and adds the arm64 runners (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`, `windows-11-arm`) only when the repository is public.
  - **clis:**
    - macOS: one universal binary (arm64 and x86_64, deployment target 11.0);
    - Linux: static against musl, in `alpine:3.20` via `docker run`, since GitHub's actions don't run inside Alpine on arm64; also used for alpine-*;

- **Portability:** checked that nothing tunes the build to the build machine. There's no `-march`, and kb's SIMD paths come from each architecture's baseline (NEON, SSE2).

**Tests:**
- `actionlint` 1.7.7 reports no problems on both workflows. It caught a YAML break in the release notes, now written with a heredoc.
- Simulated the package step locally with stand-in PE and ELF binaries: the win32-x64 and alpine-arm64 packages build on macOS, carry `bin/lap.exe`/`kb.exe` and `bin/lap`/`kb`, and pass `check.mjs`. I deleted those two .vsix files afterwards.

**Not verified:**
- any run on GitHub;
- whether lap's and kb's `ctest` pass under musl in Alpine;
- whether `npm test` passes on Windows.

The first push and the first tag are the real test.

item.title: Windows: tests expect kb's folder root with backslashes
item.description:
**Bug (from CI on windows-latest).** `kb-js`'s test "a folder through this package: filed, filed again, and a file gone kept or forgotten as asked" fails: `first.root` is `C:/Users/.../tree`, and the test expects `fs.realpathSync(tree)`, which on Windows is `C:\Users\...\tree`. kb writes every path with `/` on every platform (`cli/kb-cli/src/platform.h`), and the only code reading `root` (`index-vscode/src/refresh.ts`) splits on either separator. So kb is right and the tests are wrong. `kb-mcp`'s `cli.test.ts` has the same assertion.

**Fix.** Both tests compare with the native path's separators turned into `/`.

**Done when**
- both tests pass on macOS as before;
- the Windows CI run passes them (verified by the user).

author: claude
body:
Fixed in lap session S267 (L5974–L5975), git `3a5453a`. The folder tests in `kb-js` (`cli.test.ts:617`) and `kb-mcp` (`cli.test.ts:223`) now compare `root` with `fs.realpathSync(tree).replace(/\\/g, "/")`, each with a comment saying kb writes `/` on every platform. I searched the other tests for the same pattern: those that compare kb paths either pass both sides through `realpathSync` or compare TypeScript-built paths with each other, so they're fine.

**Tests (macOS):** kb-js 129/129, kb-mcp 147/147.

**Not verified:** Windows, until the next CI run.

item.title: Windows: the test stand-ins for kb and lap run through node, not a shebang
item.description:
**Bug (from CI on windows-latest).** The test stand-ins for the CLIs are scripts named `kb` (or `lap`) that start with `#!/usr/bin/env node`. Only Unix kernels honour a shebang. Windows' `CreateProcess`, which Node's shell-less `spawn` uses, runs only real executables, so every test that drives a stand-in fails to start it there. For example, kb-mcp's "kb_add with no store…" gets `failed` (kb could not be started) instead of `refused`. author: claude
body:
Fixed in lap session S269, git `80a1287`.

- **coboard:** `lapCommand` in `lap.ts`.
- **lap-vscode:** `lapCommand` in the new `src/lapcommand.ts`. It isn't in `branches.ts` because the webview compiles that file without Node's types. All four lap calls go through a new `execLap`.
- A script gets `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`, because inside VS Code `process.execPath` is VS Code's own runtime.

**Stand-ins:**
- kb-js's and kb-mcp's `FakeKb` are now `kb.js`, with no `#!` and no executable bit. kb-mcp's stdio tests carry it through `KB_BIN` unchanged.

item.title: Windows: the last six Unix-only test assumptions (CRLF, \ paths, exec bit, chmod)
item.description:
**Why.** After T-244, the Windows CI job (run 36539360660) still fails on six tests, while ubuntu and macOS pass. The same six fail locally on Windows:

- kb-mcp `the only stream written by name is stderr`: compares against `src/main.ts`, but `path.relative` gives `src\main.ts`.
- kb-mcp `the build outputs are ignored…` and index-vscode `the build outputs are gitignored…`: split `.gitignore` on `\n`, but a Windows checkout has CRLF.
- kb-mcp `the entry point is executable…`: Windows has no exec bit.
- coboard `a board whose folder cannot be written…` and `ticketSessions: a branch whose history cannot be read…`: `chmod` does not restrict folders on Windows, and `process.getuid` does not exist there, so the root skip never applies.

**Build**
- Split `.gitignore` on `/\r?\n/`, and use `/` separators before comparing a file's path.
- Skip the exec-bit check and the two chmod tests on win32, with the reason.
- Add a `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf`, so a checkout is LF everywhere (the index is already all LF).

**Done when**
- the full `npm test` passes on Windows locally;
- the Windows CI run passes (verified by the user).

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S272, git `88cbe8e`. Only tests and `.gitattributes` changed; no product code.

- **`.gitattributes`** (`* text=auto eol=lf`): every checkout is LF, Windows included. With `core.autocrlf=true`, this machine had checked everything out as CRLF, and that broke lap's hash-chained log: `lap session start` refused with "hash chain is broken". The index was already all LF, so no committed file changes content.
- **kb-mcp `guards.test`:** `.gitignore` is split on `/\r?\n/`; the stdout guard compares paths with `/` separators; the exec-bit check is skipped on win32, while the shebang and `require` checks still run there.
- **index-vscode `guards.test`:** `.gitignore` is split on `/\r?\n/`.
- **coboard:** the read-only-board test (`locate.test`) and the unreadable-branch test (`sessions.test`) are skipped on win32 with the reason given, because chmod cannot restrict a folder there.

**Decided:** LF everywhere through `.gitattributes` rather than per-file workarounds, because lap's log is hashed over its bytes.

**Tests (Windows, local):** the full `npm test` passes: 616 tests, 504 passed, 112 skipped, 0 failed. This ran after rebuilding the CLIs; the local `lap.exe` and `kb.exe` had predated T-219 and caused 8 unrelated failures before the rebuild.

item.title: lap: a reader fails when a conversion removes the old log between its size check and its read
item.description:
**Bug (from CI, macos-latest).** The e2e scenario "readers never see a half-converted history" failed: 1 of 40 `lap verify` reads failed during a conversion. It passes locally (60 stress runs, no failure), so it's timing.

**Suspected cause.** In `hist_open` (`cli/lap-cli/src/hist.c`), when both chunks and the old `log.jsonl` are seen, the reader checks the old file's size and then reads it. A conversion that removes the old file in between (it does so last, once the chunks are published and complete) makes the read fail with "cannot read …/log.jsonl". The branch just below already treats a vanished old file as "the conversion finished; the chunks hold all of it". This one does not.

**Build**
- A test hook between the size check and the read, like `hist_open_between`, and a unit test that removes the old file there: red before the fix.
- When the old file is gone at that read, return the chunks already listed: they were published whole before the old file was removed.

**Done when**
- the new unit test fails before the fix and passes after;
- `ctest -R '^lap\.'` passes;
- CI on macOS passes (the user's next run).

author: claude
body:
Fixed in lap session S274 (L6068–L6073), git `5651f73`.

- **Cause, confirmed:** when `hist_open` sees both chunks and the old `log.jsonl`, it takes the old file's size, then reads it. A conversion removes the old file last, once its chunks are published and complete. When that removal lands between the two steps, the read fails and the reader reported "cannot read …/log.jsonl".
- **Reproduced:** a 60-run stress loop of the e2e scenario on this Mac never hit the window. So I added a tests-only hook, `hist_open_sized`, run between the size check and the read, and a unit test that removes the old file there. Before the fix, that test was the only failure (5098/5099).
- **Fix:** when the old file can't be read because it's gone, `hist_open` lists the chunks again and opens them. Decided: relist rather than reuse the chunks listed earlier, because those could be an older lap's partial conversion that the writer has since replaced.

**Tests:** lap unit tests pass 5099/5099, and `ctest -R '^lap\.'` passes 3/3.

**Not verified:** CI on macOS. The next run confirms it.

item.description:

item.title: procode ships its CLIs: one package per platform, built by CI
item.description:
Installing procode should not require building lap and kb. CI builds static CLIs for every platform and packages one .vsix per platform with them inside. The extension installs them to `~/.procode/bin`, a path that is the same for every user and every version, and the skills name that path, so Claude's Bash finds them too.

Decided with the user (2026-09-29):
- **Publishing:** a GitHub Release on a version tag (`release.yml`). Publishing to the Marketplace and Open VSX is a separate, manual step (`publish.yml`).
- **Path:** the skills state `~/.procode/bin/<cli>` as plain text, falling back to PATH. No injection is needed, since the path never changes.
- **kb:** gets a basic skill with the same path.
- **Home folder:** procode writes its CLIs to `~/.procode/bin` but never deletes anything there. Removing it after uninstalling is the user's call.

Closed 2026-09-29, all 13 tickets done. CI is green on Windows, macOS and Ubuntu. `release.yml` and `publish.yml` have not run yet.

item.title: Keyboard shortcuts do nothing in a newly opened ticket or techdocs tab until it is left and reopened
item.description:
**Bug (reported by the user).** After opening a ticket (or epic, or review) tab, Cmd+Shift+P does nothing until you navigate away from the tab and back. After that it works.

**Likely cause.** `createWebviewPanel` focuses the new tab before its page has loaded. Focus lands in the webview's outer frame, which does not forward keys to the workbench. Coming back to the tab focuses the loaded page, which does.

item.title: release.yml: the Alpine build lacks tzdata, python3 and shasum for the tests; one failing build cancels the others
item.description:
**Bug (first manual release run).** The Linux build in `alpine:3.20` failed lap's tests. Windows passed, and macOS was cancelled.

- `lap.unit` has 7 time-zone failures: every `TZ` renders as `+00:00`, because the image has no `tzdata`.
- `lap.e2e` has 11 failures: `python3: not found` and `shasum: not found` (Alpine's `perl-utils`), so the fixtures those scenarios build were never made, plus the same time-zone case.
- macOS was cancelled by `fail-fast: true` when Linux failed.

**Build**
- `apk add` also installs `tzdata python3 perl-utils`.
- The clis matrix uses `fail-fast: false`, so a release run reports every platform.

**Done when**
- actionlint reports nothing;
- the user's next release run passes on Linux (not verifiable here: Docker isn't running).

author: claude
body:

- **Alpine packages:** the Alpine step also installs `tzdata python3 perl-utils` (`perl-utils` provides `shasum`), with a comment. The comment has no apostrophe, because it sits inside the single-quoted `sh -euc '…'`.
- **fail-fast:** the clis matrix uses `fail-fast: false`, so a failing platform no longer cancels the rest.
- **Diagnosis:** every failure in the run traced back to the environment, not lap. The unit time tests rendered every zone as `+00:00` (no zone files). The e2e fixtures needed `python3` or `shasum` and were never built.

**Not verified:** a release run. Docker isn't running here. One risk remains once zones exist: musl may resolve the ambiguous `2026-10-25 02:30` differently from glibc and macOS. If that test alone fails next time, that's the cause.

item.title: Knowledge: a search page, links that stay in the store, and code linked by its imports
Knowledge: a search page in an editor tab, one search box in the middle
item.description:
The sidebar's search bar leaves little room: results are squeezed into the sidebar's width.

**Change.** A search page that opens as an editor tab, laid out like a search engine's front page: one search box in the middle. Once a search runs, the box moves to the top and the results fill the page.

- **Opening it:** a search button in the Knowledge view's title bar, and the existing command **Knowledge: Search**, open the page (or focus it if it's already open). Whatever is typed in the sidebar's search bar carries over.
- **Where to search:** beside the box, a picker for the collections: **All** (the default), or one or more specific collections. The choice is kept while the tab is open.
- **Results:** every hit with its document title, collection, path (for a folder collection) and the snippet kb returns, with the query words marked. Clicking a result opens the document, at the passage (`kb chunk`), as the sidebar does now.
- **States:** "no store" (with **Knowledge: Initialise A Store In This Workspace**), "no results", `model_mismatch` and `unembedded` shown as notes, the same as the sidebar.
- Built with baukasten, like the other views; follows the theme.

**Not in this ticket:** more filters (type, date, source). The page should leave room for them.

**Done when:**
- the page opens from the title bar and the command, searches all or chosen collections, and opens a result at its passage;
- the sidebar search still works;
- tests cover the collection choice passed to `kb search --collection`, and the empty and error states.

item.title: Knowledge: links in an indexed page open the indexed copy they point to, and no other
item.description:
Navigation inside an indexed HTML page is broken, even when the link points to another page in the same store. A click goes to `openLink` (`packages/index-vscode/src/host.ts:382`), which only opens a local file or a web page (after a confirmation). A relative link (`../api/foo.html`, `guide.html#setup`) is never resolved against the page's own URL, and never looked up in the store.

**Change.** A link is followed only inside the store:

1. **Resolve** the `href` against the document's own locator: its source URL for a web page, or its folder's locator joined with its `path` for a folder document (`index-api.md` §2.1).
2. **Same page:** a link to a fragment of the page being read (`#setup`) scrolls to that heading.
3. **Another indexed document:** if the resolved URL (without its fragment) matches a filed document, open that document in Knowledge, at the fragment when there is one. Match on the source locator; a trailing `/` or `index.html` should not stop a match.
4. **Anything else is not followed.** The link reads as text, with a tooltip saying it points outside the store, and nothing opens. This replaces opening the web behind a confirmation for links inside a document. The document header's own "open the original" link is unchanged.

The lookup from URL to document belongs in `kb-js` (from `kb sources --json` and the documents' paths), so the view does not shell out per click; cache it per view and refresh it when the store changes.

**Done when:**
- in-page, cross-page (relative and absolute) and outside links behave as above, with tests in `view.test.ts` and for the resolver;
- `policy.ts`'s scheme rules still apply: no link can make VS Code launch anything;
- `specs/index-ui.md` §3 says how links in a document behave.

item.title: kb: code filed with --dir links each file to the files it imports or includes
item.description:
kb already parses source code with tree-sitter to chunk it (C, TS/JS, Python, Go, Rust, Assembly). The same parse can say which files a file imports, so a folder of code becomes a graph of its dependencies, drawn by **Knowledge: Graph of Links** and walkable with `kb links`.

**Change.**

- **A new link type, `imports`** (from the importing file to the imported one), added to `index-api.md` §6 and to `kb links`.
- **Created by `kb add --dir`**, never by hand: these links are marked as derived. Filing the folder again recomputes a changed file's links, and forgetting a file drops them. Hand-made links are never touched.
- **Only files in the same folder source are linked.** An import that does not resolve to a filed file (the standard library, a system header, a package from node_modules) is left out, not recorded as unresolved.
- **Resolution per language**, each from the tree-sitter parse:
  - C: `#include "x.h"`, relative to the including file, then to the folder's root. `<x.h>` only if it resolves inside the folder.
  - TS/JS: relative `import`, `export … from`, `require()`, with the usual extensions and `index.*`.
  - Python: relative imports, and absolute ones that resolve to a module or package in the folder.
  - Rust: `mod x;` to `x.rs` or `x/mod.rs`.
  - Go: imports of the module's own packages (from `go.mod`), linking to each file of that package.
  - Assembly: `.include` / `%include`.

  Start with C, TS/JS and Python; Go, Rust and Assembly can be follow-ups if the ticket grows.

**Done when:**
- `kb add --dir` on a fixture folder in each covered language creates the expected `imports` links, and re-filing after an edit updates them;
- `kb links D-n` shows them, and the Knowledge graph draws them in their own style;
- the MCP tool `kb_links` returns them (its type list follows §6);
- e2e and unit tests cover resolution, re-filing and forgetting.

item.title: CI: catch what only one platform or compiler breaks, before a release
item.description: A tree-sitter crash that only gcc -O3 on aarch64 Linux produces reached the v0.1.0 release build: `ci` never built arm64 Linux, and nothing ran the CLIs under sanitizers. This epic closes those gaps, and tracks the aliasing violation in the vendored tree-sitter runtime that the release build now works around with `-fno-strict-aliasing` (fc056c4).

item.title: ci: build and test on Linux arm64 too
item.description:
`ci.yml` runs on `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest` and `windows-latest`: x86 Linux only. `release.yml` also builds linux-arm64, so a bug that only shows there (the tree-sitter crash under gcc -O3, fixed in fc056c4) was first seen in a release.

**Change.** Add `ubuntu-24.04-arm` to `ci`'s matrix, building the CLIs in Release (the same `-O3` as a release) and running `ctest` and `npm test` like the other jobs. GitHub's arm64 runners are only available to public repositories, so this needs the repository to be public.

**Done when:** a hand-run `ci` has a green Linux arm64 job, and the README's Releasing section says `ci` covers it.

item.title: ci: run lap's and kb's tests under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer
item.description:
Undefined behaviour in C can pass every test at one optimisation level and crash at another, on one compiler. Nothing in CI runs the CLIs under sanitizers today; lap's README documents a sanitizer build (`make CFLAGS="… -fsanitize=address,undefined" test`), but only by hand.

**Change.** A `ci` job (one Linux runner is enough) that builds both CLIs in Debug with `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer` and `UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1`, then runs `ctest`. The vendored third-party code may need suppressions; each one gets a comment saying why.

**Done when:** the job is green in a hand-run `ci`, and a deliberate out-of-bounds read in a scratch branch makes it fail.

item.title: tree-sitter runtime: find the aliasing violation behind the arm64 crash, fix or report it
item.description:
gcc -O3 on aarch64 Linux miscompiled the vendored tree-sitter runtime (`src/third_party/tree-sitter/lib/src/lib.c`), which does not keep to C's strict aliasing rules: kb segfaulted on its first parse of source code. fc056c4 works around it by compiling that one file with `-fno-strict-aliasing`.

**Change.**
- Find the violation in `lib.c` (it amalgamates the runtime's sources; bisecting by file, or building with `-Wstrict-aliasing=1`, should narrow it).
- Check whether a newer tree-sitter release already fixes it; if so, update the vendored copy (`TREE-SITTER.md` says how it was vendored).
- If not, report it upstream with a reproducer.
- Then either drop the flag or keep it on purpose, with the comment in `cli/kb-cli/CMakeLists.txt` saying which.

**Done when:** the cause is known and written down, and the flag is removed or its comment explains why it stays.

author: claude
body: Blocked on purpose: the user doesn't want this worked on now. It stays blocked until they authorize it themselves. The `-fno-strict-aliasing` workaround (fc056c4) covers the release in the meantime.

item.title: lap: rough edges found while using it
item.description: Things that got in the way while using lap day to day: being interrupted mid-write, and committing large new files in parts.

item.title: lap: an interrupt during a write waits until the write is done
item.description:
Agents get interrupted, often mid-command, and so does lap. An interrupt that lands while a writer is between its steps (appending to the log, updating the shadow copies, saving state) can leave the caches out of step with the log. Once, a shadow copy of `site/index.html` existed with no commit behind it; `lap verify --deep` reported "shadow/log mismatch" and `lap rebuild` fixed it. Which command wrote it is not known.

**Change.** Every command that writes (`commit`, `amend`, `session start`/`end`, `merge`, `branch …`, `rebuild`, `init`) holds off SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP from the moment it takes the write lock until its writes are finished. A signal that arrives in between is remembered. When the writes are done, the command releases the lock and exits as that signal would have made it exit (status 130 for SIGINT). Nothing is left half written.

- Read-only commands are unchanged: they stop at once.
- A second interrupt doesn't force an exit either. The window is short, and a forced exit is what this ticket removes. `kill -9` can't be caught and stays the exception; the existing heal-on-next-write covers it.
- Windows: the same through `SetConsoleCtrlHandler`, for Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Break.
- SPEC's "Concurrency & crash safety" section says so.

**Done when:** a test sends SIGINT to a writer inside its critical section (a test-only hook that pauses there) and checks that the write completes, `lap verify --deep` passes, and the exit status is 130.

item.title: lap: --lines takes any part of a pending insertion, so a new file can be committed in as many parts as wanted, in any order
item.description:
T-221 meant a new file to be committed in parts, with `--lines` picking any range. As built, only the **first** `--lines` on a new file picks freely. After it, the rest of the file is one pending edit, and `--lines` must match a listed edit exactly. So a 300-line file committed as `--lines 1-40` can then only take `41-300` whole: `--lines 41-90` is refused. To commit the site's `sections.tsx` one chapter at a time, the file had to be cut back on disk before each commit and restored after. That's a misimplementation of T-221.

**Change.** `--lines A-B` accepts any range inside a pending **insertion** (lines added, none replaced), in a new file or in an existing one. Committing it records exactly those lines, placed where they are in the working file; what's left of the insertion stays pending as one edit or two. Parts can be taken in any order and any number: top, bottom, then middle all work.

- Line numbers are those of the working file, as `lap status` shows them.
- An edit that **replaces** lines keeps the exact-match rule: a part of a replacement is ambiguous (which old lines go with it?).
- `large_create` is unchanged: a new file over 50 lines committed whole still needs parts or `--whole-file`.
- `--dry-run` shows the part it would take.
- The lap skill and README say a large new file is committed in parts along its natural seams (types, functions), in any order.

**Be careful:** lap has grown a lot. Keep the change in edit selection (`cmd_commit.c` and `diff.c`), and leave replay, blame and merge alone. A part of an insertion is an ordinary insertion record.

**Tests** (unit and e2e, no need to be exhaustive):
- a new file in three parts, taken top, bottom, then middle: the replayed file equals the working file and `lap verify --deep` passes;
- a part in the middle of an insertion into an existing file leaves two pending edits, correctly numbered;
- a range that crosses the insertion's edge, or covers part of a replacement, is refused and says why;
- blame (`lap search --file --line`) names the part that added each line.

**Done when:** the above works and is tested, and SPEC's section on `--lines` says it.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S292 (L6143–L6165); git commit to follow in the same step.

**What changed**
- `--lines A-B` names a region whole, as before, or **any part of a pending insertion** (a region that only adds lines). The part is committed on its own, at the place the whole insertion would take in the committed file. Parts can be taken in any number and any order: top, bottom, then middle all work, in a new file or an existing one.
- A range that runs past an insertion's edge, or touches an edit that replaces lines, is refused with `lines_mismatch`. The message names the edit and why ("touches edit 1 (lines 2-2), which replaces lines: commit it whole with --edit 1").
- The logic is one pure function, `regions_pick_lines`, in `diff.c`. `cmd_commit.c` calls it; replay, blame and merge are untouched.
- A part that stops before the working file's end is committed ending in a newline when it lands at the committed file's end, even if the file has no final newline, since more lines follow it there.
- SPEC, `lap commit --help`, lap's README (its example now takes parts out of order), the top README, and the lap and tickets skills say so.

**Decided:** only pure insertions split. A part of a replacement can't say which old lines go with it, so replacements stay whole.

**Tests**
- Unit: 5118 passed, 0 failed, including new `regions_pick_lines` cases: a whole region, parts of an insertion at the right position, past an edge, touching a replacement, unchanged lines.
- e2e: 201 scenarios, 0 failures, with three new ones. A 90-line file taken top, bottom, then middle: the shadow equals the file, `verify --deep` passes, and blame on line 45 names the middle part. A part inside an insertion leaves the rest as separate edits, and both refusals are checked. A file without a final newline split into parts.
- `scripts/skills.test.mjs`: pass (the external `skills-ref` validator isn't installed, so that one check was skipped).

**Not verified:** the `prop` merge cases weren't rerun (merge wasn't touched). The installed `~/.procode/bin/lap` is still the old build until the CLI is rebuilt and installed.

item.title: lap: --lines takes any part of a pending insertion, so a new file can be committed in as many parts as wanted, in any order
item.description:
T-221 meant a new file to be committed in parts, with `--lines` picking any range. As built, only the **first** `--lines` on a new file picks freely. After it, the rest of the file is one pending edit, and `--lines` must match a listed edit exactly. So a 300-line file committed as `--lines 1-40` can then only take `41-300` whole: `--lines 41-90` is refused. To commit the site's `sections.tsx` one chapter at a time, the file had to be cut back on disk before each commit and restored after. That's a misimplementation of T-221.

**Change.** `--lines A-B` accepts any range inside a pending **insertion** (lines added, none replaced), in a new file or in an existing one. Committing it records exactly those lines, placed where they are in the working file; what's left of the insertion stays pending as one edit or two. Parts can be taken in any order and any number: top, bottom, then middle all work.

- Line numbers are those of the working file, as `lap status` shows them.
- An edit that **replaces** lines keeps the exact-match rule: a part of a replacement is ambiguous (which old lines go with it?).
- `large_create` is unchanged: a new file over 50 lines committed whole still needs parts or `--whole-file`.
- `--dry-run` shows the part it would take.
- The lap skill and README say a large new file is committed in parts along its natural seams (types, functions), in any order.

**Be careful:** lap has grown a lot. Keep the change in edit selection (`cmd_commit.c` and `diff.c`), and leave replay, blame and merge alone. A part of an insertion is an ordinary insertion record.

**Tests** (unit and e2e, no need to be exhaustive):
- a new file in three parts, taken top, bottom, then middle: the replayed file equals the working file and `lap verify --deep` passes;
- a part in the middle of an insertion into an existing file leaves two pending edits, correctly numbered;
- a range that crosses the insertion's edge, or covers part of a replacement, is refused and says why;
- blame (`lap search --file --line`) names the part that added each line.

**Done when:** the above works and is tested, and SPEC's section on `--lines` says it.

item.title: lap: an interrupt during a write waits until the write is done
item.description:
Agents get interrupted, often mid-command, and so does lap. An interrupt that lands while a writer is between its steps (appending to the log, updating the shadow copies, saving state) can leave the caches out of step with the log. Once, a shadow copy of `site/index.html` existed with no commit behind it; `lap verify --deep` reported "shadow/log mismatch" and `lap rebuild` fixed it. Which command wrote it is not known.

**Change.** Every command that writes (`commit`, `amend`, `session start`/`end`, `merge`, `branch …`, `rebuild`, `init`) holds off SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP from the moment it takes the write lock until its writes are finished. A signal that arrives in between is remembered. When the writes are done, the command releases the lock and exits as that signal would have made it exit (status 130 for SIGINT). Nothing is left half written.

- Read-only commands are unchanged: they stop at once.
- A second interrupt doesn't force an exit either. The window is short, and a forced exit is what this ticket removes. `kill -9` can't be caught and stays the exception; the existing heal-on-next-write covers it.
- Windows: the same through `SetConsoleCtrlHandler`, for Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Break.
- SPEC's "Concurrency & crash safety" section says so.

**Done when:** a test sends SIGINT to a writer inside its critical section (a test-only hook that pauses there) and checks that the write completes, `lap verify --deep` passes, and the exit status is 130.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S293 (L6166–L6182); git commit follows.

**What changed**
- While a command holds lap's lock, SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP (Ctrl-C and Ctrl-Break on Windows) are remembered, not acted on. When the last lock is released, the first signal takes effect: output is flushed and the signal is raised again, so the command ends exactly as it would have (130 for SIGINT, 143 for SIGTERM). Nothing is left half written.
- It lives in `plat_lock` / `plat_trylock` (hold, once the lock is actually held) and `plat_unlock` (release). That covers every writer at once (`commit`, `amend`, `session`, `merge`, `branch`, `rebuild`, `init`, and `status`'s stat-cache write) rather than command by command. Holds nest. Waiting *for* the lock can still be interrupted, and so can readers.
- A signal the process started ignoring stays ignored. `kill -9` can't be held off and is left to the existing heal-on-next-write.
- The code is in a new `src/signals.c`, added to both CMake and make. It defines `_XOPEN_SOURCE 700` for itself, because glibc hides `sigaction`/`SA_RESTART` under plain `-std=c11`; `platform.c`'s feature set is unchanged.
- Test hook: with `LAP_TEST_PAUSE=commit`, `lap commit` pauses for up to 2 s between its log append and its shadow update. The pause ends early when a signal arrives.
- SPEC's "Concurrency & crash safety" section says all of this.

**Tests**
- e2e: 202 scenarios, 0 failures. The new case interrupts a paused commit with SIGINT (under job control, since a background job otherwise starts with SIGINT ignored) and with SIGTERM. In both, the commit's line is printed, the exit status is 130 or 143, nothing is left pending, and `verify --deep` passes. Without the hold, the commit would die in the pause before printing, so the test would catch a regression.
- Unit: 5118 passed, 0 failed. No new unit test: raising a real signal in the unit-test process would kill it, and the e2e case exercises the actual path.
- Built with make and CMake on macOS, and `signals.c` compiles under `-std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -pedantic`.

**Not verified:** the Windows branch (`SetConsoleCtrlHandler`, ending with `STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT`) was written but not compiled or run, and `signals.c` hasn't been compiled on Linux. `ci`'s Windows and Linux jobs will be the first to build them.

item.title: ci: build and test on Linux arm64 too
item.description:
`ci.yml` runs on `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest` and `windows-latest`: x86 Linux only. `release.yml` also builds linux-arm64, so a bug that only shows there (the tree-sitter crash under gcc -O3, fixed in fc056c4) was first seen in a release.

**Change.** Add `ubuntu-24.04-arm` to `ci`'s matrix, building the CLIs in Release (the same `-O3` as a release) and running `ctest` and `npm test` like the other jobs. GitHub's arm64 runners are only available to public repositories, so this needs the repository to be public.

**Done when:** a hand-run `ci` has a green Linux arm64 job, and the README's Releasing section says `ci` covers it.

body:
Code done in lap session S294 (L6183–L6185); git commit follows. **Blocked on a hand-run of `ci`**, which only the user can start.

item.title: ci: run lap's and kb's tests under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer
item.description:
Undefined behaviour in C can pass every test at one optimisation level and crash at another, on one compiler. Nothing in CI runs the CLIs under sanitizers today; lap's README documents a sanitizer build (`make CFLAGS="… -fsanitize=address,undefined" test`), but only by hand.

**Change.** A `ci` job (one Linux runner is enough) that builds both CLIs in Debug with `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer` and `UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1`, then runs `ctest`. The vendored third-party code may need suppressions; each one gets a comment saying why.

**Done when:** the job is green in a hand-run `ci`, and a deliberate out-of-bounds read in a scratch branch makes it fail.

author: claude
body:
Code done in lap session S295 (L6186–L6187); git commit follows. **Blocked on a hand-run of `ci`**, which only the user can start.

**What changed**
- `ci.yml` has a `sanitizers` job on `ubuntu-latest`. It builds both CLIs in Debug with `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g`, then runs `ctest` (lap unit, e2e and merge cases; kb unit and e2e) with `UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1:print_stacktrace=1`.
- `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0`, with a comment: lap and kb are short-lived and leave their arenas to exit, so LeakSanitizer would flag every run. Memory errors stay fatal.
- No suppressions were needed for the vendored code (tree-sitter, utf8proc).
- The README's Releasing section mentions the job.

**Checked locally (macOS, clang, the same flags):**
- All five suites pass: lap.unit, lap.e2e (184 s under ASan), lap.prop, kb.unit, kb.e2e.
- An out-of-bounds read injected into a scratch copy of `diff.c` aborts the unit tests (exit 134, "index 2 out of bounds for type 'int32_t[2]'").
- Caveat: lap allocates from arenas, so an overrun that stays inside an arena chunk is invisible to ASan. Stack and bounds errors are caught.

**Not verified:** Linux, gcc and LeakSanitizer are untried until `ci` runs. To unblock: Actions → ci → Run workflow, and check `sanitizers (ubuntu-latest)` is green.

item.title: Knowledge: links in an indexed page open the indexed copy they point to, and no other
item.description:
Navigation inside an indexed HTML page is broken, even when the link points to another page in the same store. A click goes to `openLink` (`packages/index-vscode/src/host.ts:382`), which only opens a local file or a web page (after a confirmation). A relative link (`../api/foo.html`, `guide.html#setup`) is never resolved against the page's own URL, and never looked up in the store.

**Change.** A link is followed only inside the store:

1. **Resolve** the `href` against the document's own locator: its source URL for a web page, or its folder's locator joined with its `path` for a folder document (`index-api.md` §2.1).
2. **Same page:** a link to a fragment of the page being read (`#setup`) scrolls to that heading.
3. **Another indexed document:** if the resolved URL (without its fragment) matches a filed document, open that document in Knowledge, at the fragment when there is one. Match on the source locator; a trailing `/` or `index.html` should not stop a match.
4. **Anything else is not followed.** The link reads as text, with a tooltip saying it points outside the store, and nothing opens. This replaces opening the web behind a confirmation for links inside a document. The document header's own "open the original" link is unchanged.

The lookup from URL to document belongs in `kb-js` (from `kb sources --json` and the documents' paths), so the view does not shell out per click; cache it per view and refresh it when the store changes.

**Done when:**
- in-page, cross-page (relative and absolute) and outside links behave as above, with tests in `view.test.ts` and for the resolver;
- `policy.ts`'s scheme rules still apply: no link can make VS Code launch anything;
- `specs/index-ui.md` §3 says how links in a document behave.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S296 (L6188–L6229); git commit follows.

**What changed**
- **kb-js** (`src/address.ts`, exported from `kb-js/pure` and the main entry):
  - `documentAddress` gives a document's address: a web page's locator, or a folder file's locator joined with its path as a `file:` URL.
  - `addressKey` normalizes an address: no fragment, no trailing `/`, `index.html` taken as its folder, query kept.
  - `addressIndex` builds the address → document table from one `ls`.
- **index-vscode** `src/view/links.ts` (pure): `followLink(href, base, index, self)` answers one of:
  - `here`: a bare fragment, or a link back to this page;
  - `document`: another filed document, with its fragment;
  - `outside`.
  
  `anchorSlug` / `headingMatches` let `#getting-started` find the heading "Getting Started".
- **Webview**: `webview/links.tsx` has a context and `DocLink`. HTML anchors (`Body.tsx`) and non-`kb:` Markdown links render as `DocLink`:
  - a link-coloured button when it's followed;
  - its text with a muted dotted underline and a tooltip ("…: outside the store, not followed") otherwise. Nothing opens, not even behind a confirmation.
  - `kb:` references still open their tab. The header's link to the original is unchanged.
- **Document tab**: builds the table from `ls`, asked again when the store changes, and provides the resolver to its body. A fragment going to another tab rides where a chunk id would, as `#…`, so `useReveal` scrolls to its heading and the protocol didn't change.
- **Styles and spec**: `knowledge.css` styles `.kb-link-outside` with baukasten tokens. `specs/index-ui.md` §3.2 says how links in a document behave.
- **Guard**: the test that bans `href={…}` in the webview was right to fire. DocLink's prop is `to`, so the ban stays flat. Its comment is updated.

**Tests**
- kb-js: 133/133 pass, including 4 new address tests (web and folder addresses, Windows paths, inline content, key normalization, the index).
- index-vscode: 143/143 pass, including 4 new link tests: here, relative, absolute and folder links; outside links, `javascript:` and `mailto:`; fragments to headings. The guards pass.
- Rendered the real `knowledge-webview.js` in headless Chrome with a stubbed host. On a page at `https://docs.example.com/guide/`, clicking "files API" (`../api/files#open`) sent `open D-2` with `#open`. "setup" and "files API" show as links, and the outside link as dotted text.

**Not verified / known limits**
- The dark render's page background stayed white because the harness's stand-in theme didn't set it. Text and link colours followed the theme; a real dark VS Code theme wasn't tried. The light render is right.
- `html.ts` drops element ids from the original page, so a fragment finds its heading by slug. A fragment naming something other than a heading lands nowhere (the page stays put).
- The scroll-to-heading on a real click wasn't observed; only the `open` message was.

item.title: Knowledge: a search page in an editor tab, one search box in the middle
item.description:
The sidebar's search bar leaves little room: results are squeezed into the sidebar's width.

**Change.** A search page that opens as an editor tab, laid out like a search engine's front page: one search box in the middle. Once a search runs, the box moves to the top and the results fill the page.

- **Opening it:** a search button in the Knowledge view's title bar, and the existing command **Knowledge: Search**, open the page (or focus it if it's already open). Whatever is typed in the sidebar's search bar carries over.
- **Where to search:** beside the box, a picker for the collections: **All** (the default), or one or more specific collections. The choice is kept while the tab is open.
- **Results:** every hit with its document title, collection, path (for a folder collection) and the snippet kb returns, with the query words marked. Clicking a result opens the document, at the passage (`kb chunk`), as the sidebar does now.
- **States:** "no store" (with **Knowledge: Initialise A Store In This Workspace**), "no results", `model_mismatch` and `unembedded` shown as notes, the same as the sidebar.
- Built with baukasten, like the other views; follows the theme.

**Not in this ticket:** more filters (type, date, source). The page should leave room for them.

**Done when:**
- the page opens from the title bar and the command, searches all or chosen collections, and opens a result at its passage;
- the sidebar search still works;
- tests cover the collection choice passed to `kb search --collection`, and the empty and error states.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S297 (L6230–L6279); git commit follows.

**What changed**
- `kb:/search` is a new place, and `webview/Search.tsx` is the page. Until the first search it shows one box in the middle, with the collection chips under it: **All** (the default), or any picked. After a search the box sits on a bar at the top and the results fill the page below, in a readable column. The rows are the sidebar's own `KnowledgeRow`/`List` (now exported), so a result reads the same in both, and clicking one opens its document at the passage. "No store", "Nothing matched", the unembedded note and refusals such as `model_mismatch` come from the same `Resolved` and notes the sidebar uses.
- It opens from **Knowledge: Open Search Page** (`knowledge.searchPage`), which is also the search button first on the Knowledge title bar, and it focuses the tab if one is open.
- It starts from the sidebar's text: the sidebar sends a `typed` request as its text settles, the host keeps it, and the command hands it to the tab through the existing `reveal` channel. That's the same way a chunk reaches a document, now documented on the `open` request.
- The chosen collections go to `kb search --collection` as one comma list; none chosen sends no `collection`, which is All. This is pure code in `src/view/search.ts`.
- `specs/index-ui.md` §5 describes the page and §6 lists `kb:/search`. The styles use baukasten tokens.

**Decided, differently from the ticket as written**
- **A new command, not a replacement for Knowledge: Search.** §5 makes that one the keyboard QuickPick on purpose, and a guard keeps it off the title bar. It stays as it was.
- **No marking of the query's words.** index-ui.md §2 ("matches are not marked up") and §7 (match highlighting not included) refuse it, and a guard fired when I added it. I wrote that into the ticket without checking the spec, so it was taken out again (still in lap: #c2687e2, then #1653629 onwards). If you want highlighting, it means changing §2 and §7 first; it's then small to add.

**Tests**
- index-vscode: 145/145 pass. New: the page's query for All and for chosen collections, collection toggling, and `kb:/search` parsing to the search place.
- Guards updated: `Search.tsx` may hold an `<input>` (a query, which writes nothing); `typed` is a request kind; the page's button is required on the title bar, and `Knowledge: Search` still isn't allowed there.
- Combined build and `check.mjs`: 37 commands registered, 3 MCP servers, no errors.
- Rendered the real bundle in headless Chrome with a stubbed host. The front shows the box, title and chips with All pressed. With the sidebar's text ("submission queue") arriving as a reveal, the page searched `{"k":50,"q":"submission queue"}` and drew both rows with their collection and match chips.

**Not verified**
- In the dark render the page background stayed white, because the harness didn't set the VS Code variable it comes from. The light render is right.
- Picking a collection chip and then searching wasn't clicked through in the render; the unit test covers the query it sends.
- Not tried inside a real VS Code window.

item.title: kb: code filed with --dir links each file to the files it imports or includes
item.description:
kb already parses source code with tree-sitter to chunk it (C, TS/JS, Python, Go, Rust, Assembly). The same parse can say which files a file imports, so a folder of code becomes a graph of its dependencies, drawn by **Knowledge: Graph of Links** and walkable with `kb links`.

**Change.**

- **A new link type, `imports`** (from the importing file to the imported one), added to `index-api.md` §6 and to `kb links`.
- **Created by `kb add --dir`**, never by hand: these links are marked as derived. Filing the folder again recomputes a changed file's links, and forgetting a file drops them. Hand-made links are never touched.
- **Only files in the same folder source are linked.** An import that does not resolve to a filed file (the standard library, a system header, a package from node_modules) is left out, not recorded as unresolved.
- **Resolution per language**, each from the tree-sitter parse:
  - C: `#include "x.h"`, relative to the including file, then to the folder's root. `<x.h>` only if it resolves inside the folder.
  - TS/JS: relative `import`, `export … from`, `require()`, with the usual extensions and `index.*`.
  - Python: relative imports, and absolute ones that resolve to a module or package in the folder.
  - Rust: `mod x;` to `x.rs` or `x/mod.rs`.
  - Go: imports of the module's own packages (from `go.mod`), linking to each file of that package.
  - Assembly: `.include` / `%include`.

  Start with C, TS/JS and Python; Go, Rust and Assembly can be follow-ups if the ticket grows.

**Done when:**
- `kb add --dir` on a fixture folder in each covered language creates the expected `imports` links, and re-filing after an edit updates them;
- `kb links D-n` shows them, and the Knowledge graph draws them in their own style;
- the MCP tool `kb_links` returns them (its type list follows §6);
- e2e and unit tests cover resolution, re-filing and forgetting.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S298 (L6280–L6341) for C, TypeScript/JavaScript and Python; git commit follows.

**What changed**
- **A new link type, `imports`** (kb's `LINK_TYPES`, count 6). `kb links add`/`delete` refuse it ("imports links are kept by kb add --dir from the files' code, not made or removed by hand"). That makes every `imports` link derived by construction, with no new field in the log. The "not a link type" message still lists only the five a person may write.
- **Extraction** (`syntax_imports` in `syntax.c`): a tree-cursor walk over the real parse, so imports inside comments or strings don't count.
  - C: `#include "…"` and `<…>`, including under `#if`.
  - TS/TSX/JS: `import … from`, `export … from`, `import x = require()`, `require()` and `import()`.
  - Python: `import a.b`, and `from .m`/`..p.q`/`pkg.sub import …`; `from . import x` gives `.x`.
- **Resolution** (`import_resolve` in a new `imports.c`, pure):
  - C: quoted includes beside the file, then from the root; `<…>` the other way round.
  - TS/JS: relative specifiers only, tried as written, with each extension, as `index.*`, and as the `.ts` behind a `.js`.
  - Python: relative imports from the package, climbing a folder per extra dot; absolute ones from the file's folder up to the root, as a module, a package or a stub.
  - Nothing outside the folder is ever linked.
- **Sync** (`imports_sync`, called by `add --dir` after filing and forgetting):
  - It computes the wanted edges from every scanned file, unchanged ones included, so a newly added file that makes an old import resolve gets linked.
  - It compares them with the existing `imports` links out of those files, or touching documents just forgotten, and appends only `link`/`unlink` records for the difference.
  - A document kept with `--no-forget` keeps its links.
  - `add --dir` reports `"imports":{"linked":n,"unlinked":m}` in JSON and "imports: n linked, m unlinked" in text.
- **kb-js**: `LINK_TYPES` includes `imports`; `HAND_LINK_TYPES` is the five; `KbDirAdded.imports` is read.
- **kb-mcp**: `kb_links`' description says a list also shows `imports` links and that agents can't add them. The add enum stays at the five.
- **Knowledge**: the graph draws `imports` edges thin in the info colour, and the empty graph mentions them. After **Add Folder**, the message says how many were linked and unlinked.
- **Docs**: `index-api.md` §6 (the type and its rules) and §2.1 (the answer's example and fields); the kb skill.

**Tests**
- Unit (kb, 3124 passed, 0 failed): extraction per language (and not from comments or strings), and resolution per language against a fake folder, including climbing out of it.
- e2e (kb, 185 passed): a mixed folder gets exactly its 5 links; nothing links for `stdio.h`, `react` or `os`. Filing again unchanged writes 0/0. After an edit that drops a `require` and a deleted header, 3 are unlinked and the right ones remain. `kb links add … imports …` is refused.
- Also checked: lap (unit, e2e, merge cases) pass; kb-js 133/133, kb-mcp 147/147, index-vscode 145/145; the combined `check.mjs` has no errors.
- By hand on a larger sample folder: 8 correct links, including `./f.js` finding `f.ts`, and one edge reached both relatively and absolutely counted once.
