- **Go, Rust and Assembly** have no import rules yet; the ticket allowed them as follow-ups. Say if you want a ticket for them.
- `kb forget D-n` by hand leaves that document's `imports` links, which read as `resolved: false`, until its folder is filed again.
- The graph's `imports` edge style wasn't rendered.
- Cost: every filing reparses every code file for its imports (tree-sitter, milliseconds per file). It wasn't measured on a large folder.

item.title: kb: code filed with --dir links each file to the files it imports or includes
item.description:
kb already parses source code with tree-sitter to chunk it (C, TS/JS, Python, Go, Rust, Assembly). The same parse can say which files a file imports, so a folder of code becomes a graph of its dependencies, drawn by **Knowledge: Graph of Links** and walkable with `kb links`.

**Change.**

- **A new link type, `imports`** (from the importing file to the imported one), added to `index-api.md` §6 and to `kb links`.
- **Created by `kb add --dir`**, never by hand: these links are marked as derived. Filing the folder again recomputes a changed file's links, and forgetting a file drops them. Hand-made links are never touched.
- **Only files in the same folder source are linked.** An import that does not resolve to a filed file (the standard library, a system header, a package from node_modules) is left out, not recorded as unresolved.
- **Resolution per language**, each from the tree-sitter parse:
  - C: `#include "x.h"`, relative to the including file, then to the folder's root. `<x.h>` only if it resolves inside the folder.
  - TS/JS: relative `import`, `export … from`, `require()`, with the usual extensions and `index.*`.
  - Python: relative imports, and absolute ones that resolve to a module or package in the folder.
  - Rust: `mod x;` to `x.rs` or `x/mod.rs`.
  - Go: imports of the module's own packages (from `go.mod`), linking to each file of that package.
  - Assembly: `.include` / `%include`.

  Start with C, TS/JS and Python; Go, Rust and Assembly can be follow-ups if the ticket grows.

**Done when:**
- `kb add --dir` on a fixture folder in each covered language creates the expected `imports` links, and re-filing after an edit updates them;
- `kb links D-n` shows them, and the Knowledge graph draws them in their own style;
- the MCP tool `kb_links` returns them (its type list follows §6);
- e2e and unit tests cover resolution, re-filing and forgetting.

ci sanitizers: kb's imports sync sorts a NULL array; lap's e2e assumes a 512 MB ulimit and bash's job control
item.description:
The first hand-run of `ci`'s sanitizers job (T-258) failed on Linux:

- **kb:** `imports.c:206` in `unique()` calls `qsort(NULL, 0, …)` when a folder has no import edges. That's undefined behaviour even with a count of zero, and UBSan aborts on it, so every `add --dir` failed (27 of kb.e2e's 28 failures follow from it).
- **lap, "status over many files…":** the test runs `lap status` under `ulimit -v 524288`, and ASan can't reserve its shadow memory under any such limit.
- **lap, "an interrupt in the middle of a commit…":** the runner's `/bin/sh` is dash, which starts a background job with SIGINT ignored even under `set -m`. lap correctly keeps an ignored signal ignored, so the commit finished with exit 0. It passed on macOS, where `sh` is bash.

**Done when:** `unique()` and any other sort or search on a possibly empty array never pass NULL; the ulimit test leaves the limit off under ASan (`ASAN_OPTIONS` set); the SIGINT half of the interrupt test runs only when the shell really delivers SIGINT to a background job, and the SIGTERM half always runs; both suites pass locally under the sanitizers and with dash as `sh`.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S301 (L6362–L6365); git commit follows.

**What changed**
- **kb** (`imports.c`): `unique()` returns at once for zero edges, so a folder without imports never hands `qsort` a NULL array. That's undefined behaviour which glibc's non-null annotation lets UBSan catch, and it aborted every `add --dir` in the sanitizers job. The other sorts and lookups in the file were checked: each is guarded on zero or gets an array that is always allocated.
- **lap e2e, many-files status:** the 512 MB `ulimit -v` stays off when `ASAN_OPTIONS` is set, since ASan reserves terabytes of address space before `main`. The rest of the check is unchanged.
- **lap e2e, interrupt:** SIGTERM is sent first and always (exit 143, line printed, nothing pending). SIGINT (exit 130) is then sent only if a background `sleep` started the same way dies of SIGINT. Ubuntu's dash without a terminal starts background jobs with SIGINT ignored, and lap correctly keeps an inherited ignore, so the test mustn't demand SIGINT there. It prints a `skip:` line instead.

**Tests (macOS)**
- The lap e2e passed three ways: run by `sh`, 202/202; run by `/bin/dash`, 202/202; and with SIGINT ignored from the start, which takes the skip branch as CI's dash does, 202/202.
- Sanitizer build with CI's `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0` and `UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1`: lap unit, e2e and merge cases, kb unit and e2e all pass. The normal Release build's 5 suites pass too.

**Not verified:** the `qsort(NULL)` report only happens on glibc, so this fix is confirmed only when `ci` runs again on Linux.

item.title: ci: build and test on Linux arm64 too
item.description:
`ci.yml` runs on `ubuntu-latest`, `macos-latest` and `windows-latest`: x86 Linux only. `release.yml` also builds linux-arm64, so a bug that only shows there (the tree-sitter crash under gcc -O3, fixed in fc056c4) was first seen in a release.

**Change.** Add `ubuntu-24.04-arm` to `ci`'s matrix, building the CLIs in Release (the same `-O3` as a release) and running `ctest` and `npm test` like the other jobs. GitHub's arm64 runners are only available to public repositories, so this needs the repository to be public.

**Done when:** a hand-run `ci` has a green Linux arm64 job, and the README's Releasing section says `ci` covers it.

author: claude
body: Unblocked and done: the user reports the hand-run `ci` is green, the sanitizers job included. Its first run failed and found a real bug, `qsort(NULL, 0)` in kb's imports sync, plus two tests that assumed macOS; all three are fixed in T-263 (`dc5b422`). The "deliberate out-of-bounds read makes it fail" half was checked locally (see the earlier comment), and the first CI run showed the job fails on a real report too.

item.title: ci: run lap's and kb's tests under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer
item.description:
Undefined behaviour in C can pass every test at one optimisation level and crash at another, on one compiler. Nothing in CI runs the CLIs under sanitizers today; lap's README documents a sanitizer build (`make CFLAGS="… -fsanitize=address,undefined" test`), but only by hand.

**Change.** A `ci` job (one Linux runner is enough) that builds both CLIs in Debug with `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer` and `UBSAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1`, then runs `ctest`. The vendored third-party code may need suppressions; each one gets a comment saying why.

**Done when:** the job is green in a hand-run `ci`, and a deliberate out-of-bounds read in a scratch branch makes it fail.

item.title: Board tabs navigate in place: a click on an item replaces the tab, ⌘/Ctrl-click and middle-click open a new one
item.description:
## Why

Browsing epic → milestone → ticket opens a new tab for every click, and tabs pile up. Clicking a link inside a board tab should work like a browser: go there in the same tab. A new tab is opened only when asked for.

Chosen over VS Code-style preview tabs, which need the move to a custom editor (bare `createWebviewPanel` has no preview option). That move stays possible later and doesn't conflict with this.

## Behaviour

Applies to links **inside** item tabs (epic, milestone, ticket): `IdLink` (`webview/parts.tsx`), `open()` (`webview/rpc.ts`), the ticket rows (`webview/views.tsx`).

- **Plain click / Enter:** the current tab navigates to the item. Its title and content change, and the item is added to the tab's history.
- **⌘-click (macOS) / Ctrl-click (elsewhere), middle-click, ⌘/Ctrl+Enter:** opens the item in a new tab.
- **Already open elsewhere:** in both cases, if the item already has a tab, that tab is focused and nothing navigates. There is still one tab per item.
- **Sidebar:** unchanged. A click opens or focuses the item's tab, as now.
- **Reviews:** unchanged. A review always opens in its own tab (it's a different page, `ReviewApp`).

## Back / forward: shortcuts only, no buttons

VS Code users already have Go Back / Go Forward keys, so we reuse them rather than add buttons:
- `coboard.back` / `coboard.forward` commands, bound to the same keys as `workbench.action.navigateBack` / `navigateForward` (macOS ⌃- / ⌃⇧-, Windows/Linux Alt+← / Alt+→), `when: activeWebviewPanelId == 'coboard.item'`.
- When the tab's history has nothing left in that direction, run VS Code's own navigateBack / navigateForward, so the key still does what the user expects.
- Mouse back/forward side buttons inside the page (`mouseup`, buttons 3/4) do the same.

## Implementation notes (from the audit)

- A tab's id is fixed today: it's baked into the HTML (`data-id`, read once in `webview/main.tsx`), captured by the `onMessage` closure, and used as the tab's key in `panels`. Make it changeable: the page takes the id from each `data` message; the host keeps the current id and a back/forward stack per panel, and re-keys `panels` on navigation.
- `open` in `src/protocol.ts` gains `newTab: boolean`.
- `push()` already sets the title; `pushSessions` must follow the new id for tickets.
- Anything else that looks tabs up in `panels` (refresh, delete, archive) must see the re-keyed entry.

## Tests

In `src/test/host.test.ts`:
- a plain open navigates and re-keys;
- a `newTab` open creates a panel;
- an open of an item already in another tab focuses that tab, in both modes;
- back/forward walk the stack, and fall through to VS Code's commands at either end;
- deleting the current item of a tab it was navigated to still updates that tab.

## Out of scope

- Tabs still disappear on window reload (no panel serialiser); separate ticket.
- techdocs tabs.

author: claude
body:
**lap S302 · git 4ba2be8**

**What changed**
- A plain click on an item inside a board tab (id links, titles, links in Markdown descriptions, Kanban cards) now shows the item **in that tab**. The tab's title, icon and page change, and the page scrolls to the top.
- **⌘-click / Ctrl-click, the middle button, and ⌘/Ctrl+Enter on a Kanban card** open the item in a new tab. The middle button's press is stopped so it doesn't start autoscroll.
- **If the item already has a tab**, that tab is focused, whichever way it was clicked. An item is still never in two tabs.
- **Back/Forward.** Each tab keeps its own history. The mouse's side buttons walk it inside the page, and so do the new `coboard.back` / `coboard.forward` commands. Those are bound to VS Code's Go Back / Go Forward keys (macOS ⌃- / ⌃⇧-, Windows Alt+← / Alt+→, Linux Ctrl+Alt+- / Ctrl+Shift+-), only while `activeWebviewPanelId == 'coboard.item'`. They're hidden from the command palette. When the history is empty, the key runs VS Code's own Go Back / Go Forward.
- **Unchanged:** sidebar clicks, the tabs created by New ticket/milestone, and review tabs. A click in a review tab still opens a new tab.

**Decided**
- **Back/Forward to an item open in another tab** focuses that tab and uses the history entry up, so the next press goes past it. This keeps one tab per item.
- **Tab identity** is now a per-panel place: the current id plus back/forward lists. The host reads it on every message instead of a key captured when the tab opened, and re-keys `panels` when the tab moves.
- **What the page keeps per item:** it takes its item from each `data` message and is keyed by it, so drafts and open pickers don't carry over. A ticket's sessions that arrive after the tab has left it are dropped.

**Tests**
- coboard-vscode: 47 pass, 0 skipped. That includes a new host test covering: a plain click, ⌘/middle-click, clicks on items already open elsewhere, a refresh after a move, Back/Forward from both the mouse and the key with the fallback at both ends, a history entry that's open elsewhere, and deleting the item a moved tab shows.
- Combined build check: 39 commands, no errors.
- **Headless Chrome, real production bundle:** the page sends the right `open`/`history` messages for plain, ⌘, Ctrl, middle and right clicks, the side buttons, and Kanban cards with Enter. It also re-renders as the new item. This check caught a crash (the scroll effect returned `scrollTo`'s result as its cleanup), fixed in L6399.

**Not verified**
- **Not tried in a running VS Code:** the keybindings' `activeWebviewPanelId` when-clause, the keys reaching the host while focus is inside the webview, and the side buttons in the real webview.
- **Theme renders:** nothing visual changed, so no light/dark renders were done.
- **Window reload:** tabs still disappear on reload (no serialiser), and their history with them.

item.title: kb MCP: kb_add files web pages by URL, fetched as they are, so an agent's web research lands in the knowledge base
item.description:
## Why

Agents search the web and should file what they read into kb, so the next question on the topic is answered from disk. Today `kb_add` takes only `documents` (text the agent already has) or `dir`. To file a page, an agent fetches it itself, and Claude Code's WebFetch returns a model-written **summary** of the page, not the page. So what kb stores is a paraphrase carrying the page's URL as its source, which makes kb's provenance wrong.

Knowledge's **Add URL** already fetches correctly (`fetchPage` in `packages/index-vscode/src/commands.ts`):
- follows redirects;
- a non-2xx response files nothing;
- files the bytes exactly as they arrived (HTML is rendered as prose when read, not rewritten when filed);
- keeps the ETag for refresh;
- takes the title from the page.

## Change

- **Move `fetchPage` and `titleOf` into `kb-js`,** so the Knowledge extension and the kb MCP server share one fetcher. Knowledge's Add URL keeps working unchanged.
- **Add `urls` to `kb_add`, beside `documents` and `dir`:** `{ urls: [{ url, collection, title? }] }`.
  - The server fetches each URL and files it through `kb add` with the URL as its locator, its mime type, its ETag, and the page's title unless one is given.
  - Each URL gets its own result: filed, unchanged (the same bytes are already filed under that URL), or failed with the status.
  - One failed URL doesn't stop the others.
- **Only `http` and `https`.** Refuse other schemes, and hosts that resolve to localhost or private network ranges, so an agent can't be used to read internal services.
- **A size cap per page** (for example 5 MB). A page over it is refused, not truncated.
- **kb itself stays offline.** The fetch happens in the MCP server, as Knowledge's happens in the VS Code extension. `kb` never touches the network.
- **Update the kb server's instructions and the kb skill:** to file a page, pass its URL to `kb_add` rather than fetching it and passing the text, so kb stores the page, not a summary.

## Privacy

**This makes the kb MCP server a second thing that goes online.** The Marketplace README's Privacy section says only Knowledge's Add URL does, so it must now also name `kb_add` with `urls`: it fetches pages an agent asks for, and the agent's own tool approval is the consent.

## Done when

- An agent calls `kb_add` with `urls` and gets per-URL results. The filed document's content is the page's bytes, its locator the URL, and **Refresh** in Knowledge refreshes it.
- A 404, a redirect to a non-2xx, a non-http(s) URL, a private address and an oversized page are each refused with a clear reason, and nothing is filed for them.
- Tests in `kb-js` and `kb-mcp`, with a local HTTP server as the fixture, covering: success, not modified, each refusal, and a mix of good and bad URLs in one call.
- The server instructions, the kb skill and the README's Privacy section describe the new behavior.
- The combined build check passes.

## Out of scope

- Crawling, or following links from a page.
- Converting pages to text before filing (rendering stays at read time).
- PDFs by URL, unless kb already accepts the bytes as they come.

item.title: Board tabs navigate in place: a click on an item replaces the tab, ⌘/Ctrl-click and middle-click open a new one

item.title: Knowledge: Index This Workspace — one command and a toolbar button that file the open folders' code
item.description:
## Why

Filing the code you're working on takes Add Folder…, a folder dialog and a collection picker, every time. Indexing the workspace should be one click, and running it again should be how the index stays up to date.

## What already exists (no change needed)

`kb add --dir` (`cli/kb-cli/src/dirscan.h`) already decides what gets filed:
- **Hidden paths:** any `.`-prefixed segment, so `.git`, `.lap`, `.kb`, `.coboard` and editor state are out.
- **`.gitignore`:** git's full rules, including nested files.
- **Vendored code:** `node_modules`, `vendor`, `third_party` and similar, even when committed.
- **Generated, binary and large files:** lock files, minified bundles, `@generated` files, non-UTF-8 files, anything over 1 MB.
- **Running again:** only what changed is filed, and files that are gone are forgotten.

`addFolder` in `packages/index-vscode/src/commands.ts` wraps it. This ticket adds a shortcut on top and doesn't change those rules.

**Not read: `.lapignore`.** It lists what lap shouldn't record, which is not the same as what's worth searching, and in this repo everything it adds is already covered by the rules above. If extra exclusions are ever needed, they'd go in a `.kbignore`, which is a separate ticket.

## Behaviour

- **New command `knowledge.indexWorkspace`, titled "Index This Workspace"** (category Knowledge, in the command palette).
  - It shows no dialogs. Each `file:` workspace folder is filed with `kb.addDir(folder, { collection: <folder's name> })`. In a multi-root workspace, each folder goes into its own collection.
  - It runs with progress, and ends with the same `folderMessage` as Add Folder (added / updated / unchanged / forgotten / skipped), one message per folder.
  - With no folder open it says so and does nothing. With no store yet, it takes the same path as the other add commands.
- **Toolbar button:** the command gets a button in the Knowledge view's title bar (`view/title`, `view == knowledge.documents`) with an icon distinct from Add Folder's. There are already eight buttons there, so check how it looks; if it's too crowded, put it first in the overflow menu instead.
- **Running it again** refreshes: only changes are filed, and deleted files are forgotten. That's how the index is kept current for now.

## Done when

- One click on the Knowledge toolbar files the open workspace folder(s) into a collection named after each folder, with no dialogs.
- Running it again reports what changed.
- Tests (`packages/index-vscode/src/test/`, in the style of `addfolder.test.ts`):
  - no dialogs are shown;
  - one `addDir` call per workspace folder, with the folder's name as the collection;
  - with no folder open, nothing is filed and the user is told;
  - the command is in the manifest and the toolbar menu.
- The combined build check passes.

## Out of scope

- Re-indexing automatically on save or through a file watcher. That's a possible follow-up once the manual version has been used.
- `.kbignore`.

item.title: Knowledge document tab: a toolbar with the file name, Save As, zoom (−, +, 100%) and find-with-highlight
item.description:
## Why

A document open in Knowledge has no way to save it as a file, change its size, or search inside it. ⌘F / Ctrl+F does nothing there: no webview in procode sets VS Code's find widget, so the key has nothing to open.

## Behaviour

A toolbar across the top of a Knowledge document tab (`webview/Document.tsx`; check what header it already has and extend that rather than stacking a second one):

- **File name.** Show the document's title, or the source file's name for a document filed from a file, so you can tell what's open without scrolling.
- **Save As…** Save the document's text to a file through VS Code's save dialog (`showSaveDialog`), defaulting to its title and a matching extension (`.md` for Markdown, the original extension for code). It saves the text kb holds, exactly as stored; the document in kb doesn't change.
- **Zoom:** −, +, and a 100% button that resets. Show the current level. It applies to that tab's content only, not to VS Code's own zoom. It's remembered per tab while the tab is open (a setting for a default level isn't needed yet).
- **Find**, with highlighting:
  - ⌘F / Ctrl+F and a toolbar button both open it.
  - Matches are highlighted in the text, with next and previous (Enter / Shift+Enter) and a count ("3 of 12").
  - Escape closes it and clears the highlights.
  - **Cheapest route to check first:** VS Code's built-in find widget. Set `webviewOptions.enableFindWidget: true` on the custom editor (`src/editor.ts`, `registerCustomEditorProvider`); a toolbar button can open it with the command `editor.action.webvieweditor.showFind`. If that widget's highlighting works well on the rendered document, use it. Build a find bar of our own only if it doesn't, and say why in the commit.

## Done when

- Every Knowledge document tab shows the toolbar with the name, Save As, the zoom controls and find.
- Save As writes the stored text to the chosen file.
- Zoom −, + and 100% change only that tab's content, and the level is shown.
- ⌘F / Ctrl+F opens find; matches are highlighted and you can step through them; Escape clears it.
- Tests in `packages/index-vscode/src/test/`:
  - Save As writes the document's stored text to the path the dialog returns, and nothing when the dialog is cancelled;
  - zoom steps and the 100% reset (a pure helper);
  - if we build our own find: matching and next/previous over the rendered text.
- Rendered headless in a light and a dark theme.

## Out of scope

- The same toolbar on techdocs pages and board tabs. Their tabs have the same missing ⌘F; that could be a follow-up.

item.title: Knowledge document tab: a toolbar with the file name, Save As, zoom (−, +, 100%) and find-with-highlight
item.description:
## Why

A document open in Knowledge has no way to save it as a file, change its size, or search inside it. ⌘F / Ctrl+F does nothing there: no webview in procode sets VS Code's find widget, so the key has nothing to open.

## Behaviour

A toolbar across the top of a Knowledge document tab (`webview/Document.tsx`; check what header it already has and extend that rather than stacking a second one):

- **File name.** Show the document's title, or the source file's name for a document filed from a file, so you can tell what's open without scrolling.
- **Save As…** Save the document's text to a file through VS Code's save dialog (`showSaveDialog`), defaulting to its title and a matching extension (`.md` for Markdown, the original extension for code). It saves the text kb holds, exactly as stored; the document in kb doesn't change.
- **Zoom:** −, +, and a 100% button that resets. Show the current level. It applies to that tab's content only, not to VS Code's own zoom. It's remembered per tab while the tab is open (a setting for a default level isn't needed yet).
- **Find**, with highlighting:
  - ⌘F / Ctrl+F and a toolbar button both open it.
  - Matches are highlighted in the text, with next and previous (Enter / Shift+Enter) and a count ("3 of 12").
  - Escape closes it and clears the highlights.
  - **Cheapest route to check first:** VS Code's built-in find widget. Set `webviewOptions.enableFindWidget: true` on the custom editor (`src/editor.ts`, `registerCustomEditorProvider`); a toolbar button can open it with the command `editor.action.webvieweditor.showFind`. If that widget's highlighting works well on the rendered document, use it. Build a find bar of our own only if it doesn't, and say why in the commit.

## Done when

- Every Knowledge document tab shows the toolbar with the name, Save As, the zoom controls and find.
- Save As writes the stored text to the chosen file.
- Zoom −, + and 100% change only that tab's content, and the level is shown.
- ⌘F / Ctrl+F opens find; matches are highlighted and you can step through them; Escape clears it.
- Tests in `packages/index-vscode/src/test/`:
  - Save As writes the document's stored text to the path the dialog returns, and nothing when the dialog is cancelled;
  - zoom steps and the 100% reset (a pure helper);
  - if we build our own find: matching and next/previous over the rendered text.
- Rendered headless in a light and a dark theme.

## Out of scope

- The same toolbar on techdocs pages and board tabs. Their tabs have the same missing ⌘F; that could be a follow-up.

item.title: kb MCP: kb_add files web pages by URL, fetched as they are, so an agent's web research lands in the knowledge base
item.description:
## Why

Agents search the web and should be able to file what they read into kb easily, so the next question on the topic is answered from disk. Today `kb_add` takes only `documents` (text the agent already has) or `dir`. To file a page, an agent has to fetch it itself, and Claude Code's WebFetch returns a model-written **summary** of the page, not the page. So kb stores a paraphrase with the page's URL as its source.

Knowledge's **Add URL** already fetches pages (`fetchPage` in `packages/index-vscode/src/commands.ts`):
- follows redirects;
- a non-2xx response files nothing;
- files the bytes as they arrived;
- keeps the ETag for refresh;
- takes the title from the page.

## Change

- **Move `fetchPage` and `titleOf` into `kb-js`,** so the Knowledge extension and the kb MCP server share one fetcher. Knowledge's Add URL keeps working unchanged.
- **Add `urls` to `kb_add`, beside `documents` and `dir`:** `{ urls: [{ url, collection, title? }] }`.
  - The server fetches each URL and files it through `kb add` with the URL as its locator, its mime type, its ETag, and the page's title unless one is given.
  - Each URL gets its own result: filed, unchanged, or failed with the reason.
  - One failed URL doesn't stop the others.
- **Update the kb server's instructions and the kb skill:** to file a page, pass its URL to `kb_add` instead of fetching it and passing the text.

## Done when

- An agent calls `kb_add` with `urls` and gets per-URL results. The filed document is the page as fetched, its locator is the URL, and **Refresh** in Knowledge refreshes it.
- A URL that fails (a 404, an unreachable host) is reported as failed, and nothing is filed for it.
- Tests in `kb-js` and `kb-mcp`, with a local HTTP server as the fixture, covering: success, not modified, a failure, and a mix of good and bad URLs in one call.
- The combined build check passes.

## Out of scope

- Crawling, or following links from a page.
- Converting pages to text before filing (rendering stays at read time).

author: claude
body:
**lap S314 · git 5c5b31b**

**What changed**
- **`kb_add` takes `urls`:** `[{ url, collection, title? }]`, given on its own without `documents` or `dir`. The kb MCP server fetches every page together, then files each one through `kb add` with:
  - the page's bytes exactly as served;
  - its URL as the locator;
  - its mime type and ETag;
  - its own title, unless one is given.
- **Per-URL answers:** each URL is `filed`, `updated`, `unchanged`, or `failed` with the reason. One failure doesn't stop the others, and the call is an error result only when nothing was filed.
- **One fetcher:** `fetchPage` and `titleOf` moved from Knowledge into `kb-js`. Knowledge's Add URL and refresh import them from there and behave as before.
- **Agent guidance:** the kb tool's description, the server's instructions and the kb skill now say to file a web page by its URL rather than its text, since a web-fetch tool often returns a summary, not the page.

**Tests**
- kb-js: 136 pass, 3 new, against a local HTTP server. Covered: bytes, type, ETag and title; a redirect; a 304; a 404; an unreachable host; title fallbacks.
- kb-mcp: 150 pass, 3 new, with a local page server and the fake kb:
  - two pages reach `kb add` with their exact bytes on stdin, plus `--url`, `--mime`, `--etag` and `--title`, while a 404 is reported and the rest go on;
  - an all-failed call is an error with nothing filed;
  - invalid arguments are refused;
  - the schema test now includes `urls`.
- Knowledge: 155 pass, unchanged.
- **Against the real kb:** a served page was filed as D-1, and filing it again reported `unchanged`. The locator is the URL, mime `text/html`, the title comes from the page, the stored text is byte-identical to the page, and a keyword search finds it.
- Combined build check: 41 commands, 3 MCP servers, no errors.

**Noted:** kb-js's no-shell guard looks for the text `exec(`, which flagged `titleOf`'s regular-expression `.exec(text)`. I used `text.match(…)` instead of loosening the guard.

**Not verified (for the user):** a real agent in Claude Code calling `kb_add` with `urls`.

item.title: Docs and website: kb's models in one download (kb-models.zip), unzipped into ~/.kb/models
item.description:
## Why

Semantic search and reranking need models in `~/.kb/models/`. Today the docs offer nomic as a download, and the default embedder and the reranker only by converting them with Python. All three are now published as one zip:
- **URL:** https://procode.s3.fr-par.scw.cloud/kb-models.zip (632 MB);
- **layout:** flat, holding `gte-modernbert-base.F16.gguf`, `gte-reranker-modernbert-base.F16.gguf`, `nomic-embed-text-v1.5.Q4_K_M.gguf`, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE.md` and `SHA256SUMS`.

## Change

- **Root README, website (kb section and FAQ), Marketplace README:** the quick way is to download the zip and unzip it into `~/.kb/models/`, then check `SHA256SUMS`. Give commands for macOS/Linux (curl or wget) and Windows (PowerShell).
- Converting from source stays documented, as the way to build the files yourself.
- Say what's in the zip, that it's Apache-2.0 (`LICENSE`, `NOTICE.md`), and that a store indexed with another model needs `kb reindex`.

## Done when

- All three places give the download and the unzip, with the platform commands.
- The site builds.

author: claude
body:
**lap S316 · git 7a1cc20**

**What changed**
- **Root README** ("kb's models"), the **website** (kb → "Installing the models", plus the FAQ entry) and the **Marketplace README** (kb section) now say to download `kb-models.zip` and unzip it into `~/.kb/models/`:
  - curl or wget on macOS/Linux, with a `shasum -c SHA256SUMS` check (`sha256sum -c` on Linux);
  - PowerShell on Windows (`$HOME\.kb\models`, which is where kb looks, using USERPROFILE).
- **The three models, named:** gte-modernbert-base (the default embedder), gte-reranker-modernbert-base (the reranker) and nomic-embed-text-v1.5 (a smaller embedder), all Apache-2.0, with `LICENSE`, `NOTICE.md` and `SHA256SUMS` in the zip.
- **nomic's separate download is gone,** since the zip includes it. Converting the gte files from Hugging Face stays documented, as building them yourself.
- **The Marketplace README** gives the two-line Unix install and links the website for Windows and checksums.

**Checks**
- **The uploaded zip is the one built locally:** same size, 631,652,894 bytes, and identical first and last 64 KB, which is where a zip keeps its file list. So the layout is flat, and kb only reads `.gguf` files from that folder, so `LICENSE`, `NOTICE.md` and `SHA256SUMS` can sit beside the models.
- **Site:** `npm run build` (tsc plus vite) passes. The built page renders the new section with all five zip links, and the Windows paths show single backslashes.
- **Combined build check:** 41 commands, 3 MCP servers, no errors. The packaged README carries the new section.

**Left:** the Marketplace README's privacy section still says only Knowledge's Add URL goes online. `kb_add` by URL (T-265) now fetches pages too, so that sentence should be updated.

item.description: Agents ask the user several questions at once in a small chat box. item.title: ask: design the tool's schema, how questions are rendered, and how the answers get back
item.description:
Settle the design with the user before any code.

Open questions:
- **Schema:** each question has a title, a body, a kind (single choice, multiple choice, free text) and options, with a free-text "Other" always offered.
- **Rendering:** Markdown only, or also a sandboxed HTML preview per option (styled like techdocs)?
- **Transport:** the MCP server writes the request under `.ask/` and the extension watches for it, as techdocs does. The tool call blocks until the answer file appears. Check MCP client timeouts for long waits.
- **Shipping:** its own package, kept out of the combined build behind a flag until the user decides to publish it.

**Done when** the user has agreed the design and the build tickets are on the board.

author: claude
body:
Decided with the user (2026-10-02):

- **Display:** Markdown for question bodies and options, plus an optional HTML preview per option, sandboxed and styled with techdocs' variables.
- **Where:** an editor tab, not the sidebar.
- **Navigation:** one form holds many steps. They can be answered in any order, skipped, and revisited. A list of steps shows each one as answered, skipped or open.
- **Asking for more:** on any step the user can write "I need more on this" in place of an answer. Submit returns each step as answered, skipped or needs-more (with the user's question). The agent replies and asks those steps again, and the earlier answers stay filled in.
- Why: Claude's questions in the chat box mean scrolling a long block and answering at the bottom. The form puts each question on its own page and lets the user work through them their own way.

Build tickets: T-271 (server and transport), T-272 (the editor tab), T-273 (combined behind a flag, plus a skill telling agents when to use ask).

item.title: ask: the MCP server — the ask tool, its schema, and a file handoff to VS Code that waits for the answers
item.description:
New package `packages/ask`, built like `packages/techdocs`.

- The `ask` tool takes a title and steps. Each step has an id, a title, a Markdown body, a kind (single, multi or text) and options. Each option has a label, an optional Markdown description and an optional HTML preview. Choice steps always offer "Other". An optional `previous` carries earlier answers to fill in again.
- The server writes the request to `.ask/<id>/request.json`, waits for `.ask/<id>/answer.json`, and returns each step as answered, skipped or needs-more.
- First, test how long the MCP client lets a tool call wait. If the limit is too short, split it into `ask` (opens the form and returns at once) and `ask_wait` (waits for the answers).

**Done when** unit tests cover the schema checks, the request and answer round trip, a cancelled form and a timeout, and the waiting limit is written down.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap S318, git 3aa067b.

**What changed.** New package `packages/ask` (an npm workspace, not in the combined build), with `specs/ask.md` §1–4.
- `ask {title, steps, from?}` checks the steps and writes `.ask/F-<n>/request.json`. It waits for `answer.json` and returns every step as answered, skipped or needs_more. When a step is needs_more, a `next` hint tells the agent to answer the question in that step's body and ask again with `from`.
- `ask_wait {id}` resumes a form handed back as `waiting`.
- When the client cancels the call (`notifications/cancelled`) or disconnects, the server writes a cancelled answer, so the tab can close.

**Decided, and why.**
- **Waiting.** Claude Code allows about 28 h per tool call, but cuts off a stdio call that sends nothing for 30 min. So the call waits at most 25 min and sends progress every 15 s when it has a progress token. That makes one blocking call fine, and `ask_wait` is only the fallback. Source: Claude Code docs, MCP page, 2026-10-02. Known exception: anthropics/claude-code#63379 reports the desktop app cancelling stdio calls at about 60 s.
- **`from`** carries over only the answered steps. Skipped and needs_more steps open fresh.
- **Ids.** `mkdir` claims the next F-<n>, so two servers never get the same id.
- **`.ask/`** writes its own `.gitignore` (`*`), since a form belongs to the conversation and isn't worth keeping.
- **Polling, not `fs.watch`:** the answer is written by another process and the file system may be synced.

**Tests:** 12/12 pass (`npm test --workspace ask`). A smoke run of `bin/ask-mcp` over stdio worked: an answered call returned its steps, and a cancelled call wrote a cancelled answer and sent no reply.

**Not verified:** a run against real Claude Code. The extension side doesn't exist yet (T-272).

- The server writes the request to `.ask/<id>/request.json`, waits for `.ask/<id>/answer.json`, and returns each step as answered, skipped or needs-more.
- First, test how long the MCP client lets a tool call wait. If the limit is too short, split it into `ask` (opens the form and returns at once) and `ask_wait` (waits for the answers).

**Done when** unit tests cover the schema checks, the request and answer round trip, a cancelled form and a timeout, and the waiting limit is written down.

- The tab writes `answer.json` when the form is submitted.

**Done when** there are unit tests for the answer state, and the tab has been rendered in light and dark themes with headless Chrome over the real bundle.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap S319, git f532853.

**What changed.** New package `packages/ask-vscode` (a workspace, not in the combined build yet), with `specs/ask.md` §5.
- The extension watches `.ask/F-*/request.json` and opens one editor tab per form. On startup it opens forms with no answer that are under 30 minutes old. **ask: Open Pending Questions** opens the rest.
- **Layout:** the steps down the left, marked answered, open, skipped or needs more, ending with **Review and submit**. On the right, one step at a time: its Markdown body, option cards with key badges, Other, and two fields that open on demand, **Add a note** and **I need more on this**. A footer has Back, Skip and Next. The review page lists every answer, and each row jumps to its step.
- **Previews:** an option's HTML preview shows beside the options, in a frame sandboxed with nothing allowed, themed with baukasten's tokens, the theme's values and techdocs' `page.css`.
- **Submit and close:** Submit writes `answer.json` through the new `Ask.submit`, which keeps only the steps asked and only the first answer. Closing the tab without submitting cancels the form. When the agent's call is cancelled, the tab shows that it was closed.

**Decided, and why.**
- **No scripts in previews.** A preview is a picture. The webview's policy would block its scripts anyway, so the frame says the same thing.
- **State updates right away.** The tab's state lives in one ref that changes on every edit. The headless renders showed that two keys pressed before a re-render read stale state: a pick followed by Enter lost the pick, and "2" on the next step picked an option from the previous one. Both are fixed and checked in the renders again.
- **Skipping sets an answer aside.** It isn't sent, but it isn't erased either, and touching the step brings it back.
- **Open steps** are sent as skipped. Plain Enter never submits.

**Tests:** ask 14/14 (added store tests for `submit` and `pending`) and ask-vscode 11/11 (answer state, keys, preview document).

**Rendered:** headless Chrome over the real bundle, with a stand-in VS Code API and Dark+ and Light+ theme values. I checked the single-choice step with a preview (light and dark), the multi-choice step, the text step, needs more, and the review page.

**Not verified:** running inside VS Code. The file watcher, opening the tab, cancelling on close and the closed notice were not exercised. That needs the combined build (T-273) or an Extension Development Host.

item.title: ask: in the combined build behind a flag, and a skill telling agents when to use it
item.description:
- `scripts/build.mjs --with-ask` bundles the ask server and tab. Without the flag, the published .vsix is unchanged.
- A skill tells agents to use ask in place of their built-in question tool when they have more than one question or a question needs a preview.

**Done when** the combined check passes with and without the flag.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap S320, git 88b9607.

**What changed**
- `node packages/combined/scripts/build.mjs --with-ask` (or `npm run package --workspace combined -- --with-ask`) adds ask-vscode to the parts. Its command and media merge in, its tab bundle goes to `out/parts/ask.js`, and its server to `out/mcp/ask.js`. The package is named `procode-<version>[-target]-ask.vsix`.
- The extension loads optional parts from `out/parts/` and defines ask's MCP server (listed last) only when those files exist. **Set Up MCP for Claude Code** writes ask into `.mcp.json` along with the others, and its message names every server it wrote.
- `check.mjs` handles both kinds of build. With ask, it checks that the tab's command is registered and the server is defined. Without ask, it checks there's no `out/parts` and nothing of ask in the manifest.

**Decided**
- **No separate skill.** ask's server instructions already tell agents to use it instead of their own question tool when there are two or more questions or a preview is needed. Claude Code loads those instructions with the server, so a skill would repeat them.
- **Optional parts are found by their files**, so the published build has no trace of ask.

**Tests:** the plain build's check passes (41 commands, 3 servers), and so does the `--with-ask` build's (42 commands, 4 servers). The bundled `dist/out/mcp/ask.js` answers `tools/list`. Packaged `packages/combined/procode-0.1.1-ask.vsix`.

**Not verified:** a real run in VS Code with a Claude Code call.

author: claude
body:

item.title: ask: the tab opens on its own when the form is written outside the open folder (a folder with no .git of its own)
item.description:
Reported by the user: the form's tab doesn't open by itself, and only **ask: Open Pending Questions** shows it.

**Cause.** `.playground` has no `.git` of its own. With no `.ask/` yet, the server puts it at the enclosing git root (`procode/.ask/`). The extension's watcher (`**/.ask/F-*/request.json`) only sees the open workspace folder, so it never fires. Open Pending Questions walks up the way the server does, which is why it found the form.

**Fix.** The extension looks for forms where the server puts them: for each folder, `findAsk(folder) ?? defaultRoot(folder)`. It checks those places every second for new forms and for answers written elsewhere, instead of relying on a workspace file watcher.

**Done when** a form written at the git root above the open folder opens a tab by itself, and this is covered by a unit test of where forms are looked for.

author: claude
body:
Superseded, nothing committed (lap S322 holds no edits).

The cause is confirmed: the form went to `procode/.ask/` because `.playground` has no `.git` of its own. A fix that looked once a second where the server writes worked against the real extension bundle with a stand-in `vscode`: the tab opened by itself, and cancelling showed the closed notice. Then the user asked why there's a `.ask/` folder at all, and chose to have the VS Code extension host ask's MCP server over HTTP, so there's no folder for the server and the tab to disagree about. That work is T-277. The fix was reverted.

`procode/.ask/` still holds F-1 from the user's test. lap sees it as untracked files, since lap doesn't read the `.gitignore` inside `.ask/`. It's the user's to delete.

item.title: ask: the MCP server runs inside the VS Code extension, over HTTP — no .ask/ folder
item.description:
Today Claude Code starts ask's server over stdio, and the server hands forms to the extension through `.ask/` files. Instead, the extension runs the MCP server itself, over Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1. Claude Code connects to it directly, the `ask` call opens the tab in the same process, and the reply goes out when the person submits. No files, no folder. The user chose this knowing a server just for ask is more than strictly needed, and suggested a settings page later to turn MCP servers on and off.

1. **First, test Claude Code's HTTP timeouts.** For HTTP it allows 60 s to the first response byte and 5 min of idle time. Find out whether progress notifications, or SSE output, keep a 10-minute call alive.
2. **Then build it.** The HTTP server lives in the extension. The port is chosen per window, and **Set Up MCP for Claude Code** writes it into `.mcp.json`. `ask` and `ask_wait` work as before, and the tab is unchanged.
3. **Remove the stdio server and the `.ask/` store** from the build.

**Done when** a real Claude Code call opens the tab by itself and gets the answers back, the combined check passes with and without `--with-ask`, and unit tests cover the HTTP transport.
